If a symbol string contains a double-quote or AppleScript metacharacter (e.g. a malformed/attacker-influenced ticker), it breaks out of the string literal — AppleScript injection executing arbitrary osascript. Symbols normally come from an allowlist, but msg formatting trusts them without escaping.
fix: Escape embedded double-quotes/backslashes in msg before interpolation, or pass the text via osascript's argv (-e with a quoted-form of) rather than inline string concatenation.

title: Session whitelist default differs from config default, masking misconfig
description: due_to_run uses cfg.get('session_whitelist') or ['regular']. If an operator deliberately sets session_whitelist to an empty list (meaning 'no sessions tradable'), the `or ['regular']` overrides it to allow regular-session auto-runs — silently re-enabling trading the operator tried to disable.
fix: Distinguish missing key from empty list: wl = cfg.get('session_whitelist'); if wl is None: wl = ['regular']; then test `session not in wl`.

title: maybe_escalate de-escalation requires a 15% drawdown but escalation only blocks at 5%, leaving a gap
description: De-escalation triggers at dd>=15%. Escalation requires dd<5%. Between 5% and 15% drawdown the agent neither steps down nor up but also nothing protects it — and crucially, after escalating to aggressive the only way back down is a full 15% drawdown. Combined with maybe_escalate running each cycle, a brief Sharpe>0.5 spike can ratchet to aggressive, then it stays there through a 5-14% drawdown. The asymmetry is steep.
fix: Tighten the de-escalation trigger (e.g. step down at >=8-10% drawdown) or require sustained metrics before escalating, so the agent doesn't sit at max risk through a moderate drawdown.

title: maybe_escalate compares win_rate to 0.55 without checking it's a fraction not percent
description: wr = stats.get('win_rate') from aj_analytics.trade_stats(), which returns a 0-1 fraction (round(len(wins)/n,3)). The check wr>=0.55 is correct for a fraction. But the same value is later formatted with '{:.0%}'.format(wr). If any caller passes a percent-scaled win_rate (e.g. from a different stats source via the cfg-injected path), the 0.55 comparison silently misfires. Low-confidence but the lack of a domain assertion is fragile given the dual interpretation across modules.
fix: Normalise/assert win_rate domain (e.g. if wr is not None and wr>1: wr/=100) before the comparison, or document the contract explicitly.

title: _fees uses bps even when bps config is negative, producing a negative fee floored by min_fee_usd only if min set
description: bps = cfg.get('crypto_fee_bps' or 'fee_bps'); fee = max(min_fee_usd, abs(notional)*bps/1e4). If an operator stores a negative fee_bps (config coercion clamps? not for this), abs(notional)*negative is negative, and max(0, negative)=0, so fees silently become 0. Not catastrophic but means a misconfig produces free trading without warning.
fix: Clamp bps to >=0 (e.g. max(0.0, float(bps or 0))) before computing the fee so a negative config can't zero out fees.

title: PaperBroker.cash reads aj_paper_cash but ignores realized P&L/fills, so paper buying power never reflects trades
description: cash() returns the static aj_paper_cash setting via money(). It is never decremented by buys or incremented by sells/realized P&L from the paper book. Any caller using cash() for buying-power checks sees a constant figure, so paper sizing/affordability is wrong as soon as the book has trades.
fix: Compute cash as starting aj_paper_cash minus net cost of open positions plus realized_total from aj_positions.paper_book(), or document that cash() is the static seed and don't use it for buying-power gating.

title: PaperBroker marketable-buy limit fill ignores that a non-marketable buy (quote>lp) should rest, but adverse-adjusted price not used in the test
description: Buy marketability test is `quote <= lp` using the raw quote. If quote is just above lp but quote*(1-? ) — for a buy, slippage raises the effective price, so the test should arguably compare the price the buyer would actually pay. Using raw quote can both (a) let a buy fill where the slipped price exceeds lp (capped by min, so OK) and (b) rest a buy that at raw quote looks non-marketable. The asymmetry between the marketability test (raw quote) and the fill price (slipped) is internally inconsistent.
fix: Make the marketability test and the fill price use a single consistent reference (either both raw quote or both slipped); document the chosen convention so paper fills are reproducible and not optimistic.

title: main() catches all exceptions and serializes str(e) to stderr, leaking secret-related error text
description: The top-level except prints json with str(e). For cmd_secret/cmd_verify_pass failures the exception message could include the scope or partial value context, and more generally a broad catch hides the traceback that an operator needs to debug a kill/recon failure. For a kill-switch CLI that must be dependable, swallowing the traceback into a one-line message reduces diagnosability.
fix: Print the traceback to stderr (logging.exception) in addition to the JSON error, and ensure secret command errors never echo argv content.

title: cmd_verify_pass marks ANY 'aj_verify_<gate>' as pass with no contract test, enabling gates from the CLI
description: verify-pass <gate> directly does set_setting('aj_verify_'+gate, 'pass') for arbitrary gate strings, with no check that the gate's contract test actually passed. The module docstrings repeatedly state a gate must only be set to pass AFTER its contract test succeeds. This CLI lets an operator (or a script) flip alpaca/robinhood/ccxt live-trading gates to 'pass' without any verification, defeating the fail-closed VERIFY design.
fix: Restrict the accepted gate names to the known set and, where a self-test exists (e.g. mcp_read.contract_ok()), require it to pass before writing 'pass'; for broker gates, require an explicit '--force-i-ran-the-contract-test' acknowledgement and audit the action.

title: cmd_config --set parses k=v but never validates the key, silently storing nothing for unknown keys without feedback
description: cmd_config builds updates from --set k=v and calls aj_config.set_config(updates). set_config logs a warning and IGNORES unknown keys, but the CLI returns the full config as if the update applied, giving no signal to the operator that their 'k' was a typo and was dropped. For risk config this can leave the operator believing a cap was set when it wasn't.
fix: Diff requested keys against DEFAULTS in cmd_config and print which keys were ignored, or have set_config return the set of ignored keys for the CLI to surface.

title: Probability clamp reads cfg.get(k, 0.5) but never recovers a non-numeric value to a sane default
description: After the negative-guard loop, _PROB_KEYS are clamped via `v = cfg.get(k, 0.5); cfg[k] = min(1.0, max(0.0, v))`. Since these keys are also in _FLOAT_KEYS, the value is already a float, but if a future refactor leaves a None/str in cfg[k], min/max(...) raises TypeError. More concretely today: there is no validation that buy_prob_threshold >= sell_prob_threshold, so a misconfiguration (buy=0.4, sell=0.6) makes nearly every signal both a buy and a sell candidate.
fix: After clamping, enforce ordering: if cfg['sell_prob_threshold'] > cfg['buy_prob_threshold'], reset both to their DEFAULTS (or swap), so the gate logic cannot be inverted.

title: default_broker validity check lowercases input but compares against a set that may contain mixed-case registered names
description: `str(cfg['default_broker']).lower() not in _valid_brokers()`. _valid_brokers() unions _BASE_BROKERS (all lowercase) with aj_broker._BROKERS.keys(). If any registered broker key is not lowercase, a valid configured broker name gets reset to 'paper' because the lowercased cfg value won't match the mixed-case registry key.
fix: Lowercase both sides: `brokers = {b.lower() for b in _BASE_BROKERS | set(aj_broker._BROKERS.keys())}` and compare the lowercased value against it.

title: session_whitelist sanitizer lowercases entries but stored values may already be normalized uppercase via _coerce_list
description: _coerce_list (used for _LIST_KEYS incl. session_whitelist) uppercases every item (line 200: t = str(it).strip().upper()). So a stored session_whitelist is ['REGULAR']. get_config then does `[s.lower() for s in cfg['session_whitelist'] if s.lower() in _TRADABLE_SESSIONS]`. The lower() rescues it, but _serialize stores the uppercased JSON, so the persisted value disagrees with the runtime-normalized one, and any external reader of the raw setting sees 'REGULAR' which is not in _TRADABLE_SESSIONS.
fix: Treat session names as case-insensitive consistently: either don't uppercase session_whitelist in _coerce_list (only symbols should be uppercased), or store the lowercased normalized form.

title: _coerce_list uppercases ALL list keys, corrupting session_whitelist values
description: _coerce_list is shared by symbol_allowlist and session_whitelist (both in _LIST_KEYS). Uppercasing is correct for ticker symbols but wrong for session names ('regular' -> 'REGULAR'). Combined with the sanitizer's lower() pass it happens to work at runtime for sessions, but the persisted setting and any direct consumer of _coerce_list output for sessions is wrong-cased.
fix: Parameterize _coerce_list with an `upper: bool=True` flag and call with upper=False for session_whitelist, or special-case session_whitelist to lowercase.

title: _serialize does not clamp probabilities or enforce enum validity, so out-of-range values persist and only get fixed on read
description: set_config -> _serialize stores buy_prob_threshold='5.0', daily_loss_basis='garbage', entry_order_type='banana', session_whitelist=['closed'] verbatim (after type coercion only). get_config sanitizes on read, but the PERSISTED setting is invalid, so any other consumer reading the raw setting (or a future direct reader) sees the bad value, and the round-trip is lossy/misleading.
fix: Validate/clamp in _serialize (or set_config) to the same rules get_config applies: clamp probs to [0,1], reject/reset invalid enums and non-tradable sessions before persisting.

title: release() can leak the lock file handle when fcntl import succeeds but _fh is None
description: In acquire() the lease path (_acquire_lease) sets _have=True but never opens self._fh. release() then imports fcntl (succeeds on POSIX) and only unlocks/closes if self._fh; that branch is fine, but if acquire() took the fcntl path and the open succeeded yet flock failed, _fh was closed and set None — OK. The real leak: when fcntl path is used and release() raises before reaching close (e.g. flock UN throws), the except swallows it and the file handle is never closed.
fix: Wrap the fcntl unlock and the _fh.close() in independent try/finally so close() always runs even if flock(LOCK_UN) raises; set self._fh=None after closing.

title: backup_db leaks source/dest connections if sqlite3.connect(dest) raises
description: s = sqlite3.connect(src) is opened first; if sqlite3.connect(dest) then raises (bad path, permission, disk full), the function exits via exception with s never closed (the try/finally only starts after both connects). The source connection FD leaks.
fix: Open both connections inside the try, or guard: s = connect(src); try: d = connect(dest) ... finally close both. Move the dest connect inside a try whose finally closes s.

title: Good-Friday and other NYSE half/closed days are missing from holiday set
description: _us_market_holidays omits Good Friday (a full NYSE close) and the early-close days. market_session() will therefore report 'regular' on Good Friday and on half-days past 1pm ET. Since live trading is off by default the safety impact is bounded, but the gate's session check (aj_risk.evaluate step 2) will pass on a day the market is actually closed, which is a correctness bug for session gating.
fix: Add Good Friday (Easter-based computus minus 2 days) to the holiday set; optionally model the known early-close half-days. At minimum document and add Good Friday so session gating doesn't green-light a closed day.

title: insert/update/get_row/query interpolate the table name and column names directly into SQL (injection if caller-controlled)
description: insert(), update(), update_if(), get_row() format table and column names via str.format into the SQL string. Values are parameterized (good), but identifiers are not validated. These are internal helpers, yet enhanced_gate/strategy modules pass through them; any path where a table/column name is derived from external/config input is a SQL-injection vector, and even internally a typo'd column produces a confusing SQL error rather than a guarded failure.
fix: Whitelist allowed table names and validate column identifiers against a regex (^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$) before interpolation, raising on anything else.

title: audit() reads _last_row_hash then inserts under _write_lock, but other writers using insert() bypass the hash chain entirely
description: The hash chain integrity assumes ALL aj_audit writes go through audit(). But insert('aj_audit', ...) via the generic helper would write a row with no prev_hash/row_hash, silently breaking verify_audit_chain. There is no constraint preventing a generic insert into aj_audit. The chain's tamper-evidence is only as strong as the discipline of always using audit().
fix: Guard insert() to reject table=='aj_audit' (force callers through audit()), or add a NOT NULL/trigger requirement on row_hash so a chain-bypassing insert fails.

title: prune_routing cutoff uses isoformat() which may not match stored ts format
description: cutoff = (utc_now()-timedelta).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() yields e.g. '2026-06-26T00:00:00+00:00'. If aj_routing.ts is stored via utc_now_iso() the format matches, but if ts is stored without timezone or with a 'Z' suffix, the string comparison ts < cutoff (lexicographic) silently mis-prunes (deletes too much or nothing). String-based timestamp comparison is fragile across format variants.
fix: Ensure cutoff is formatted identically to how ts is written (reuse aj_db.utc_now_iso-style formatting / the same serializer), or compare via a parsed/normalized column.

title: State coercion uses 'accepted' default that can downgrade a broker 'filled' with zero recorded fills to 'unknown' incorrectly
description: If broker returns state='filled' but provides no fills array (some brokers report terminal state separately from fill detail), agg['filled_qty']==0, so line 179-180 sets state to 'unknown'. A genuinely filled order then sits in 'unknown' awaiting reconciliation that may never re-pull fills if the broker only reports cumulative fills going forward. This can strand a filled order.
fix: When broker state=='filled' and no fills were reported, synthesize a single fill from res['filled_qty']/res['avg_fill_price'] (if present) before recomputing, or trust the broker's filled_qty/avg for the aggregate rather than forcing 'unknown'.

title: _recompute_order avg fill price is a raw float, never money()-rounded, causing cent drift in avg_fill_price
description: avg = notional/total_qty is stored to aj_orders.avg_fill_price without money() rounding (only fees_usd is rounded). Downstream P&L and display use this unrounded avg, reintroducing the float drift money() exists to prevent. For fractional-share/crypto it can be many decimals.
fix: Round avg through aj_db.money(avg) (or round to an appropriate price precision) before returning, consistent with the module's single-rounding-authority rule.

title: Reconcile adopts broker partial/cumulative fills but does not validate transition, may overwrite a locally-canceled order
description: _resolve_open_orders calls _set_state(oid, tstate, ...) which validates transitions, but tstate comes straight from broker.get_order without bounding to the allowed set. A broker returning an unexpected string (e.g. 'pending_cancel') is passed to valid_transition which returns False, and _set_state then returns False silently leaving the order in 'unknown' but counting it as resolved (out['resolved'] was already incremented).
fix: Normalize/validate tstate against the known state set before _set_state; only increment out['resolved'] when _set_state returns True, otherwise increment still_unknown.

title: execute_trade qty falls back through 'or' so a legitimate decision qty of 0 silently uses proposal qty
description: qty = float(decision.get('qty') or proposal.get('qty') or 0). If decision qty is a valid 0.0 (shouldn't pass the gate, but defensively) the `or` skips it; more realistically if decision qty is None and proposal qty is 0, qty becomes 0 and the order is submitted with qty 0 (PaperBroker rejects, but a live adapter might not). The gate already computed the authoritative qty in decision — fallback chains weaken that.
fix: Prefer decision['qty'] explicitly when present (is not None) rather than via truthiness; reject qty<=0 here before insert.

title: Partial-fill detection uses fixed 1e-6 tolerance against order qty, wrong scale for crypto fractional sizes
description: agg['filled_qty'] + 1e-6 < order_qty decides 'short fill'. For crypto where qty can legitimately be 0.0005 BTC, a 1e-6 absolute tolerance is a relative 0.2% — meaningful — while for large equity quantities 1e-6 is negligible. A uniform absolute epsilon mis-scales the partial-fill judgment across asset classes.
fix: Use a relative tolerance (e.g. filled_qty < order_qty*(1-1e-6)) or scale epsilon to the order size so the short-fill test behaves consistently for fractional crypto and whole-share equity.

title: valid_transition allows 'unknown' -> any terminal, but _set_state on a row already terminal returns early without honoring extra writes for partially_filled aggregation
description: _set_state: if frm==to and to!='partially_filled', it does a compare-and-set of extra and returns True. For a 'filled' order re-reported by reconcile with new fills, frm=='filled' is terminal and valid_transition('filled', 'filled') returns False (frm in _TERMINAL), so the function returns False and the recomputed avg/filled_qty/fees are NOT written — a late fill on an order the broker prematurely marked filled is silently dropped.
fix: Allow same-terminal-state metadata updates (avg_fill_price/filled_qty/fees_usd) via compare-and-set even when frm==to is terminal, so reconciliation can correct aggregates without an illegal-transition rejection.

title: _client() creates a new Langfuse client every emit and never closes it; flush is best-effort but the client/threads leak
description: emit_cycle_trace builds a fresh Langfuse() on every cycle. The Langfuse SDK spins up a background flush thread/HTTP session per client. There's a best-effort lf.flush() but no lf.shutdown()/close(), so each cycle leaks a client object with its worker thread and connection pool — over a long-running auto_run, this accumulates threads and sockets.
fix: Either memoize a single module-level client (lazy singleton) reused across cycles, or call lf.shutdown() in a finally block after flush to release the thread/session.

title: _t_proposals/_t_orders run SELECT * with a caller-supplied LIMIT but int() can be huge/negative, and rows may be large unbounded
description: limit = int(args.get('limit') or 20) is passed straight into the SQL. A negative limit in SQLite means 'no limit' (returns ALL rows), so a caller passing limit=-1 over the read MCP path can exfiltrate the entire proposals/orders history in one call, and a huge positive limit can OOM the response. The read path is supposed to be a bounded, frozen-surface read.
fix: Clamp: `limit = max(1, min(int(args.get('limit') or 20), 200))` before binding it into the query.

title: cumulative_pnl returns book["realized_total"]/book["fees_total"] via [] indexing
description: The return statement uses book['realized_total'] and book['fees_total'] with hard indexing. If paper_book() ever omits these keys (e.g. an error path returning {'positions':{}} like aj_alpha._paper_book's fallback), cumulative_pnl raises KeyError uncaught (the try only wraps the unrealized loop). Callers like _current_equity catch it, but status() calls cumulative_pnl directly and would 500.
fix: book.get('realized_total') or 0.0 and book.get('fees_total') or 0.0 in the return.

title: alerts() indexes os_["by_state"] which may be absent if order_stats changes shape
description: unknown = os_['by_state'].get('unknown',0). order_stats always returns by_state, so currently safe, but the line is inside the try so a shape change would be swallowed and ALL later alerts (which there are none after) lost. More importantly the earlier os_['total'] (line 96) and os_['fill_rate'] are accessed via [] under the same try — a KeyError there silently drops every subsequent alert including the critical recon/halt ones, hiding critical conditions.
fix: Use .get() for os_ fields and structure each alert check in its own try so one failure doesn't suppress the critical alerts that follow.

title: fill_rate denominator 'submitted' subtracts only 'new', counting rejected/canceled as submitted
description: submitted = total - by_state.get('new',0). Orders in 'rejected' or 'canceled' states are counted in the denominator as if submitted, deflating fill_rate. A batch of rejected (never-sent) orders makes fill_rate look like a collapse, which feeds health_autohalt (aj_autonomy health_check fill-rate<0.4 → CRITICAL kill switch). A bad denominator can trigger an autonomous halt.
fix: Define submitted as the count of states that were actually sent to a broker (e.g. submitted+accepted+partially_filled+filled+expired+unknown), excluding 'new','rejected','canceled' from the denominator.

title: status() config projection uses cfg[k] hard-index for keys that may be absent
description: config:{k:cfg[k] for k in (...)} hard-indexes each listed key. get_config() is expected to populate all of them, but if a future config omits e.g. 'auto_approve_paper' or 'daily_loss_basis' (or an older persisted config is loaded), status() raises KeyError and the whole dashboard/status endpoint 500s.
fix: Use cfg.get(k) in the comprehension so a missing key yields None instead of crashing the status snapshot.

title: path_allowed treats fnmatch patterns without wildcards as literal, so 'wealth.db' blocks only exact basename but variants slip through
description: FORBIDDEN_PATHS includes 'wealth.db' and 'wealth.db-*'. The segment loop checks fnmatch(seg, pat). A path like 'backups/wealth.db.bak' has segment 'wealth.db.bak' which does NOT match 'wealth.db' or 'wealth.db-*' (the WAL/journal pattern uses a dash, but SQLite WAL files are 'wealth.db-wal'/'wealth.db-shm' which DO match 'wealth.db-*'; however a copy named 'wealth.db.bak' or 'wealth_db' does not). The guard can be bypassed by trivially renamed copies of the DB.
fix: Add broader patterns ('*wealth.db*', 'wealth.db*') and normalize, or block any path whose basename contains 'wealth.db'; treat the DB family as a prefix match, not exact.

title: held dict comprehension assumes every position dict has a 'qty' key (KeyError on malformed book)
description: held = {s: p['qty'] for s,p in book['positions'].items()} subscripts both 'positions' and 'qty'. paper_book always provides these today, but any future/error path returning a position without 'qty' raises KeyError inside run_once's main try, marking the entire cycle 'crashed'.
fix: Use book.get('positions',{}) and p.get('qty',0.0) defensively, consistent with other consumers.

title: _process_exits pre_book snapshot is only taken when signal_scorecard is on, but realized scoring also reads it unconditionally later
description: pre_book = paper_book()... if cfg.get('signal_scorecard') else {}. Later (line 245) avg is read from pre_book only inside the same signal_scorecard guard, so it's consistent. However the exits themselves execute BEFORE the snapshot is used, and because each _propose_and_execute mutates the book via fills, using pre_book (pre-sell) avg_cost is correct — but the snapshot is taken AFTER update_position_state and expire_stale_orders may have run in run_once, not necessarily reflecting the true entry basis if multiple exits for the same symbol occur in one pass (second exit sees stale avg).
fix: Take the pre_book snapshot once at the very start of the exits pass (it is) but key realized scoring on the lot basis consumed per-sell rather than a single pre-pass avg, or compute realized from realized_trades() after each sell to avoid double-counting when a symbol has multiple exit signals.

title: reconcile(venue=default_broker) constructs a broker that may raise BrokerNotEnabled for a live default, caught as generic error
description: When default_broker is a live venue and live is off, get_broker returns PaperBroker (fine). But if default_broker is a live venue and live IS enabled but VERIFY gate not passed, get_broker raises BrokerNotEnabled inside reconcile, caught by the broad except and reported as reconcile='error' — masking a misconfiguration that should halt or alert, not be a soft non-fatal error at end of cycle.
fix: Catch BrokerNotEnabled distinctly in reconcile or before calling it; surface it as an alert/halt rather than a generic 'error' status so a misconfigured live default is visible.

title: run_once returns without closing the cycle when lock acquisition fails, but a cycle was NOT opened — OK; however lock not released either path is fine, yet aj_init side effects partially ran
description: If lock.acquire() fails, run_once returns early. That's correct (no cycle opened). But aj_db.aj_init() already ran (migrations etc.) which is fine. The real issue: there is no finally to release the lock on the early-return path — acceptable since acquire failed and _have is False, but if acquire() partially set state (fcntl open succeeded, flock failed) the half-open file handle in self._fh is closed inside acquire's except. Confirm: acquire closes _fh on failure. So no leak. Low risk.
fix: No change strictly required; for robustness, ensure run_once early-return path does not leave any partially-acquired lock by always calling lock.release() in a finally even when acquire returns False (release is a no-op when _have is False).

title: _propose_and_execute indexes sizing['qty'] and sizing['notional'] directly; a sizer omitting either raises KeyError mid-insert
description: The proposal insert uses sizing['qty'] and sizing['notional'] (and decision['side']) via subscript. If aj_strategy.size_order returns a dict missing 'notional' (only 'qty'), this raises KeyError, caught by the per-symbol except and logged as a generic symbol failure, losing the real cause.
fix: Validate/normalize the sizing dict (qty, notional, order_type, limit_price) before insert, or use .get with sane fallbacks (notional default = money(qty*price)).

title: avg_cost guard `if tot_qty else 0.0` is dead because the loop already skipped abs(tot_qty)<=_EPS
description: The ternary `(cost/tot_qty) if tot_qty else 0.0` can never hit the 0.0 branch because positions with abs(tot_qty)<=_EPS were `continue`d above. Harmless, but it hides that the intended divide-by-zero protection is at the wrong place; a tot_qty of exactly 0 that is >_EPS in abs is impossible, so the guard is misleading and any future change to the epsilon filter could reintroduce a ZeroDivisionError that this dead guard won't catch.
fix: Remove the dead guard or make it meaningful by basing the skip and the divide on the same condition; document that the loop guarantees tot_qty != 0.

title: is_today uses naive string-prefix on filled_at (UTC ISO) but realized_today is consumed as the trading day P&L
description: is_today compares filled_at[:10] to aj_db.utc_now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d') — a UTC calendar date. But compute_day_pnl's session baseline uses the ET trading date (_session_date). So realized_today rolls over at 00:00 UTC (~7-8pm ET), splitting an ET trading session across two 'today' buckets and mis-attributing late-session realized P&L vs the unrealized baseline that resets on ET date. The daily-loss halt mixes two different day definitions.
fix: Compute 'today' for realized fills using the ET session date (convert filled_at to America/New_York before slicing), matching aj_risk._session_date so realized and unrealized legs share one trading-day boundary.

title: realized_trades subtracts the FULL fill fee from each closing trade even when the fill also opened a new lot
description: net = money(closed_pl - fees) charges the entire fill's fees against the closed portion, even when part of the fill opened/extended a new lot (remaining>_EPS appended). A sell that closes 10 longs and opens 5 shorts attributes 100% of the sell fee to the realized close, overstating realized loss and understating the open lot's basis-adjacent cost.
fix: Pro-rate fees by closed_qty/qty so only the fee share attributable to the closed quantity is booked against realized; carry the rest with the opened lot (or ignore, but consistently).

title: infer_asset_type misclassifies equity tickers that collide with crypto hints (e.g. 'LINK', 'UNI', 'MATIC')
description: _CRYPTO_HINTS contains bare tickers like LINK, UNI, MATIC, DOT, ATOM that are also (or were) listed equities/ETFs. A user holding equity LINK gets asset_type='crypto', so marks/fees/exit rules use the -USD crypto quote and the crypto fee tier — wrong instrument, wrong P&L.
fix: Restrict crypto inference to the explicit -USD suffix (already handled) and remove the ambiguous bare-ticker hints, or require an external asset-type source rather than guessing from a collision-prone symbol set.

title: _marks non-finite filter compares p to float('inf') tuple instead of using math.isfinite
description: The guard `p not in (float('inf'), float('-inf'))` plus `p == p` is meant to reject inf/NaN. It works for those exact float values, but the construct is fragile and (more importantly) does not reject a price of 0 or negative, which downstream code (e.g. unrealized P&L) treats as a valid mark, propagating a bogus (mark-avg)*qty.
fix: Replace with `out[s] = float(p) if isinstance(p,(int,float)) and not isinstance(p,bool) and math.isfinite(p) and p>0 else None` so non-positive marks are also rejected, consistent with _order_price which rejects price<=0.

title: notional->qty conversion ignores qty when both qty and notional present, and treats qty=0 as falsy via earlier branch
description: `if proposal.get('qty') is not None: qty=float(proposal['qty'])` — correct — but `elif proposal.get('notional_usd')` uses truthiness, so a notional of 0.0 falls through to 'no qty/notional'. More importantly float(proposal['qty']) can raise ValueError/TypeError on a non-numeric qty, which is caught only by the outer except and reported as a generic 'gate exception' rather than a clean 'invalid qty' block.
fix: Wrap the float() conversions in a try and return a precise 'invalid qty/notional' block; use `is not None` for notional_usd too so an explicit 0 notional is rejected with a clear reason rather than the generic branch.

title: is_halted() reads cached config while the gate uses uncached fresh read — inconsistent halt view
description: is_halted() returns based on aj_config.get_config() (5s-cached via get_settings), but evaluate() deliberately uses _trading_enabled_fresh() to see a kill immediately. Any caller relying on is_halted() (e.g. UI/CLI status) can report 'not halted' for up to 5s after a kill_switch, contradicting the gate. This is a correctness/observability mismatch around a safety control.
fix: Make is_halted() use the same uncached path: `return not _trading_enabled_fresh()`.

title: IPS post-trade breach detection uses count delta, missing breaches that replace others
description: _ips_block_reason blocks only when len(breaches_after) > len(breaches_before). If a trade clears one pre-existing breach while introducing a different one (count unchanged), na>nb is False and the new breach is allowed. The intent (don't introduce new breaches) is not satisfied by a pure count comparison.
fix: Compare breach identity, not just count: block if any breach present in 'after' that was not present in 'before' (by symbol+rule key), rather than comparing lengths.

title: _held_qty does not consider short positions, so a risk-reducing BUY-to-cover is blocked by the allowlist
description: closing_sell logic (line 417) only permits SELLs of held longs past the allowlist. A short position (qty<0) that needs a BUY to cover is risk-reducing too, but _held_qty returns a negative number and the closing-sell branch only checks side=='sell' and held_now>0. A buy-to-cover on a since-narrowed allowlist gets blocked, preventing risk reduction.
fix: Also permit a BUY past the allowlist when _held_qty(symbol)<0 and the buy qty does not exceed the short size (a covering buy), mirroring the closing-sell carve-out.

title: rearm session_open check reads session_whitelist default ['regular'] but evaluate() uses the same default — premarket re-arm impossible even if whitelisted via config absence
description: rearm with halt_rearm=='session_open' requires market_session() in cfg.get('session_whitelist',['regular']). If the operator intends premarket trading but left session_whitelist unset, the default ['regular'] blocks re-arm during premarket. This is defensible, but the default differs from the operator's apparent intent and there's no signal to the user why re-arm failed beyond 'session not tradable'.
fix: No behavior change required; ensure the returned reason names the whitelist so the operator understands the default is in effect, and document that session_whitelist must include 'premarket' to re-arm then.

title: trades/day cap counts orders by created_at/submitted_at UTC date, not ET session date — cap resets at 00:00 UTC mid-session
description: _trades_today counts aj_orders where substr(COALESCE(submitted_at,created_at),1,10)=_today() and _today() is UTC. The daily trade cap therefore resets at 19:00-20:00 ET (00:00 UTC), allowing the per-day cap to be effectively doubled across a single ET evening/after-hours session.
fix: Compute the trade-day boundary in ET (convert to America/New_York before slicing) so the trades/day cap aligns with the trading session, matching the intended daily semantics.

title: PUBLIC retry sets fallback_used=1 though it re-calls the same chat_any backend
description: On the public quality-floor miss, the code sets fallback_used=1 and escalated=1 and then simply calls _ai().chat_any(...) again. chat_any does not switch to a different/fallback model on demand — it's the same routing — so the recorded fallback_used telemetry is misleading and pollutes the eval loop that consumes aj_routing rows.
fix: Only set fallback_used when a different backend is actually used, or rename/clear the flag; record escalated=1 alone for a same-backend retry.

title: check-then-act on local model availability: _local_available() then _ollama_chat can race a server going down
description: route() calls _local_available() (a 60s-cached probe) and, if true, proceeds to _ollama_chat. The probe is cached, so a PRIVATE prompt can be routed 'local available' while the local server is actually down; _ollama_chat then returns None and ok=False — acceptable fail-closed — but escalation logic at line 111 (`text is not None`) means a None first result skips the retry, so a transient blip yields a hard step failure even though a retry might have reached a recovered server.
fix: Allow one retry on private path even when first text is None (transient connection blip), bounded by max_escalations, since fail-closed semantics are preserved either way.

title: is_private classifier is heuristic and order-dependent; a private prompt lacking cue words egresses to a cloud model
description: When sensitivity is None it's inferred from is_private(_messages_text(messages)). is_private only matches money/share regex, first-person-holding phrases, and a fixed cue list. A genuinely private prompt that paraphrases (e.g. 'liquidate everything we discussed' or a ticker list with target weights but no $ sign and no cue word) classifies PUBLIC and is sent to chat_any -> potentially OpenAI, leaking portfolio intent. The spec demands fail-closed on privacy; a heuristic that defaults ambiguous prompts to PUBLIC is fail-open.
fix: Default to PRIVATE when the prompt is non-trivial and any portfolio context module is in play (e.g. when called from the operator/holdings path, pass sensitivity=PRIVATE explicitly), and broaden/strengthen the classifier; treat unknown as private for holdings-adjacent callers.

title: Time-of-day filter assumes a fixed 390-min session and ignores half-days/DST edge
description: _minutes_into_regular computes (hour*60+min) - (9*60+30) in America/New_York and enforces mins>(390-skip_close). On NYSE half-days (1:00pm close = 210 min) the 390 constant lets late-session trades through when they should be blocked, and pre-open/after-hours minutes go negative making mins<skip_open trivially true. The session==regular check from aj_db.market_session presumably gates this, but the hard-coded 390 is wrong on early-close days.
fix: Derive the session length from market_session/calendar (handle half-days) instead of the literal 390; clamp negative mins to a sentinel.

title: expire_stale_orders counts cycles with a strict > on created_at, off-by-one on same-timestamp cycles
description: cycles_since counts aj_cycles WHERE started_at > created_at. A cycle that started at exactly the order's created_at timestamp (same second, since utc_now_iso truncates microseconds) is excluded, under-counting elapsed cycles by one and delaying TTL expiry by a cycle. With second-granularity timestamps and fast cycles, the order and the creating cycle frequently share a timestamp.
fix: Use >= and subtract the creating cycle, or count cycles started strictly after the order's cycle_id rather than its wall-clock created_at; alternatively store cycle_id on the order and compare ids.

title: peak_mark uses `marks.get(sym) or avg_cost`, masking a real 0.0 mark and capping peak low
description: mark = marks.get(sym) or float(p.get('avg_cost') or 0). A legitimate 0.0 mark (illiquid/quote glitch) is treated as missing and replaced by avg_cost. While 0 is implausible for a real price, a transient mark below avg_cost that happens to round/parse to 0 would peg peak/last to avg_cost, corrupting the trailing-stop peak. Use explicit None handling to avoid the `falsy 0` trap.
fix: mark_val = marks.get(sym); mark = mark_val if mark_val is not None else float(p.get('avg_cost') or 0).

title: Merging alpha exits dedups by symbol but can drop a tighter core stop in favor of nothing
description: exit_signals adds alpha exits only if e['symbol'] not in have (core reasons win). That's the documented intent. However the alpha TP-ladder emits PARTIAL qty for a symbol; if a core full-exit is NOT queued for that symbol but a previous alpha rung already added it to `have` within the same call, a second alpha signal for the same symbol (e.g. ATR-stop full exit) is silently dropped — so a partial ladder sell can suppress a same-cycle full protective stop on that name.
fix: Allow a full-exit alpha signal to supersede an already-queued partial for the same symbol, or evaluate protective stops (ATR/time) before the ladder so the stronger exit wins.

title: Key-file generation has a TOCTOU window: O_EXCL loser re-reads, but a partially-written winner file can be read empty
description: The O_EXCL path correctly makes the loser re-read the winner's file, but the winner writes the key in two steps (open with O_EXCL, then fchmod, then os.write). A concurrent process that hits the `os.path.exists(path)` branch at line 55 (or the FileExistsError re-read at line 70) can open and read the file in the tiny window after creation but before os.write completes, getting b'' (empty), then `.strip()` yields b'' and Fernet(b'') raises later — an intermittent startup failure.
fix: Write to a temp file then os.rename() into place atomically (rename is atomic on POSIX), so any reader sees either no file or the complete key, never a half-written one.

title: Reading the key file does not validate it; an empty or truncated file yields a key that fails downstream, not at load
description: _load_master_key returns f.read().strip() from the key file without validating it through Fernet(kb) the way the env path does (line 52). A zero-byte or corrupted key file (e.g., disk-full during first write, or the race above) returns bad bytes; the failure only surfaces later inside _fernet()/encrypt where it's harder to diagnose and may be swallowed by store()'s broad except.
fix: Validate the file-loaded key with Fernet(kb) before returning (mirroring the env-key validation), so a malformed key file fails loudly at load time.

title: delete() commits via db.get_conn() outside set_setting, but never goes through the cache-coherent write path
description: delete() does a raw DELETE + commit under db._write_lock, then best-effort calls db._invalidate_settings_cache(). Because secret keys are __-prefixed they're excluded from get_settings() cache, so this is mostly fine — but has() and lease() read the settings table directly (not via cache), so they will see the delete. The real issue: the manual `db.get_conn().execute(...); db.get_conn().commit()` pattern relies on both calls returning the same thread-local conn; under db's pooling that holds, but it bypasses set_setting's invariants. If a future change makes get_conn pool across calls, the DELETE and commit could hit different connections.
fix: Add a database.delete_setting() helper (mirroring set_setting) and call it, so deletion uses the same audited, cache-coherent path; avoid the two-call get_conn pattern.

title: size_order does not guard aj_risk._order_price returning non-numeric/NaN
description: price = aj_risk._order_price(...). The check `price is None or price <= 0` does not catch NaN (NaN<=0 is False), so a NaN price passes through and propagates into qty = target/price (NaN) and notional, ultimately producing a NaN-qty order that downstream money()/risk checks may mishandle.
fix: Add a finite/NaN guard: if price is None or not math.isfinite(price) or price <= 0: return None (import math).

title: target capped to max_notional AFTER multiplier but min-notional floor applied to post-cap notional only
description: target = min(target, max_notional) clamps the up-sized target to the per-order cap (good). But when sizing_multiplier up-sizes target above max_notional, the clamp silently discards the conviction/Kelly up-size — capping is correct, yet the min_order_notional floor (line 71-72) then operates on the capped notional. If max_notional itself is below min_order_notional (misconfig), every order is silently skipped with only a debug log, hiding a config error.
fix: Emit a warning (not debug) when notional < min_notional because max_notional < min_order_notional, so the contradictory config is visible to the operator.

title: _summarize formats day_pnl with ',.2f' but the value may be a non-numeric/None-coerced string
description: `'${:,.2f}'.format(data.get('day_pnl') or 0)`. If aj_risk.compute_day_pnl() returns day_pnl as a string (e.g. '123.45') or a Decimal-as-str, format spec ',.2f' raises ValueError (can't format str with .2f). The except at line 75 catches it and returns the generic 'Here's what I found.', silently losing the actual P&L the user asked for.
fix: Coerce numerically: `'${:,.2f}'.format(float(data.get('day_pnl') or 0))` inside the try, so numeric strings are handled.

title: _summarize hardcodes 'on (paper)' regardless of live mode, misreporting a live-enabled state
description: For aj_status it says "Trading is {'on (paper)' if on else 'off'}". If the operator has enabled live trading, the spoken status still says 'on (paper)', actively misinforming the operator about whether real money is at risk — a dangerous misstatement for a trading agent.
fix: Read the actual mode/live flag from the status dict and report 'on (live)' vs 'on (paper)' accordingly.

title: alt_data_engine cache dicts mutated without a lock
description: _cache_get/_cache_set touch shared `_cache`/`_cache_ts` with no synchronization while nowcast_bulk fans out via safe_executor. Concurrent writes/reads can corrupt the dicts or read partially-written entries.
fix: Protect _cache/_cache_ts with a threading.Lock.

title: intel_filing_detail parses non-existent EDGAR -index.json schema
description: The route fetches `{acc}-index.json` and reads `idx_data.get('documents', [])` (lines 1542-1553). Per sec_edgar.py's own comment (line 377) the real EDGAR index.json structure is `{'directory': {'item': [...]}}`, not a top-level `documents` list (each item has 'name', not 'document'/'type'/'sequence'). So `idx_data.get('documents', [])` is always empty, primary_doc stays None, and the route returns 'Cannot find primary document' 400 for every uncached filing — the full-text filing analysis feature never works.
fix: Parse the actual schema: iterate `idx_data.get('directory', {}).get('item', [])`, match by `item.get('type') == form_type` or the first item, and use `item.get('name')` as the document filename. Keep the existing fallback to the first item.

title: Crypto price alerts never trigger in the snapshot worker
description: The alert loop reuses `prices` from _portfolio_live_prices, then fetches any missing alert symbols via fetcher.get_quotes_batch(missing) (line 283). For a crypto alert symbol like 'BTC', get_quotes_batch fetches the literal 'BTC' (an equity lookup), not 'BTC-USD', so it returns no price and the alert is skipped forever. The portfolio path special-cases crypto by appending -USD, but the alert path does not, so crypto price alerts can never fire.
fix: When building the `missing` set, map crypto alert symbols to their -USD Yahoo pair before fetching, mirroring _portfolio_live_prices (track which alert symbols are crypto via the watchlist/holdings asset_type, append '-USD', and map the returned -USD price back to the bare symbol key).

title: portfolio_ai_analysis crashes when a live price is 0
description: `market_value = price * h['shares'] if price is not None else cost_basis` uses `price is not None` (correct), but later line 1349 `round(price, 4) if price else None` and the surrounding math assume price truthiness inconsistently. More concretely, a quote dict missing 'price' gives price=None handled, but a returned price of 0.0 (real but falsy) makes current_price None while market_value computed as 0*shares=0, diverging from the cost-basis fallback the rest of the code uses (e.g. stress_test line 1247 explicitly treats real 0 as not-missing). The inconsistency yields a position valued at 0 in the AI summary instead of cost basis.
fix: Use the same convention as stress_test/dividends: `cur = price if price is not None else h['avg_cost']` then `market_value = cur * h['shares']`, and set current_price with `round(price,4) if price is not None else None` (drop the truthiness test).

title: update_settings persists keys partially with no rollback on later failure
description: The loop writes each setting immediately via db.set_setting(k, v) (line 1032). If a later sensitive key fails api_keys.save_key validation, the route returns 400 (line 1026) but all earlier db.set_setting writes have already committed. The client sees an error and assumes nothing saved, leaving settings in a half-applied state.
fix: Validate all keys first (build a list of (k,v) to write and run save_key checks) and only commit the db.set_setting writes after every key passes; or wrap the writes in a single transaction and roll back on the first error before returning 400.

title: earnings_dossier caches AI brief even when AI generation failed
description: After building the dossier, brief = ai_summarizer.generate_earnings_brief(...) (line 1303). If the AI call returns an error/empty/placeholder brief (e.g. no API key, rate-limited), the code still db.cache_earnings_dossier(symbol, dossier) (line 1307). Because the cache check at line 1292 only requires cached.get('brief') truthy, a failed/placeholder brief gets cached for 6h and subsequent requests keep serving the bad brief even after the key is fixed.
fix: Only cache when the brief is a genuine success: check brief truthiness and absence of an error marker before db.cache_earnings_dossier, e.g. `if brief and not (isinstance(brief, dict) and brief.get('error')): db.cache_earnings_dossier(...)`.

title: Snapshot worker thread has no shutdown path; daemon loop can double-write across reloads
description: _snapshot_worker is an infinite `while True` daemon thread started at import. There is no stop event, so on Werkzeug reload (or repeated imports in tests) additional snapshot threads can accumulate; each independently calls db.save_snapshot for 'today' (INSERT OR REPLACE) and re-fetches quotes every 5 min, multiplying upstream load. The _IS_RELOADER_PARENT guard only prevents the parent, not repeated child reloads.
fix: Add a module-level threading.Event and only start the worker once (guard with a module-level _snapshot_started flag set under a lock); honor the event in the loop's sleep so reloads can stop the prior thread.

title: add_position does not validate asset_type, allowing invalid types that break crypto pricing
description: The route accepts data.get('asset_type', 'stock') verbatim and stores it. Crypto pricing throughout the app keys on `asset_type == 'crypto'` (e.g. _portfolio_live_prices line 112). A typo like 'Crypto' or 'CRYPTO' is stored as-is, so the holding is treated as an equity, its symbol fetched as a stock (no -USD), and it never gets a live price. add_to_watchlist/add_transaction have the same gap.
fix: Normalize/validate asset_type to a known set before storing: `asset_type = (data.get('asset_type') or 'stock').strip().lower(); if asset_type not in ('stock','crypto','etf',...): asset_type='stock'`.

title: portfolio_import accepts negative/zero avg_cost as 0 and never validates symbol via _valid_ticker
description: Import allows avg_cost None/<=0 to become 0.0 (line 940-941) and validates symbol only with a looser regex `^[A-Z0-9.\\-]{1,10}$` (line 934) rather than _valid_ticker. More importantly each row calls db.add_position directly, bypassing the transaction-logging and numeric-finiteness checks of /api/portfolio/add, so a row with shares like 'inf' (float('inf') parses) or NaN could be stored. float(str(...).replace(',','')) accepts 'inf'/'nan'.
fix: After parsing, reject non-finite values: `if not math.isfinite(shares) or not math.isfinite(avg_cost): skipped += 1; continue`. Optionally route imports through the same validation as add_position.

title: aj_approve_route has a check-then-act TOCTOU on proposal status
description: The approval flow reads the proposal row (get_row), checks status in ('approved','proposed'), then evaluates risk and executes (lines 3439-3455) with no lock or atomic status transition. Two concurrent approval POSTs for the same pid both pass the status check and both call aj_execution.execute_trade, potentially double-executing a trade. For a trading agent this is a serious duplicate-order risk.
fix: Atomically claim the proposal before executing: do a conditional DB update (UPDATE aj_proposals SET status='approving' WHERE id=? AND status IN ('approved','proposed')) and only proceed if exactly one row changed; otherwise return 409.

title: cache_get writes back the (value,expiry,now) tuple outside _mem_lock — can resurrect an evicted key
description: To refresh last_access, cache_get does `_mem[k] = (value, expiry, now)` without the lock. If a concurrent cache_set eviction just popped k (or replaced it with a newer value), this unlocked write can re-insert a stale tuple or clobber the newer value (lost update), because read-modify-write on the same key isn't atomic across the get/set sequence even though a single dict assignment is. Result: a freshly-set value can be overwritten by an older one that a reader had in hand.
fix: Either skip the last_access refresh under contention, or do the write-back under `_mem_lock` with a re-check that _mem[k] is still the same tuple object before replacing.

title: prune_disk size-cap eviction can delete the most-recently-written hot rows (orders by size only)
description: The size cap evicts strictly largest-value-first with no regard to freshness or access. A single large but actively-used cached payload (e.g. a big options chain the UI is currently paging) gets evicted before many small stale rows, causing repeated refetch churn for the hot large entry while cold small rows survive.
fix: Order eviction by a blend: prefer already-expired rows first (DELETE WHERE expiry<now already does this), then among live rows evict by oldest written_at among the largest, e.g. `ORDER BY (expiry < strftime('%s','now')) DESC, length(value) DESC, written_at ASC`.

title: cache_set failure heuristic silently drops legitimately-empty successful responses
description: `_looks_like_failure` treats any empty list/dict and any dict whose non-identifier values are all null as a failure and refuses to cache it (unless allow_empty). A legitimately empty-but-correct upstream answer (e.g. a stock with genuinely zero news items, or an options-less ETF returning {calls:[],puts:[]}) is therefore never cached, so every request re-hits the upstream for a known-empty answer — defeating the cache exactly for the symbols that 404/empty most often.
fix: Callers that can legitimately return empty (get_news, get_option_chain empty, etc.) should pass allow_empty=True with a short TTL, OR _looks_like_failure should not flag {calls:[],puts:[]}-style structured empties. Audit empty-but-valid producers and opt them in.

title: _due/_last_cycle/_fail_count dicts mutated from multiple threads without a lock
description: _loop runs in the warmer thread but _safe's success path writes _last_cycle/_fail_count/_next_retry from the per-call worker thread (_runner runs fn, but the bookkeeping in _safe runs in the loop thread after join — OK), HOWEVER status() reads these dicts from a request thread concurrently with the loop thread's writes. `dict(_last_cycle)` during a concurrent __setitem__ can raise 'dictionary changed size during iteration' under CPython for larger dicts.
fix: Guard reads/writes of _last_cycle/_fail_count/_next_retry with a small lock, or snapshot via list(items()) under that lock in status().

title: Warmer calls _portfolio_symbols()/_watchlist_symbols() every 15s tick (4 DB queries) regardless of due-ness
description: `eq, crypto = _portfolio_symbols(); wl_eq, wl_crypto = _watchlist_symbols()` run unconditionally on every loop iteration (every 15s) even when neither quotes cadence is due, and fundamentals/news/chart call _portfolio_symbols() again separately. That's a steady stream of portfolio/watchlist SELECTs (and a fresh thread-local DB connection if the loop thread rotates) burning DB work for nothing most ticks.
fix: Only fetch symbol lists when at least one consuming task is due (guard the calls behind `if _due('quotes',...) or _due('quotes_crypto',...)`), and reuse the single fetch across fundamentals/news/chart instead of re-querying.

title: Digest schedule uses local naive datetime and date watermark — DST/timezone and multi-instance double-send
description: The digest gate uses `datetime.datetime.now()` (naive local) and compares hour>=digest_hour with a `digest_last_sent` date string. If two app instances/processes run (desktop + dev server) both share the DB and can both pass the gate before either writes digest_last_sent (check-then-set without a lock/atomic), double-sending the digest. Also `_local.hour` ignores the user's configured timezone vs server local time.
fix: Make the set atomic/conditional: `UPDATE settings SET value=? WHERE key='digest_last_sent' AND value<>?` and only deliver if rowcount==1; consider an explicit timezone for digest_hour.

title: Module-level _cache/_cache_ts mutated without a lock under parallel scans
description: _get_cached/_set_cached read and mutate the shared dicts `_cache`/`_cache_ts` with no lock. build_graph/assess_contagion are invoked concurrently (safe_executor fan-out, cluster/divmap sweeps). The eviction block iterates `_cache_ts.items()` while other threads write, risking 'dictionary changed size during iteration' RuntimeError and torn reads.
fix: Guard all _cache/_cache_ts access with a module-level threading.Lock (snapshot keys to a list before iterating for eviction).

title: Lazy _session init is a check-then-act race; concurrent first callers create multiple Sessions
description: `global _session; if _session is None: _session = requests.Session(); _session.headers.update(HEADERS)`. Two threads racing the first call both see None and both build a Session; one wins the global but the other's Session (with headers) may be used for that request mid-init where headers aren't applied yet, and the discarded Session leaks its connection pool. requests.Session isn't guaranteed thread-safe for concurrent init either.
fix: Guard with a module lock (double-checked) or build the Session at import time so it's fully initialized before any request.

title: defillama_tvl_summary sorts/sums on c['tvl'] after filtering isinstance but proto sort uses p['tvl'] unfiltered
description: For protocols (line 217-219) it filters `[p for p in protos if p.get('tvl')]` then sorts by `p['tvl']` — fine. But the truthiness filter drops a protocol with tvl==0 and, more importantly, a tvl that is a string (some Llama rows return strings) passes `p.get('tvl')` truthiness and then `reverse=True` sort compares str vs float across rows -> TypeError, aborting the whole summary (caught by no try here; the function has no try/except, so it raises to the caller).
fix: Filter to numeric tvl like the chains branch does: `[p for p in protos if isinstance(p.get('tvl'),(int,float))]` before sorting, and wrap the function body defensively.

title: mempool_btc_stats indexes blocks[0] but blocks may be a dict on error responses
description: `tip_height = blocks[0].get('height') if blocks else None`. blocks comes from `_get(.../blocks) or []`. If the endpoint returns a JSON object (error body) instead of a list, _get returns that dict (truthy), so `blocks[0]` does dict-key lookup of integer 0 -> KeyError, or on a list of non-dict items `.get` raises AttributeError. The function has no try/except, so it 500s the BTC stats panel.
fix: Validate shape: `tip_height = blocks[0].get('height') if (isinstance(blocks,list) and blocks and isinstance(blocks[0],dict)) else None`.

title: treasury_yield_curve float() on avg_interest_rate_amt can raise on non-numeric
description: `float(r['avg_interest_rate_amt']) if r.get('avg_interest_rate_amt') else None`. Treasury rows occasionally carry 'null' as a literal string or '*' placeholders; float('*') raises ValueError, and the function has no try/except, so the whole yield-curve fetch 500s.
fix: Wrap per-row: `try: rate=float(r['avg_interest_rate_amt']) except (TypeError,ValueError): rate=None`.

title: cboe_vix_history reads entire CSV to find last row via full iteration; also float() unguarded
description: `for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(txt)): last = row` iterates the entire VIX history CSV (decades of rows) on every cache-miss just to get the last line — wasteful but not fatal. The real defect: `float(last['CLOSE']) if last.get('CLOSE') else None` and the HIGH/LOW equivalents raise ValueError if the trailing row is a partial/blank line (CBOE CSVs sometimes end with a stray newline producing a row of empty strings, which `last.get('CLOSE')` truthiness... empty string is falsy so guarded — but a row with 'N/A' is truthy and float() raises).
fix: Parse the tail row defensively with try/except per field, and skip blank trailing rows (`if any(row.values())`).

title: get_transactions appends limit to params even when None default but ORDER BY uses created_at that may be NULL
description: Lower risk, but get_transactions orders by `t.date DESC, t.created_at DESC`. The `date` column is nullable (schema line 129 has no NOT NULL/default) and add_transaction defaults it to today's date string, but rows imported by older builds/external tools may have NULL date — NULL sorts last/first inconsistently and LIMIT then drops real recent rows. Not a crash but can hide transactions from the UI.
fix: COALESCE the sort key: `ORDER BY COALESCE(t.date, t.created_at) DESC, t.created_at DESC`.

title: get_transaction_stats counts buys/sells via SUM(boolean) which is SQLite-specific and miscounts mixed-case beyond BUY/SELL
description: `COALESCE(SUM(upper(action)='BUY'),0)` relies on SQLite evaluating the comparison to 1/0. That works, but any action that isn't exactly 'BUY' or 'SELL' (e.g. 'DIVIDEND','DEPOSIT','BUY ' with trailing space) is excluded from both buys and sells while still counted in total_trades — so buys+sells != total_trades silently, and trailing-whitespace actions (not trimmed) are dropped.
fix: Trim in SQL: `upper(trim(action))='BUY'`; optionally document that non-BUY/SELL actions are intentionally excluded so callers don't assume buys+sells==total.

title: cache_filing dereferences ai_result without None/dict guard
description: cache_filing does `ai_result.get('key_points', [])` and several more `ai_result.get(...)`. If a caller passes ai_result=None (e.g. AI step failed and returned None), this raises AttributeError inside the _write_lock, and unlike other helpers there is no try/except — the exception propagates and the lock context exits without commit (rollback), losing the filing cache write entirely.
fix: Coerce at top: `ai_result = ai_result or {}`.

title: save_scan_history float(composite) coerces None->0 silently and can raise on non-numeric
description: `float(opp.get('composite') or 0)` turns a missing composite into 0.0 (a real score), which pollutes the scanner history timeline and get_scanner_watchlist AVG/MAX stats with spurious zeros. If composite is a non-numeric string, float() raises inside executemany's list comprehension, aborting the entire batch insert (no rows saved).
fix: Skip rows without a numeric composite or store NULL: compute composite safely with try/except per row and use None instead of 0 when absent, so AVG/MAX ignore them.

title: init_db runs DDL/commits without _write_lock while other threads may write
description: init_db() executes many CREATE/ALTER/INSERT and conn.commit() with no _write_lock. If the cache warmer or a request thread is already running (start() is called from multiple boot paths) a concurrent writer can interleave; the ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN migrations are particularly racy and a concurrent get_conn() on another thread can hit a half-migrated schema.
fix: Wrap the migration/DDL section (or at least the ALTER TABLE migrations and the settings seeding) in `with _write_lock:` consistent with every other writer.

title: fast_info.regular_market_price accessed via attribute, not getattr — AttributeError fallback path
description: In get_quote() (line 566) and get_quotes_batch._resolve() (line 672) the code does `info.regular_market_price` directly on yfinance's fast_info. fast_info has no `regular_market_price` attribute (the correct name is `last_price`); accessing a missing key on fast_info raises (KeyError/AttributeError). This only triggers when last_price is None, but in exactly that degraded case the intended secondary lookup raises instead of returning None, so the whole quote falls into the except branch and the result/structured fields are never built — losing the genuine fallback the code intended.
fix: Use getattr with default: `price = _lp if _lp is not None else _safe(getattr(info, 'regular_market_price', None))` in both locations, mirroring how the other optional fast_info fields are read.

title: Sortino denominator uses full-period downside std but annualizes inconsistently
description: Sortino computes `sortino_denom` from `downside.std()*sqrt(252)` for the guard, but then the actual ratio divides by `downside.std()` (un-annualized) and multiplies numerator by sqrt(252). That is internally consistent only by luck; more importantly `downside = r[r<0]` computes std over only negative days but is divided as if it were the full-sample downside deviation. Standard Sortino uses sqrt(mean(min(r,0)^2)) over ALL observations, not std of the negatives subset. The result understates downside risk (denominator too small because positive days are dropped from the deviation base), inflating the Sortino ratio.
fix: Compute downside deviation over the full sample: `dd = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.minimum(r - rf_daily, 0.0)**2)))` then `sortino = (r.mean()-rf_daily)/dd*sqrt(252)` when dd>0.

title: _yahoo_chart_direct drops a legitimate flat/zero prev_close change to None
description: `chg = round(price-prev,4) if (price is not None and prev) else None` uses truthiness of `prev`; a prev_close of 0 (rare but possible for some instruments) yields None for change AND change_pct is then None. More commonly, `chg_pct` is gated on `chg is not None and prev` — fine — but a genuine 0.0 change is computed correctly here. The real bug: when price is a valid 0.0 (e.g. a defaulted/penny value) `price is not None` is True but a 0 price with valid prev still computes negative change; that's acceptable. The concrete defect is the `prev` truthiness gate silently nulling change for a 0 previous close instead of leaving price intact.
fix: Guard explicitly on None and zero only for the division: `chg = round(price-prev,4) if (price is not None and prev is not None) else None` and `chg_pct = round((chg/prev)*100,4) if (chg is not None and prev) else None`.

title: ATR uses highs[-i]/lows[-i] with closes[-i-1] but iterates i from 1..14 over the WRONG bars
description: ATR loop: `for i in range(1, min(15, len(closes)))` uses highs[-i], lows[-i], closes[-i-1]. For i=1 this is the latest bar's high/low vs the previous close — correct. But it only averages up to 14 true ranges taken from the most recent 14 bars, which is a simple TR average, not Wilder's ATR (which is an EMA-style smoothing). More concretely, `highs` and `lows` are full-length lists while the TR uses `closes[-i-1]`; when len(closes)==15 exactly, i can reach 14 making closes[-15] valid, but the count of TRs is 14 — fine. The defect is mislabeling a 14-bar simple TR mean as ATR; downstream consumers expecting Wilder ATR get a different (more jumpy) value.
fix: Either rename to atr_simple or implement Wilder smoothing: seed with the first 14-TR mean then `atr = (atr*(13)+tr)/14` across remaining bars. At minimum document that this is a simple TR average.

title: Dividend year extraction can raise on non-date index slipping past hasattr guard
description: `yr = dt.year if hasattr(dt,'year') else int(str(dt)[:4])`. If dt is a string like '' or a value whose first 4 chars aren't numeric (e.g. a malformed index), `int(str(dt)[:4])` raises ValueError. The whole block is wrapped in try/except so it degrades to div_growth_5y=None, but it silently loses the computation for an entire ticker whenever any one index entry is malformed.
fix: Wrap the per-entry parse: `try: yr = dt.year if hasattr(dt,'year') else int(str(dt)[:4]) except (ValueError,TypeError): continue` so one bad row doesn't abort the whole CAGR.

title: Options flow scan assumes ticker.options is a sliceable sequence
description: `scan_exps = exps[:6]` after `exps = ticker.options`. yfinance returns a tuple normally, but on partial/rate-limited responses .options can be None or a non-sequence; the `if not exps` guard catches None, but a non-empty non-sliceable (e.g. a generator) would raise. Lower risk, but the per-exp loop also calls `ticker.option_chain(exp)` with no validation that exp is a date string.
fix: Coerce defensively: `exps = list(ticker.options or [])` then slice; skip exps that aren't 'YYYY-MM-DD' shaped before option_chain().

title: impliedVolatility multiplied by 100 again in option chain while unusual-flow path also multiplies
description: _option_chain_uncached stores `impliedVolatility: round(iv*100,2)` (percent). But yfinance's impliedVolatility is already a decimal (0.45 = 45%), so *100 is correct here. However get_unusual_options_flow (line 2506) reads `iv = _safe(row.get('impliedVolatility'))` directly from the raw df (decimal) and also does `iv*100`. These two code paths are consistent with each other, BUT any consumer mixing get_option_chain output (already-percent) with raw rows will double-count. The concrete bug is inconsistency risk; verify no consumer feeds get_option_chain's already-scaled IV back through a *100 path.
fix: Document the unit contract; ensure only one layer scales IV. Prefer returning raw decimal IV from both and scaling only at the presentation layer.

title: top_movers losers slice can still overlap gainers when ranked length is odd
description: `split = len(ranked)//2; gainers = ranked[:min(10,split or len(ranked))]; losers = ranked[-min(10, len(ranked)-len(gainers)):]`. When len(ranked) is small and odd (e.g. 3), split=1, gainers=ranked[:1], losers=ranked[-min(10,2):]=ranked[-2:] — the middle element (index1) is excluded, OK. But when len(ranked)==1, split=0, `split or len(ranked)` -> 1, gainers=ranked[:1]; losers slice = ranked[-min(10,0):]=ranked[-0:]=ranked[:] which is the FULL list — so the single name appears in BOTH gainers and losers.
fix: Guard the losers slice on remaining count: `rem = len(ranked)-len(gainers); losers_slice = ranked[-min(10,rem):] if rem>0 else []` (the current code computes rem but `ranked[-0:]` is the whole list — use an explicit rem>0 check before slicing).

title: get_crypto_chart volume join by exact ms timestamp will almost always miss
description: `volumes = {int(v[0]): v[1] for v in data.get('total_volumes',[])}` keyed on price-point ms, then `volumes.get(int(ts_ms), 0)`. CoinGecko's prices[] and total_volumes[] timestamps are sampled independently and frequently differ by a few ms/seconds, so the exact-key lookup misses for most points and volume is reported as 0 across the chart.
fix: Align by index (prices and total_volumes are returned in parallel order/length) or bucket timestamps to the nearest sample; e.g. zip prices and total_volumes by position.

title: Brier outcome uses realized_return>0 but ensemble logs RANGE/NEUTRAL as direction with prob_up around 0.5
description: _brier_from_rows scores outcome = 1 if realized_return>0 else 0 and compares to metadata prob_up. NEUTRAL ensemble calls (direction NEUTRAL, prob_up≈0.5) are logged with a prob_up in metadata and DO get scored here even though research_tracker._direction_matches treats NEUTRAL as unscored (hit None). So the Brier sample includes neutral calls while the hit-rate leaderboard excludes them — the two metrics are computed over different populations, making brier_skill and hit_rate inconsistent for the same component.
fix: Filter pairs to directional rows only (skip rows whose predicted_direction is NEUTRAL, or whose hit is None) so Brier and hit-rate cover the same population; pass hit/direction through get_scored_rows (already available) and require it to be non-null.

title: Missing-signal default weight of 0.1 distorts adaptive renormalization
description: total_w = sum(weights.get(k, 0.1) for k in raw_signals) and per-signal w = weights.get(key,0.1)/total_w. _BASE_WEIGHTS covers all six component keys, so .get default 0.1 should never fire for known signals. But adaptive_weights returns a dict that is renormalized to the same TOTAL as base (sum ~1.0) across all six keys; when only a subset of signals is available, using weights.get(k,0.1) over the available subset re-normalizes correctly, yet the 0.1 fallback could silently mask a missing key produced by a future adaptive_weights that drops keys, giving an arbitrary 0.1 weight rather than the intended base. Fragile coupling.
fix: Use the explicit base weight as the fallback: `weights.get(k, _BASE_WEIGHTS.get(k, 0.1))`, so a key missing from adaptive output falls back to its real base weight rather than a flat 0.1.

title: parallel_map results assumed positionally aligned with jobs without checking for exceptions
description: results = safe_executor.parallel_map(...) is zipped back by index into by_name. If parallel_map returns exceptions as results (or a shorter list on partial failure), `results[i]` could be an Exception object or raise IndexError. The extractors are documented to never raise, but parallel_map's contract isn't validated here; a thread that raised would put a non-dict into by_name and later `by_name.get('ml') or {}` handles ml, but bootstrap/narrative could be an Exception passing the truthiness check and then `.get` would AttributeError in _build_return_cone / probs access.
fix: Defensively coerce: after building by_name, replace any non-dict/Exception values with None (e.g. `v = v if isinstance(v, dict) else None`) for bootstrap/narrative, and for ml ensure it's a dict. Or wrap each job to guarantee a dict/None return.

title: Gamma wall support/resistance labels are inverted
description: For each top wall, type='resistance' if strike>=spot else 'support'. Strikes ABOVE spot with large positive gamma act as resistance and strikes BELOW as support is the conventional read, but the frontend (app.js line 7528) colors 'support' green and 'resistance' red and the GEX narrative treats walls below spot as support — consistent. However the assignment uses a pure price test and ignores the SIGN of net_gex; a large NEGATIVE net_gex strike below spot is mislabeled 'support' when short-gamma below spot accelerates declines. The label therefore can mislead in short-gamma regimes.
fix: Optionally factor net_gex sign into the wall classification, or document that 'type' is purely positional; at minimum keep it consistent with the regime so short-gamma walls aren't shown as stabilizing support.

title: _weighted_pick comment claims watchlist weight redistribution but never redistributes; empty pools just get lower selection odds skewed
description: The function builds sources/weights only for non-empty pools, then random.choices over them. The comment 'If watchlist is empty/excluded, redistribute its weight pro-rata' is not implemented — when watchlist is empty it's simply absent from sources, so equity(0.70)/crypto(0.15) are used with un-normalized weights (random.choices normalizes internally, so it's actually fine). The dead comment is misleading but behavior is acceptable. However, if ALL of a chosen source's candidates are excluded, it falls back to ANY non-excluded across all pools, ignoring weights entirely — a subtle bias, not a crash.
fix: Remove the misleading comment; optionally, on the exclude-fallback, re-run the weighted pick over pools that still have candidates rather than flattening to a uniform random.choice.

title: CONCENTRATES verdict_detail uses f-string with literal {symbol} then .format(symbol=...) — double-templating fragility
description: verdict_detail is built as an f-string that contains a literal '{symbol}' inside the second line (not interpolated by the f-string because it's on a concatenated plain string), then .format(symbol=symbol) is applied. This works only because the f-string parts don't contain other braces. If avg_corr or high_count rendering ever introduced a literal brace it would raise KeyError in .format(). The DIVERSIFIES/NEUTRAL branches use pure f-strings with {symbol} already interpolated — inconsistent and error-prone.
fix: Make the CONCENTRATES branch a single consistent f-string (interpolate {symbol} directly) and drop the trailing .format(), matching the other two branches.

title: Peer rank uses order.index(symbol.upper()) fallback to order.index(symbol) but order holds raw r['symbol'] which may already be the pick's case
description: In _compute_peers ranks, `order` is built from r['symbol'] (the original-cased symbols). pick_pos tries order.index(symbol.upper()) then order.index(symbol). If the pick symbol in rows is lower/mixed case and differs from both symbol.upper() and symbol-as-passed, both .index() raise ValueError and the metric is silently skipped (caught). Peers fetched via fetcher may echo a canonical case. This can drop the pick from rank computations for symbols with case mismatches.
fix: Normalize all r['symbol'] to upper when building rows/order, and look up with symbol.upper() only; or compare case-insensitively when locating pick_pos.

title: _compute_sizing divides by per_share_risk and price without guarding price<=0 after stop derivation
description: shares = max_loss/per_share_risk guarded by per_share_risk>0, but then `shares = position_value/price` in the cap branch divides by price with no >0 guard. The function early-returns if not price, but price could be a tiny positive that still passes truthiness; and if price is negative (bad data) the cap recompute yields negative shares. Also `2 if price < 50 else 0` rounding assumes price>0.
fix: Validate price>0 explicitly at entry (`if not price or price<=0: return {available:False}`) instead of relying on truthiness.

title: Trade-plan entry band uses daily_vol/100*0.5 where daily_vol is already a percent — fine, but annual_vol default 25.0 silently applied when vol missing skews stops
description: annual_vol defaults to 25.0 when risk has no annual_volatility_pct, but per the comment at line 636-637 the risk_block keys were historically mis-mapped. If risk_block.annual_volatility_pct is None (e.g. crypto/ETF with no risk metrics), every trade plan uses a flat 25% vol → identical stop distances regardless of the asset's true risk. Functional but produces misleading uniform stops.
fix: When vol is missing, derive a fallback from the asset's recent ATR or mark the plan as 'vol-unavailable, default stop' so the UI flags the assumption.

title: get_warmed_dossier / list_warmed_symbols read via db.get_conn() without holding _write_lock during a concurrent INSERT OR REPLACE checkpoint
description: Reads use db.get_conn() (thread-local) while warm_pool does INSERT OR REPLACE + wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) under _write_lock. With WAL this is generally safe for readers, but the TRUNCATE checkpoint briefly takes an exclusive lock; a reader mid-statement could hit 'database is locked' since these read paths have no retry/try-except (unlike _count_fresh/_state_get which catch). An exception here propagates into the /api/ideas request path.
fix: Wrap get_warmed_dossier and list_warmed_symbols DB reads in try/except returning None/[] on sqlite OperationalError (matching the defensive pattern used elsewhere in the module), or use a busy_timeout.

title: unrealized_pct returns 0 (not None) when cost<=0, polluting all-time best/worst ranking
description: `"unrealized_pct": round((mv-cost)/cost*100,2) if cost>0 else 0`. A position with zero/unknown cost gets unrealized_pct=0, which then ranks as a valid 0% return in _answer_portfolio's all-time best/worst (which filters with _finite, and 0 is finite). A free/gifted position with cost 0 distorts the best/worst-all-time answer by appearing as exactly breakeven.
fix: Use None instead of 0 when cost<=0 so downstream _finite filters exclude it from ranking.

title: _streak_card drops snapshots whose total_value is exactly 0 via truthiness filter
description: `vals = [_finite(s.get("total_value")) for s in snaps]; vals = [v for v in vals if v]`. The second filter drops any value of 0.0 (falsy). A legitimate snapshot with total_value 0 (empty book day) is silently removed, which can splice together non-adjacent sessions and miscount the streak, or hide a real down-to-zero event.
