fix: Filter on `v is not None` instead of `if v`, so a real 0.0 snapshot is preserved.

title: Streak counting treats a flat (zero-diff) day inconsistently
description: In _streak_card, diffs of exactly 0 hit the else branch and break the streak, which is intended, but the conditions `d>0 and streak>=0` / `d<0 and streak<=0` mean the very first nonzero diff from streak=0 always counts. A sequence ending in [+,+,0] breaks at the 0 (correct), but [0,+,+] starting mid-window is fine. The subtle bug: a single 0 diff in the MIDDLE of an up-run silently truncates the streak even when the run clearly continues, understating streaks. Likely acceptable but worth noting as a correctness edge.
fix: If intended to ignore flat days, `continue` on d==0 instead of breaking; otherwise document that flat days reset streaks.

title: away_digest gap computed from naive strptime of UTC strings, but last_seen may carry tz/format drift
description: gap_min parses both now and last_seen with strptime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') after slicing [:19]. If last_seen was ever stored in ISO format with a 'T' (e.g. '2026-06-26T12:00:00'), [:19] keeps the 'T' and strptime raises, silently setting gap_min=None and then treating the visit as a valid 'away' (skips the <30min guard), replaying the digest on every tab switch.
fix: Normalize last_seen by replacing 'T' with ' ' before slicing, or parse with a tolerant fromisoformat fallback.

title: portfolio_attribution share_of_move_pct can mislead when total has opposite sign to day_pnl
description: share_of_move_pct = day_pnl/total*100 when abs(total)>=1. If a holding's day_pnl is +500 but the net total is -2000 (book down despite a winner), share_of_move_pct becomes -25%, a negative 'share of move' that the _answer_why _phrase only prints when `>0`, so it's hidden — fine for _answer_why. But the raw tool output (portfolio_attribution) is consumed by the agent/LLM with a negative share_of_move that reads nonsensically ('contributed -25% of the move').
fix: Either omit share_of_move_pct when its sign opposes the net move, or document it as signed contribution so the LLM interprets it correctly.

title: attribution_window baseline selection can pick a snapshot older than 1.5x window via fallback
description: older = snapshots <= target; base = older[-1] if older else snaps[0]. When there's no snapshot old enough, it falls back to snaps[0] (the oldest), then rejects via `span > days*1.5`. But if snaps[0] happens to be, say, 10 days old for a requested 7-day window, span=10 <= 10.5 passes, and the answer claims to attribute 'the last week' using a 10-day baseline — the very mislabeling the docstring warns against, because 1.5x of 7 is 10.5 not strictly tied to the label.
fix: Tighten the fallback acceptance (e.g. span<=days*1.25) or always surface the actual span days in the label when it diverges (already partially done in _answer_why_window, but the tool consumer attribution_window doesn't).

title: Thanks-ack rotation keyed on len(q) of ORIGINAL query but remainder already stripped
description: _answer_social: the ack index is `len(q) % len(_THANKS_ACKS)` using q (original full message). The comment says deterministic per query length — fine, but q includes the stripped thanks phrase, so 'thanks' and 'thank you' map to different acks by length, which is intended. No bug in rotation itself. The real issue: _THANKS_RE.search matches anywhere, so a long message containing 'thanks' as a substring of another word? \b boundaries prevent that. This is acceptable; downgrading. Keeping as a note that q vs ql length is used inconsistently across the module.
fix: No change required; documented for consistency.

title: _SEMMEM_BACKFILLED check-then-set is not atomic across threads
description: _memory_block sets `global _SEMMEM_BACKFILLED; if not _SEMMEM_BACKFILLED: _SEMMEM_BACKFILLED=True; index_memories()`. Two concurrent requests can both read False before either sets True, running index_memories() twice (the one-shot guarantee fails). index_memories backfill running twice concurrently could double-embed or contend.
fix: Guard the flag flip with a module lock, or set the flag inside a lock-protected critical section before launching the backfill.

title: ask_stream deadline computed as ~1050s far exceeds typical proxy/client timeouts
description: _ASK_STREAM_DEADLINE = 55*3*(5+1)+60 = 1050 seconds (17.5 min). A streaming worker can keep billing OpenAI for ~17 minutes before the deadline abandons it. The comment justifies sizing to the loop, but 1050s is far beyond any reasonable user-facing wait and most reverse proxies will drop the SSE connection long before, leaving the daemon worker running (and billing) with no consumer until it finishes.
fix: Cap the deadline to a sane ceiling (e.g. 180-240s) and rely on the cancel flag + per-round cap re-check to stop spend; the agent's own _cap_exceeded and round cap already bound cost.

title: web_research citation harvesting calls c.get on items not verified to be dicts
description: In _agent_ask: `cites=(json.loads(result) or {}).get('citations') or []; for c in cites: if c.get('url')...`. If a citation entry is a string or non-dict, c.get raises AttributeError. It's inside a try/except (line 825), so it's swallowed — but a single malformed citation aborts harvesting ALL citations for that call, dropping legitimate sources.
fix: Filter `for c in cites if isinstance(c, dict)` before calling c.get, so one bad entry doesn't discard the rest.

title: _confidence 'two engines' branch reached for any distinct count of exactly 2, but len>=3 high and ==1 moderate leave ==2 as the final return — correct, yet salvaged-with-2 mislabeled
description: _confidence: when salvaged=True it returns low first (good). But when succeeded is passed and equals e.g. 2 tools that returned data on a clean run, the final `return {'level':'moderate','note':'two engines consulted'}` is fine. The actual bug: when `succeeded` is an empty list [] (not None) — all tools errored — `graded=succeeded=[]`, distinct=[], and it hits `if not distinct: if used: low 'no usable data'`. Good. But if succeeded is None and used has 2 entries, it says 'two engines consulted' even if both errored, overstating confidence. The succeeded-aware grading only triggers when succeeded is explicitly passed.
fix: Ensure callers always pass succeeded (even []) so error-only runs never grade on mere invocation; or treat succeeded is None with used present as low-confidence until proven.

title: _answer_forecast prints prob_up default 0.5 when prob is None, fabricating a coin-flip
description: `(prob or 0.5)*100`. When ens.get('prob_up') is None or 0.0, this substitutes 0.5 (50%) — fabricating a neutral forecast the engine never produced. A genuine prob_up of 0.0 (strong down) becomes 50%, inverting the signal.
fix: Branch on `prob is None`: if None, omit the P(up) clause; only default-display when truly absent, and never coerce 0.0 to 0.5.

title: Forecast clarify choices sort by shares*avg_cost (cost basis) not market value
description: When forecast is asked with no symbol, the quick-reply chips pick the top holdings sorted by `-(shares*avg_cost)` — i.e. largest by COST BASIS, not current market value. A position that has dropped 80% but was bought large will rank above a smaller position that has appreciated, so the suggested symbols don't reflect the user's actual largest current exposures.
fix: If a quick price fetch is acceptable, rank by market value; otherwise document that chips are by cost basis. At minimum, this diverges from 'biggest position' semantics used elsewhere.

title: _greeting uses local machine time while market phase uses ET, producing mismatched greetings
description: _greeting() defaults to datetime.now() (server local time), while _market_phase uses _et_now(). On a server in UTC or another timezone, get_briefing's greeting ('Good morning. Markets are open.') can say 'Good evening' while ET markets are mid-session, contradicting itself.
fix: Pass _et_now() into _greeting() in get_briefing/_answer_social so the greeting and market phase share the same clock.

title: _answer_holding_period uses naive datetime.now() vs a date parsed without tz, off-by-one near midnight/DST
description: d0=strptime(date[:10]) is midnight-naive; days=(datetime.now()-d0).days uses server-local now. Across timezones/DST or just near midnight, the holding-day count can be off by one, and 'bought today' (days<1) can mislabel a purchase made yesterday in ET as today (or vice versa) depending on server tz.
fix: Compute days using date arithmetic on date objects (datetime.now().date() - d0.date()).days, avoiding time-of-day and tz skew.

title: _answer_trading_agent recent-orders formatting calls float(o.get('qty') or 0) but o.get('side','').upper() assumes string
description: `o.get("side","").upper()` — if an order row has side=None (not missing), o.get('side','') returns None (default only applies to MISSING keys), and None.upper() raises AttributeError. The whole _answer_trading_agent is wrapped in try/except returning a generic error, so the activity read fails entirely when any order has a null side.
fix: Use `str(o.get('side') or '').upper()` to tolerate explicit None values.

title: _answer_trading_agent positions formatting indexes p['symbol'] / p['market_value_usd'] by hard key
description: `"{} ({})".format(p["symbol"], _fmt_usd(p["market_value_usd"]))` uses subscripts on agent position dicts. If a position row lacks market_value_usd (the tool maps r.get('market_value') which can be None, and the key is always present, but a malformed row could omit it), a KeyError aborts the answer (caught, generic error). Inconsistent with the .get() style used everywhere else.
fix: Use p.get('symbol') and p.get('market_value_usd').

title: conversation_id int() coercion treats '0' as falsy, dropping a valid conversation id 0
description: `conv_id = int(conversation_id) if conversation_id else None`. If conversation_id is 0 or '0' (a valid id in some schemes), the truthiness test makes it None, losing the thread. Also conversation_id='0' string is truthy so int('0')=0 then later `if conv_id is not None` is True — but conversation_id=0 (int) is falsy → None. Inconsistent handling of id 0 between string and int forms.
fix: Test `if conversation_id is not None and conversation_id != ''` before int(), so id 0 is preserved.

title: Bare-ticker quote fallthrough length check uses len(ql.split())<=4 which misroutes multi-word holdings names
description: The quote fast-path requires `len(ql.split())<=4`. A query like 'how is my palantir technologies doing' resolves a symbol via held-name map but has >4 words, so it skips the quote path and falls to the agent/help. With no agent (keyless), it lands on _HELP_ANSWER instead of quoting the resolved symbol — a regression for keyless users asking about a held name in a natural sentence.
fix: When a symbol resolved and no agent is available, fall back to _answer_quote regardless of word count (the earlier `not _agent_ready()` branch at 4603 already handles this — verify it isn't gated by _debatey incorrectly suppressing simple quotes).

title: _answer_trade resolves company name then re-validates with ^[A-Z] regex, rejecting valid mapped multi-char tickers with digits at start
description: sym=_COMPANY_NAMES.get(raw.lower(), raw.upper()); then `re.match(r'^[A-Z][A-Z0-9.\-]{0,9}$', sym)`. A ticker that legitimately starts with a digit is impossible for US equities, fine. But BRK-B maps fine. The subtler bug: the captured sym group allows up to 10 chars with digits, but _COMPANY_NAMES values like 'BRK-B' pass; however a raw symbol like '8' (single digit) from 'buy 5 8 at 10' would be captured as sym='8' and rejected (good). Net: mostly fine, but rejecting any digit-leading token means crypto-style or numeric tickers in other markets silently fail trade capture.
fix: If non-US tickers are ever in scope, relax the leading-char rule; otherwise document the US-equity assumption. Low impact.

title: Follow-up symbol inheritance fires on bare 'it/its/same/again' even for unrelated questions
description: is_follow_up triggers on any occurrence of it/its/same/again. A question like 'is the market overbought again' contains 'again' and would inherit the previous turn's symbol, turning a market question into a stale single-stock quote. The _FOLLOW_UP_RE is too broad for words like 'again'/'same' that appear in non-referential contexts.
fix: Narrow the follow-up cue (e.g. require leading 'what about'/'how about'/'and' or a sentence-initial pronoun) and exclude when market/portfolio keywords are present.

title: stderr pipe never drained while process runs; can deadlock on large stderr
description: Popen is created with stderr=subprocess.PIPE but stderr is only read AFTER the process exits (line 373). A `claude` subprocess that writes more than the OS pipe buffer (~64KB) to stderr while stdout is being consumed will block on its stderr write, the process never reaches EOF on stdout, the reader thread never gets the sentinel except via the deadline, and `proc.wait(timeout=5)` can hang. stdout is drained in a thread but stderr is not.
fix: Drain stderr concurrently too: spawn a second daemon reader thread that consumes proc.stderr into a buffer (or pass stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL if diagnostics aren't needed), then read the captured buffer instead of proc.stderr.read() at line 373.

title: Per-symbol txn limit applied as global limit truncates sells for other symbols
description: When symbol is None, db.get_transactions(symbol=None, limit=200) returns at most the 200 most recent transactions across ALL symbols. For an active trader this can entirely omit older sells, silently undercounting regret/relief and the net number. The docstring claims '200 covers years' but that is per the whole log, not per symbol, so a busy month can push real sells out of the window.
fix: Document that the 200 cap is global, or raise _TXN_LIMIT substantially / paginate. At minimum note in the returned dict when the cap was hit (len(txns) == _TXN_LIMIT) so callers know results may be partial.

title: Wash band uses abs(proceeds) but proceeds can be ~0 for penny/zero sell_price, classifying real moves as regret
description: band = _WASH_FRACTION * abs(proceeds) where proceeds = sell_price*shares. If sell_price rounds to a tiny value (penny stock, or bad data near 0), band ~0 so any nonzero delta is classed regret/relief even when economically a wash. Conversely a legitimately huge proceeds inflates the band. Minor but can mislabel verdicts on extreme prices.
fix: Guard: if proceeds <= 0, skip the row (can't grade). Otherwise unchanged. Add `if proceeds <= 0: continue` before computing band.

title: FIFO holding-period match counts held<0 lots toward shares but not days, skewing average
description: In holding_discipline, when held = (day - buy_day).days is negative (future-dated buy), the code skips adding to trip_days/trip_shares (good) but STILL consumes the lot (pop/decrement) and decrements remaining. The consumed shares vanish from matching entirely, which is intended, but a partially-future-dated trip can still register round_trips+=1 and feed quick_flips if other lots in the same SELL were valid — combining valid and invalid lots. More importantly trip_shares can be 0 for a fully future-dated match yet remaining was consumed, so those shares are silently dropped (acceptable), but quick_flip classification (trip_days/trip_shares) divides only over valid shares — fine. The genuine bug: round_trips counts a SELL as a round trip only if trip_shares>0, but a SELL that fully matched future-dated buys yields trip_shares==0 and is NOT counted, undercounting round_trips inconsistently with avg.
fix: This is borderline; if treating future-dated buys as bad data, exclude their shares from the match entirely (don't consume them) so remaining stays available for the next real lot, instead of silently dropping consumed shares. Move the pop/decrement inside the `if held >= 0` branch, or break out of the while when encountering a future-dated front lot.

title: SMTP starttls failure swallowed then login/sendmail proceed over plaintext, leaking credentials
description: s.starttls() is wrapped in try/except pass 'server may not support STARTTLS'. If STARTTLS fails on a server that DOES require it (or MITM strips it), the code falls through to s.login(user, password) over an unencrypted channel, transmitting credentials in cleartext. Silently downgrading TLS is a credential-exposure bug.
fix: Do not blanket-swallow starttls failures when credentials will be sent. Either require TLS (let the exception abort the send) when user/password are set, or use SMTP_SSL when configured; only tolerate missing STARTTLS for unauthenticated relays.

title: _ownership reads h['shares']/h['avg_cost'] by index, KeyError if columns absent
description: out.update with h['shares'] and h['avg_cost'] uses subscripting, not .get(). If a portfolio row lacks one of these keys, KeyError is raised; it is caught by the broad except at line 220, which discards the ENTIRE ownership dict (held flag, transactions count, first_buy) and logs at debug. A single missing field silently blanks the whole ownership panel.
fix: Use h.get('shares') and h.get('avg_cost'), and guard the unrealized_pct computation on both being present (already partially guarded). This keeps the rest of the ownership output intact when one field is missing.

title: Temperament 90-day window mixes naive local now with parsed naive day; DST/locale fine but recent_count uses 'now - d' on date-only
description: now = datetime.now() (naive local) and d = _parse_day -> datetime.fromisoformat(raw[:10]) (midnight naive). recent_count = (now - d).days <= 90 is fine, but _parse_ts parses created_at with time-of-day while _parse_day strips to midnight; the sort key (d, ts) and the flip loop use d (midnight) for 'held = (d - last_buy).days', discarding the intraday time that _parse_ts was specifically computed to preserve. Same-day BUY then SELL yields held=0 (correct), but a SELL recorded BEFORE its BUY on the same calendar day (bad ordering) is reordered by ts in the sort yet the flip math uses d only — so day-trade ordering fixed in the sort is thrown away in the comparison.
fix: In the flips loop, carry and compare ts (full timestamp) for ordering decisions, or at least keep using d for the day-count but rely on the (d,ts) sort (already done) so last_buy precedes sell. The current code is mostly consistent; ensure rows lacking ts don't reorder — consider falling back held computation to ts when both present.

title: Sector top/bottom slicing produces empty 'bottom' when top_n equals len(ranked)
description: half = len(ranked)//2; top_n = min(3, half) if len>=2 else 0. bottom = ranked[len(ranked)-top_n:]. For len(ranked)==2, half=1, top_n=1: top=ranked[:1], bottom=ranked[1:] — disjoint, OK. For len(ranked)==3, half=1, top_n=1: bottom=ranked[2:] skips the middle (intended). But for len==4..5 with half=2, top_n=2: top=ranked[:2], bottom=ranked[2:] (or ranked[3:]) — for len==4 top=[:2], bottom=[2:] => 2 each, adjacent, fine. The bug surfaces at line 583: it compares sectors_top[0] vs sectors_bottom[-1]; if top_n==0 (len<2) both lists empty and the guard `sectors_top and sectors_bottom` skips — OK. No crash, but with exactly len(ranked)==1 nothing renders even though one sector moved.
fix: Minor: when len(ranked)==1, still surface that single sector as 'leading' so a one-sector feed isn't dropped. Set top_n=min(3,max(1,half)) when len(ranked)>=1, and compute bottom only when len(ranked)>=2.

title: _norm(v) can return None, producing a rule dict with value=None that passes the None check
description: Branches return {'kind':..., 'value': _norm(v)} guarded by `if v is not None`. v comes from _pick which returns a float or None; the `if v is not None` guards that. _norm(None) is never hit because of the guard — OK. However _norm returns v unchanged for non-integer floats, and parse_rule for max_positions does int(v) only after is_integer check; the crypto/weight branches can return a fractional percent like 12.5 which is valid. No crash, but max_crypto_pct value 12.5 then passes through set_rule->_coerce_value which keeps it. Consistent. The real latent issue: parse_rule returns the dict directly to a route that may persist it WITHOUT _coerce_value range clamping, so a parsed 'crypto under 500%' (if _pick hi allowed) could persist. Here _pick hi=100 guards it.
fix: No fix needed if every persist path routes through set_rule/_coerce_value. Verify the POST route calls set_rule after parse_rule rather than saving parse_rule output directly; if it saves directly, route it through _coerce_value first.

title: check_proposal takes LAST max_single_buy_usd rule instead of unique; loop doesn't break
description: for r in get_rules(): if kind==max_single_buy_usd: cap=float(r['value']). Since _load_rules dedups to one rule per kind this is fine in practice, but the loop keeps iterating after finding the cap (no break) and unconditionally overwrites cap, so if duplicates ever slip in (hand-edited settings bypassing _load_rules dedup is prevented, but a future change) the LAST wins silently. Minor robustness.
fix: break after assigning cap, or use next((float(r['value']) for r in get_rules() if r.get('kind')=='max_single_buy_usd'), None).

title: max_crypto_pct sums weight_pct without rejecting bool/None consistently with max_weight check
description: csum = sum(h.get('weight_pct') or 0 for h in holdings if h.get('asset_type')=='crypto'). Unlike the max_weight_pct check (line 335) which guards `isinstance(w,(int,float)) and not isinstance(w,bool)`, this sum uses `or 0` so a weight_pct of True (bool, int subclass) would add 1, and a string weight_pct raises TypeError in sum (caught by the surrounding try, suppressing the whole crypto check). Inconsistent guarding.
fix: csum = sum(w for h in holdings if h.get('asset_type')=='crypto' for w in [h.get('weight_pct')] if isinstance(w,(int,float)) and not isinstance(w,bool)) — mirror the weight-check coercion so a malformed row doesn't zero or crash the crypto total.

title: OpenAI Responses API web_search call not routed through the shared governor/retry
description: _web_research_uncached creates its own OpenAI client and calls client.responses.create directly, bypassing ai_summarizer.governed_call. Under concurrent Jarvis usage this can self-inflict 429s that the rest of the app's calls are protected from, and there's no retry/backoff. It also doesn't respect _uses_reasoning_params concerns, but more importantly it ignores the process-wide RPM pacer.
fix: Wrap the create call: resp = ai_summarizer.governed_call(lambda: client.responses.create(...)) so it shares the concurrency cap and cooperative backoff.

title: news_sentiment trend uses first/last raw points, not chronologically ordered; GDELT order assumption
description: trend = 'improving' if vals[-1] > vals[0] else 'deteriorating'. This assumes series is chronological ascending. If gdelt_tone_timeline returns newest-first (as many feeds do), the trend is inverted (reports 'improving' when actually deteriorating). Also a flat series (vals[-1]==vals[0]) is reported as 'deteriorating' rather than flat/None.
fix: Sort series by its date/timestamp field before extracting vals, and use a 3-way compare: trend = 'improving' if last>first else ('deteriorating' if last<first else 'flat'). Confirm GDELT ordering and document it.

title: recall() reads DB outside the write lock while writers hold it; SQLite may raise 'database is locked'
description: recall does db.get_conn().execute(sql,...).fetchall() with no lock. If another thread is mid-write under db._write_lock on the same connection (shared connection), a concurrent read on that connection can raise 'cannot operate on a closed/locked' or return inconsistent cursor state. Reads are generally fine with separate connections, but the module's own writers (store/forget) use the SAME db.get_conn(); a cursor in use by a write and a read simultaneously on one sqlite3.Connection is not threadsafe.
fix: Either use a dedicated read connection, or take db._write_lock (or a read lock) around the SELECT, consistent with how the rest of database.py serializes access to the shared connection.

title: embed() records AI call only after validating length but maps by item.index which may exceed len
description: After resp.data length check, out[item.index] = list(item.embedding). If the API ever returns an index >= len(texts) (malformed), this raises IndexError inside the try and the whole batch returns failed — acceptable. But the more subtle bug: the length check `len(resp.data) != len(texts)` returns failed BEFORE _record_ai_call(), so a partial/over-length response is treated as zero cost even though the paid call was made — the daily counter under-counts real spend, defeating the cap.
fix: Call _record_ai_call() as soon as a response is received (the request was billed regardless of shape), before the length validation, then proceed with validation/return-failed.

title: Cosine normalization broadcasts query-norm into per-row norms incorrectly when q-norm is 0
description: norms = np.linalg.norm(mat, axis=1) * (np.linalg.norm(q) or 1.0). If q is a zero vector, np.linalg.norm(q)=0.0 which is falsy so `or 1.0` substitutes 1.0 — but then scores = (mat @ q)/norms = 0/norms = 0 everywhere, returning no recall (acceptable). However if a stored row vector is zero, norms[that]=0 then set to 1.0, and mat@q for that row is 0, score 0 — fine. The real issue: `np.linalg.norm(q) or 1.0` evaluates the truthiness of a numpy float scalar; for a NaN q-norm (NaN is truthy) it stays NaN and propagates NaN into every score, and np.argsort on NaN gives undefined order; MIN_SCORE comparison with NaN is always False so recall returns [] silently — but only because the break never triggers and len(out) cap... actually s<MIN_SCORE is False for NaN so it appends junk.
fix: Guard q explicitly: qn = float(np.linalg.norm(q)); if not np.isfinite(qn) or qn==0: return []. And use np.nan_to_num(scores) or filter NaN before argsort.

title: stress_test uses h["asset_type"] which can KeyError
description: Lines 267-268 filter holdings with `h["asset_type"] != "crypto"` using hard subscripts, but elsewhere the codebase consistently uses h.get("asset_type"). A holding row missing asset_type raises KeyError and the stress test returns an error instead of a result.
fix: Use h.get("asset_type") in both the syms and crypto comprehensions, matching the rest of the module.

title: recent_transactions limit of 0 silently becomes 10
description: `n = _num_arg(args.get("limit")); n = int(max(1,min(n,25))) if n else 10`. When the model passes limit=0, `if n` is False (0 is falsy) so it falls to default 10 rather than being clamped to 1. Minor, but a requested limit of 0 unexpectedly returns 10 rows. More importantly _num_arg can return a float; min(n,25) compares fine but the `if n` test treats 0.0 as falsy too.
fix: Test against None explicitly: `n = int(max(1, min(n, 25))) if n is not None else 10`.

title: price_history days=0 falls back to default instead of clamping
description: `n=_num_arg(args.get("days")); days=int(max(5,min(n,365))) if n else 30`. days=0 (falsy) yields default 30 rather than the clamp floor 5. The same falsy-vs-None mistake. Not a crash but produces a window different from what the user/model asked for.
fix: Use `if n is not None else 30`.

title: top_detractors slices attrib[-3:] from a list sorted descending by contribution
description: attribution() top_contributors uses attrib[:5] (largest first), implying attrib is sorted descending by total. top_detractors then takes attrib[-3:] and filters total<0. But [-3:] of a descending list are the THREE LOWEST (most negative) — correct only if attribution() is sorted descending. If attribution() returns ascending or unsorted order, detractors will be wrong. This is an undocumented ordering dependency that silently produces wrong detractors if attribution()'s sort changes.
fix: Sort explicitly in the tool: `worst = sorted(attrib, key=lambda a: a.get('total',0))[:3]` and filter total<0, rather than relying on attribution()'s internal ordering.

title: List truncation can produce an empty items list for a single huge element
description: In execute_read, when result is a list, `while trimmed and len(json.dumps(trimmed))>budget-60: trimmed.pop()` will pop until empty if even one element exceeds the budget. It can return {"items": [], "truncated": True} losing all data, when a better outcome is to keep one element truncated. Edge case but drops all content for a single oversized row.
fix: After the while loop, if `not trimmed and result`, keep result[:1] and stringify/truncate that single element instead of returning an empty list.

title: benchmark_compare bench return uses unaligned bars[0] when alignment fails
description: In _t_benchmark_compare, bars are aligned to the first snapshot date only if `len(aligned)>=2`; otherwise the full-period bars are used. bench_ret then computes from bars[0]..bars[-1]. If alignment failed (e.g. snapshots start late), the benchmark return covers a LONGER period than the portfolio return, making excess_return_pct an apples-to-oranges comparison — exactly the bug the alignment comment claims to fix, but it silently falls back to the misaligned full window.
fix: When alignment yields <2 bars, set bench_ret=None (don't compute excess) rather than silently comparing mismatched windows.

title: _num_arg strips % and $ and commas, silently accepting malformed money like '$1$2,,3'
description: _num_arg does `float(str(v).replace('%','').replace(',','').replace('$',''))`. Inputs like '50%' for a share count, or '$1,000' for shares, are accepted as 50 and 1000 respectively. For shares/price coercion this means '30%' passed as a price becomes 30 dollars silently, and a model passing '20%' for shares yields 20 shares — masking unit confusion that should be rejected.
fix: For shares/price specifically, reject inputs containing '%' rather than stripping it; keep the lenient strip only where a magnitude is genuinely expected (e.g. custom_drop_pct).

title: what_if add/resize requires 0<mv<100M but _num_arg(...) or 0 turns a valid 0 or None into 0 then rejects
description: `mv=_num_arg(args.get('market_value')) or 0; if not (0<mv<100_000_000): raise`. A legitimate request to resize a position TO $0 (effectively remove) is rejected with a confusing 'market_value required' error, and any _num_arg returning 0.0 (e.g. value '0') is indistinguishable from missing. The `or 0` also masks None.
fix: Distinguish None (missing → error) from 0 (explicit, possibly valid for resize_to), and tailor the message.

title: valid_proposal_args allows price==0 for add_holding (a free buy) which then logs a $0 cost basis
description: For add_holding the price guard is `0 <= price < 10M`, permitting price=0. _t_add_holding then records a position with avg_cost=0 and a BUY at $0, producing a zero cost basis that makes unrealized_pct division-by-zero-guarded but yields a 0% or skipped P&L and corrupts cost-basis analytics. record_trade at $0 is arguably valid (transfer), but add_holding at $0 cost basis is almost always a model error.
fix: For add_holding require price>0 (keep >=0 only for record_trade), so a zero-cost holding can't be silently created.

title: macro_snapshot CPI YoY divides by pts[-13]['value'] guarded by truthiness, but pts[-1]['value'] may be None
description: entry={'value': pts[-1]['value']...}; YoY uses pts[-1]['value']/pts[-13]['value']. The denominator is guarded by `pts[-13].get('value')` truthiness, but the NUMERATOR pts[-1]['value'] is not checked for None; if the latest observation value is None, the division raises TypeError (caught by the per-series except, dropping CPI entirely — but also the base 'value' entry would be None and pass through to the LLM as a null CPI).
fix: Validate pts[-1]['value'] is a number before computing YoY and before emitting the entry; skip the series if the latest value is None.

title: benchmark_compare port_ret divides by first['total_value'] without checking it is nonzero
description: `port_ret=round((float(last['total_value'])/float(first['total_value'])-1)*100,2)`. The window filter requires `s.get('total_value')` truthy, so first['total_value'] is truthy → nonzero. OK for 0, but a NEGATIVE or near-zero total_value (bad snapshot) yields an absurd return. Also float() on a non-numeric total_value raises, aborting the tool (no try/except around this division).
fix: Validate first/last total_value are positive numbers (via _num_arg) before dividing; return a note on bad data.

title: liquidity cache dicts mutated without a lock
description: _cached_get/_cached_set access shared `_cache`/`_cache_ts` without synchronization. compute_stress_score is cached under a single key but can be invoked concurrently (dashboard + warmer), and the read in compute_stress_score and write in _compute_stress_score_inner are unsynchronized check-then-act.
fix: Guard the module cache with a threading.Lock.

title: _rf_predict rebuilds full feature frame a second time unnecessarily (perf/correctness)
description: _rf_predict calls _build_features(hist) at line 136 then again at line 158 (df_full) solely to grab the latest row's features. The first df already contains the same feature columns for the latest row (it was only dropna'd into a new variable, hist is unchanged). Recomputing all rolling features/RF inputs doubles the feature-engineering cost on the hot path and, if _build_features ever becomes non-deterministic or hist is large, wastes time; it also risks subtle divergence if the two computations differ.
fix: Reuse the first computation: take the latest features from the original (pre-dropna) df via `_build_features(hist)[0][feature_cols].iloc[-1:]` once, or capture df_full = df before the train dropna. Avoid the second _build_features call.

title: Composite weight normalization double-counts when a signal is absent
description: weights = {RF:0.50, Trend:0.30, MR:0.20}; total_w = sum of weights for present signals; composite = sum(p*weight)/total_w. That is correct. However weights.get(s[0], 0.2) is used for BOTH total and numerator, so an unknown signal name (shouldn't happen) gets 0.2. Real issue: when only Trend+MR are present (RF None), total_w=0.5 and the composite is a 0.6/0.4 blend of Trend/MR — fine. But composite_signal thresholds (0.70/0.58/0.42/0.30) were calibrated assuming RF dominates; with RF absent the same thresholds are applied to a Trend/MR-only blend, mislabeling STRONG BUY/SELL on weaker evidence. Not a crash but a calibration regression when RF is unavailable.
fix: Either require RF for STRONG labels, or widen/neutralize thresholds when RF is missing (e.g. clamp composite_signal to at most BUY/SELL, never STRONG, when 'RF' not in [s[0] for s in signals]).

title: narrative cache dicts mutated without a lock
description: _cache/_cache_ts are read in analyze_narrative (check-then-return) and written at the end with no synchronization. Concurrent /api/narrative calls for the same symbol both compute and write; with many symbols the unsynchronized dict mutation risks torn state, and there's no in-flight coalescing so duplicate news fetches occur.
fix: Guard cache access with a threading.Lock (and optionally coalesce in-flight computations).

title: Reduced smart_money rescale divides by kept_max which can be 0 when components present but lack 'max', handled but kept_score/0 guard only on kept_max truthiness
description: `sm_score = round(kept_score/kept_max*100) if kept_max else sm_score`. kept_max = sum of components[k]['score'... wait 'max']. If the three kept components exist but report max=0 each, kept_max=0 → falls back to sm_score (the full composite) — which REINTRODUCES the double-counting the whole block was meant to remove. So on data where institutional/options/sec maxes are zero, the de-overlap fix silently no-ops and smart_money is double counted.
fix: When kept_max is 0 (can't isolate non-overlapping components), set sm_score to neutral 50 rather than the full composite, to avoid re-double-counting the overlapping signals.

title: Smart-money error branch writes details score 0 but result['scores']['smart_money'] later set from sm_score=50 default — detail/score divergence
description: On smart_money error, details['smart_money']={'score':0,...} but the scoring variable sm_score stays at its 50 neutral default (S4 fix), so the composite uses 50 while the UI detail shows 0. Inconsistent display vs scoring; the detail implies max-bearish while the composite treats it neutral.
fix: Set the error-branch detail score to the same neutral value used for scoring (50), or omit the numeric score, so detail and composite agree.

title: _parse_date_loose returns datetime.min (naive) compared against cutoff_30d_dt (naive ET) — works, but recent_cong uses t['txn_date'] direct index after a get check
description: `recent_cong = [t for t in buys if t.get('txn_date','') and _parse_date_loose(t['txn_date']) >= cutoff_30d_dt]`. _parse_date_loose returns datetime.min on unparseable, which is < cutoff so excluded (ok). cutoff_30d_dt is naive ET; datetime.min naive — comparable. No crash. But if txn_date is a non-string (e.g. a datetime already), strptime raises TypeError caught → datetime.min, silently dropping valid recent buys. Low severity.
fix: Have _parse_date_loose accept datetime/date inputs (return as-is) so already-parsed dates aren't coerced to datetime.min and dropped.

title: Module-global _scan_cache / _scan_cache_time mutated and read without a lock under parallel scans
description: scan_opportunities reads/writes _scan_cache[phash] and _scan_cache_time[phash] with no lock; concurrent requests with the same profile (or get_cached_scan racing scan_opportunities) can read a half-updated cache entry. Also it mutates result['scan_meta']['cached']=True on the SHARED cached dict object, so a cached read flips the stored object's flag for all subsequent readers and even the persisted copy.
fix: Guard cache access with a threading.Lock, and return a shallow copy (with 'cached' set on the copy) instead of mutating the shared cached result dict in place.

title: reflexivity cache dicts mutated without a lock
description: _get_cached/_set_cached touch shared `_cache`/`_cache_ts` with no lock; the eviction loop iterates `_cache_ts.items()` while other threads may write, risking RuntimeError under concurrent detect_loops calls.
fix: Add a threading.Lock around all cache access; snapshot keys before the eviction iteration.

title: Short-squeeze uses short_pct>0.15 assuming a fraction, but fetcher may supply a percent
description: _detect_short_squeeze treats `short_percent_float` as a fraction (>0.15 means 15%) and the detail multiplies by 100 (short_pct*100). If fetcher.get_fundamentals returns short interest as a whole percent (e.g. 15.0), the >0.15 test is trivially true for any non-trivial short interest and the detail prints 1500%. The unit must match fetcher's convention; a mismatch silently mis-detects squeezes everywhere.
fix: Normalize at the boundary: `if short_pct is not None and short_pct>1: short_pct/=100.0` before the comparisons, matching the *100 display assumption.

title: Signal-list dedup by issued_at can collapse distinct same-day signals
description: When trimming >200 signals, merged is keyed only by s['issued_at'] (a YYYY-MM-DD date). Two different signals can legitimately share the same issued_at date (the recent-100 and the extreme-100 sets overlap, and a single day may carry multiple entries if horizon logic ever emits more than one). Keying solely on the date silently drops one, undercounting the merged set and producing a non-deterministic surviving entry depending on iteration order.
fix: Key the merge on a unique tuple, e.g. `(s['issued_at'], s['direction'], s['exit_date'])`, or just dedup by object identity using a set of ids; this preserves all distinct signals while still removing the true duplicates from recent+extreme overlap.

title: adapter_ml_forecast module cache (_ML_FORECAST_CACHE) never invalidated and shared across backtests
description: _ML_FORECAST_CACHE is a module-global dict keyed only by symbol, populated on first call and never cleared. Across different backtest runs (different date windows/params) for the same symbol the SAME stale ml_forecast result is reused for the lifetime of the process, even though ml_forecast itself has a 1h TTL. A long-running server will keep using a forecast computed hours/days earlier, and concurrent backtests race on this unlocked dict.
fix: Drop the module-global cache and rely on ml_forecast's own TTL cache (call ml_forecast each time — it's cached internally), or add a timestamp/TTL and a lock to _ML_FORECAST_CACHE so it expires and is thread-safe.

title: avg_abs_event_move uses post-event window end, contradicting its T0-1..T+5 intent
description: The comment says average the absolute per-episode move from just-before-event (T0-1) through T+5. base_idx is correctly t0-1, but per_episode_total uses curves[:, post_idx] where post_idx = min(t0+5, ncols-1). For the default window_days=10 that is fine, but for small windows where window_days<5, post_idx is clamped to the last column, so the 'T+5' magnitude is actually measured over fewer days than intended, understating/altering the magnitude. More importantly the variable named avg_abs_event_move conflates the whole post window; acceptable but the clamp silently changes the horizon without flagging.
fix: Guard the window: compute the intended post offset and skip/flag avg_abs_move when window_days<5 rather than silently clamping, e.g. `if t0 + 5 <= curves.shape[1]-1: post_idx = t0+5 else: avg_abs_move=None`. At minimum document that small windows shorten the measured horizon.

title: Stock return dates derived in UTC can misalign with French factor calendar dates
description: _stock_log_returns converts bar epoch times with datetime.fromtimestamp(int(t), tz=timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d'). Yahoo daily bar timestamps are typically midnight in the exchange/local timezone; interpreting them as UTC can shift a bar to the previous/next calendar day for non-UTC exchanges or DST boundaries. The regression then inner-joins these date strings against the French calendar (which is exchange-local trading dates), dropping or mis-pairing rows and biasing alpha/betas. event/montecarlo modules normalise/tz-localize before date-stringifying; this one does not.
fix: Normalise to the bar's date the same way the other modules do, e.g. use pd.to_datetime(t, unit='s').normalize() / .date() without forcing UTC, or .dt.tz_localize(None).dt.normalize(), so the date label matches the trading-day calendar used by the factor frame.

title: French CSV parser silently miscounts columns when a row has missing trailing fields
description: _parse_french_csv builds vals = [float(parts[i+1])/100 for i in range(len(value_cols))]. If a daily row is truncated (fewer columns than expected, which happens in some French files for the most recent provisional rows), parts[i+1] raises IndexError caught by the except and the row is skipped — acceptable. But for the RF column ordering: ff5 is parsed with value_cols=[Mkt-RF,SMB,HML,RMW,CMA,RF] meaning RF is parts[6]; _merge_frames unpacks `mkt,smb,hml,rmw,cma,r = ff5[d]` — correct. The momentum file is parsed with one value col; if French ever appends a second column the (m,) = mom[d] unpacking at line 158 raises ValueError, not caught, crashing _merge_frames and the whole factor load.
fix: Make the unpack defensive: `m = mom[d][0]` instead of `(m,) = mom[d]`, so an extra momentum column doesn't raise and abort the merge.

title: sqlite connections opened per call via `with _conn()` but row_factory connections not pooled; many short-lived WAL handles
description: Every public function opens a fresh sqlite3.connect via _conn() inside a `with` block. While `with conn:` commits/rolls back the transaction, it does NOT close the connection — sqlite3's context manager only manages the transaction, not the handle. So each call leaks an open connection until GC. Under the warmer/score loop this accrues file handles on wealth.db (contrast research_tracker which pools a thread-local connection).
fix: Wrap in `with closing(_conn()) as c:` (from contextlib) or explicitly c.close() in a finally, so connections are closed deterministically. Or adopt the thread-local pooling pattern used in research_tracker.py.

title: _clean_calls accepts NaN bid/ask producing NaN mid that propagates into density
description: mid is computed when `bid is not None and ask is not None and ask >= bid and (bid+ask)>0`. yfinance frequently returns float('nan') for bid/ask (not None). NaN passes the `is not None` checks; `ask >= bid` is False for NaN so it usually falls through to lastPrice, but if last is also NaN, `last > 0` is False and the row is dropped — OK. However when bid/ask are NaN the comparison `ask >= bid` is False so mid stays None and the elif may set mid=NaN only if last>0. The real gap: there is no math.isfinite check on bid/ask/last, so a NaN lastPrice>0 is False (safe) but a NaN bid with finite ask passes (bid+ask) is NaN, (NaN)>0 False, falls through — generally safe, yet a finite bid with NaN ask yields ask>=bid False, falls through. Net: rows with NaN quotes are silently dropped rather than using available data, and no explicit finite guard exists, risking NaN leakage if yfinance shape changes.
fix: Add explicit finite coercion at the top: `bid = bid if (bid is not None and math.isfinite(float(bid))) else None` (same for ask/last) before the mid logic, so NaN can never reach the (bid+ask) arithmetic and mid is always finite or the row is dropped deterministically.

title: Density renormalization divides by integral that can be ~0, leaving an all-zero density
description: After flooring negatives, total = np.trapz(density, grid); only if total>1e-12 is density divided. When the second-derivative is non-positive everywhere (e.g. heavy no-arb violations after monotonic clamp flatten C), density is all zeros, total≈0, and the function returns an all-zero density and a flat (all-zero) CDF. _prob_above then returns values from a degenerate CDF and _moments returns all None, but the top-level _compute still emits probabilities computed from a meaningless flat CDF (every p_above interpolates to 0/constant) without surfacing an error.
fix: After computing total, if total <= 1e-12 return an error envelope (e.g. _error(sym, 'Degenerate density (no usable curvature)')) instead of proceeding with an all-zero density that yields misleading probabilities.

title: prob_touch ignores the running path within a step; uses simple any() over discrete daily NAVs
description: prob_touch is computed as (paths >= target).any(axis=1) on the simulated daily NAVs. For DOWN targets it uses <=. This is correct in spirit but the per-step NAV is the compounded value at each day only; intraday/inter-step crossings are not modeled, so prob_touch can understate the true touch probability — this is acceptable for a daily model but the field is named/returned as prob_touch_target without that caveat, and for very short horizons (horizon_days=1) prob_touch collapses to prob_term, which the Normal-fallback branch already does. Not a crash but a correctness caveat that downstream may treat as exact.
fix: Document that prob_touch is a discrete-daily approximation, and for the empty/failed-sim fallback (where prob_touch is set equal to prob_term) explicitly mark prob_touch as approximate in the payload so consumers don't treat it as exact.

title: Weight vector uses mv_by_sym.get(s,0.0) keyed by kept column names that may not match surviving symbols
description: weights built as mv_by_sym.get(s,0.0)/surviving_mv for s in kept, where kept = df column names from _build_returns_matrix. Columns are set to symbol.upper() in _fetch_returns (rets.name=symbol.upper()), and surviving symbols come from clean (already uppercased in _clean_holdings). These should match, but _build_returns_matrix can also append symbols to `dropped` as str(series[i].name) and the kept list is str(df.columns). If any symbol contains characters altered by pandas column coercion (e.g. duplicate names), get() silently yields 0.0 weight for that asset, dropping it from the portfolio without it appearing in dropped_symbols.
fix: After building weights, assert weights.sum()>0 and that every kept symbol resolved to a positive mv; if a kept symbol maps to 0.0 weight, add it to dropped_symbols and renormalize, so silent weight loss is surfaced.

title: ROC computations index iloc[-6]/-21/-61 without verifying enough non-NaN bars after dropna mismatch
description: _h5 uses close.iloc[-6] guarded by len(close)>6, _h20_fallback uses close.iloc[-21] guarded by len>=21, _h60 uses close.iloc[-61] guarded by len>=61. These guards use raw close length, but close may contain leading rows; fine. The real edge: roc5 guard is `len(close) > 6` yet accesses iloc[-6] which needs len>=6, off by potential confusion but safe. However vol60 fallback `vol5 or 0.01` (line 113) returns 0.01 when vol5 is exactly 0.0 (flat 5-day window) — vol5==0.0 is falsy so vol60 becomes 0.01 even if 60-day vol was computable; this distorts vol_ratio.
fix: Use explicit None/finite checks instead of truthiness for vol fallbacks: `vol60 = float(rets.iloc[-60:].std()) if len(rets) >= 60 else (vol5 if vol5 > 0 else 0.01)`, so a genuinely-zero short vol doesn't force the 0.01 default and skew vol_ratio.

title: risk_parity uses res.x even when optimizer did not converge without zero-guarding NaNs
description: w = np.array(res.x if res.success else w0). If SLSQP diverges, res.x can contain NaN/inf; the code then does np.where(w<0,0,w) (NaN<0 is False so NaN survives) and w/w.sum() (sum NaN), yielding an all-NaN weight vector that propagates into expected_return_pct/vol/sharpe and the JSON response.
fix: Sanitize before normalizing: `w = np.where(np.isfinite(w), w, 0.0)` and if w.sum()<=EPS fall back to equal weights, mirroring the black_litterman fallback at line 510-511.

title: black_litterman market caps looked up by `used` (upper) but mkt_caps keys may be original case
description: caps = np.array([float(mkt_caps.get(s,0.0)) for s in used]) where used contains uppercased symbols. If the caller passes mkt_caps keyed by the original (possibly lowercase) symbols, every lookup returns 0.0, caps.sum()==0, and the code silently falls back to equal market weights — discarding the user's supplied caps and the entire BL prior basis without warning.
fix: Normalize mkt_caps keys to upper when reading: build `caps_norm = {k.upper(): v for k,v in mkt_caps.items()}` and look up caps_norm.get(s,0.0); same for views' symbols (already .upper()'d there).

title: Block bootstrap truncation biases toward early days of each block when horizon not a block multiple
description: n_blocks = ceil(horizon/block_size); idx reshaped to (n, n_blocks*block_size)[:, :horizon]. The final block is truncated to fit horizon_days. This always keeps the FIRST (horizon mod block_size) returns of the last sampled block and discards its tail, so the last-block contribution is systematically the opening days of a 5-day window. Over many paths this slightly biases the horizon-return distribution if intra-block autocorrelation differs between early/late block positions. Minor statistical bias, but it is a real deviation from a clean stationary-block bootstrap.
fix: Acceptable approximation, but to remove the bias choose the number of blocks so total length >= horizon and randomly offset the truncation, or use the Politis-Romano geometric block length; at minimum document the truncation bias.

title: Trading-to-calendar horizon conversion ignores holidays, still scores early on long horizons
description: horizon_cal = ceil(h*7/5) converts trading days to calendar days assuming exactly 5 trading days per 7 calendar days. Over long horizons this accumulates error from market holidays (~9/yr): a 252-trading-day horizon maps to ceil(252*7/5)=353 calendar days, but 252 trading days is ~366 calendar days including holidays, so the close is still read ~13 days early. For shorter horizons the rounding is roughly fine, but the systematic early-read on long horizons biases realized returns.
fix: Add a small holiday cushion proportional to horizon, e.g. horizon_cal = ceil(h*7/5) + ceil(h/63)*1, or score against the actual trading-day-indexed bar by counting bars rather than calendar-day arithmetic (find the bar that is h trading days after the issue bar).

title: Candidate rows read outside the write lock; UPDATE guarded only by scored_at IS NULL but commit on shared connection
description: score_due_forecasts reads candidate rows with the thread-local connection outside _write_lock, then per-row acquires _write_lock and updates with `WHERE id=? AND scored_at IS NULL`. The guard prevents double-scoring across processes, but `_get_conn()` returns a thread-local connection; within the same process two threads each have their own connection and the WAL UPDATE+commit interleave fine due to the WHERE guard. However scored counter increments unconditionally after execute even if rowcount==0 (another thread already scored it), overcounting 'scored'. cur.rowcount is not checked.
fix: Check the UPDATE result: `cur = _get_conn().execute(...)`; only `scored += 1` when `cur.rowcount > 0`, else treat as already-scored and skip (don't count as error or scored).

title: get_recent_filings can return fewer than `limit` filings
description: The loop iterates all forms and breaks only when `len(results) >= limit`. That's correct for the cap, but the early-continue on `form_type not in forms` is fine; however the `limit` check happens AFTER appending so it can append one extra past limit only if checked before append — here it's checked at top so OK. The real issue: filings are taken in EDGAR submission order (already newest-first) which is fine, but there is no guard that `accessions`/`primary_docs` arrays are equal length to `form_types`; a malformed `recent` block with shorter parallel arrays silently yields '' fields. Index access is bounds-guarded, so the risk is degraded (empty) rows rather than a crash.
fix: Low priority: after building, drop rows with empty accession; or log when parallel arrays differ in length. (No behavior change required for the cap itself.)

title: Reflexivity proximity/timeline read wrong keys
description: _make_loop_result emits `proximity_to_trigger_pct` and `acceleration_timeline`. The JS reads `loop.proximity` and `loop.timeline`, so even a detected loop always shows Proximity '—' and Timeline '—'.
fix: Read `loop.proximity_to_trigger_pct` and `loop.acceleration_timeline` (with the existing fallbacks).

title: Reflexivity fundamentals snapshot reads wrong key
description: detect_loops() returns `fundamentals_snapshot`; the JS reads `data.fundamentals`, so the FUNDAMENTALS SNAPSHOT panel never renders.
fix: Read `data.fundamentals_snapshot || {}`.

title: GEX dealer-hedge estimates never render (dict vs array, wrong key)
description: compute_gex() returns `dealer_hedge_estimates` as a dict keyed by move label ('+1%', '-1%', ...). The JS reads `g.dealer_hedges || g.hedge_estimates` (neither key exists) and checks `.length`, so the DEALER HEDGE ESTIMATES table never renders.
fix: Read `g.dealer_hedge_estimates` and iterate its entries: `Object.entries(g.dealer_hedge_estimates||{}).map(([move,v])=>({move, price:v.price, delta_shares:v.delta_shares}))`.

title: Narrative phase reads wrong key (always UNKNOWN)
description: analyze_narrative() returns the phase under `narrative_phase`; the JS reads `data.phase`, so the Phase KPI always falls back to 'UNKNOWN' and never colorizes EMERGENCE/CONSENSUS/etc.
fix: Read `data.narrative_phase || data.phase || 'UNKNOWN'`.

title: Liquidity position-sizing and indicators table read wrong shapes
description: compute_stress_score() returns `position_sizing_multiplier` (not `position_sizing`) and `indicators` as a dict keyed by indicator name (not a list). The JS reads `data.position_sizing` (always '—') and `if (indicators.length)` on a dict (always falsy), so the STRESS INDICATORS table never renders.
fix: Read `data.position_sizing_multiplier`; build the indicator rows from `Object.entries(data.indicators||{}).map(([k,v])=>Object.assign({indicator:k}, v))`.

title: _raw_value returns 0..1 but is rounded/exposed without bounds; division by max can divide by 0 silently None-guarded but score can exceed max
description: _raw_value computes score/max with no clamp; if a component reports score>max (possible for ML components) raw_value exceeds 1.0 and is surfaced as a 'strength'. Minor, but _normalize_component clamps while _raw_value does not, producing inconsistent UI values.
fix: Clamp the return of _raw_value to [0,1]: `return max(0.0, min(1.0, float(score)/float(max_)))` inside the try.

title: Track-record gate uses n_directional for threshold but hit_rate may correspond to a different n
description: Stage 1 reads n_dir=tr.get('n_directional') and hit_rate=tr.get('hit_rate'), then if n_dir>=MIN_N and hit_rate is not None calls _posterior_mean(int(n_dir), float(hit_rate)). If the tracker's hit_rate is computed over a different/last-100 window than n_directional, hits=round(hit_rate*n_dir) misattributes counts. Not a crash but can skew weights. Lower severity.
fix: Use the tracker's own hit/miss counts if exposed (e.g. n_hits) instead of reconstructing hits=round(hit_rate*n) from a possibly-mismatched n; otherwise document and keep, but guard hit_rate into [0,1] before multiplying.

title: yfinance earnings_dates 'Reported EPS' NaN filter via .isna() can raise if column dtype is object/missing handled but index tz-compare risk
description: _upcoming_earnings_for iterates future.index and calls _to_date(idx). earnings_dates index is a tz-aware DatetimeIndex; _to_date handles datetime via .date(), fine. But `ed[ed['Reported EPS'].isna()]` assumes 'Reported EPS' is numeric; if yfinance returns it as object with strings, isna works, but the broader risk is none. Real issue: the whole earnings_dates branch is wrapped so it degrades; low severity.
fix: No change needed beyond the existing try/except; optionally coerce with pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce') before isna().

title: FOMC/OPEX events generated for every symbol including ETFs/indices, duplicating market-wide events N times
description: has_equity = bool(symbols); then for every FOMC and OPEX date the code appends an event for EVERY symbol, so a 25-name book yields 25 identical FOMC rows and 25 identical OPEX rows per date — the implied-move/historical overlay is per-symbol so they differ, but for an index like SPY appearing alongside its components this multiplies near-identical market events. Not a crash but bloats output and cost; intended? The docstring implies per-symbol FOMC overlay so likely intended. Flagging the OPEX case: OPEX is a market-wide index expiry yet implied_move/historical are pulled per single-name symbol, which is meaningless for non-index names.
fix: For opex/fomc, either compute the implied move once off SPY (with a note) or skip per-symbol historical overlay for market-wide events; at minimum dedupe so the same (date,type) market event isn't emitted once per holding.

title: Breadth bonus uses n_fired count including timed-out/None slots already filled as fired=False (ok) but composite can mislead when weights missing
description: _finalize_scan computes weighted = sum(SOURCE_WEIGHTS.get(s['name'],0) for fired). If a source name isn't in SOURCE_WEIGHTS it contributes 0 weight but still increments n_fired (used in the breadth bonus), so a fired source with no weight inflates the bonus without contributing base. All current names are in SOURCE_WEIGHTS, so latent; flag as fragility.
fix: Either assert COMPONENTS names ⊆ SOURCE_WEIGHTS keys at import, or count n_fired only over sources that have a weight, to keep base and bonus consistent.

title: Naive UTC cutoff compared against strptime of naive local-format insider/congress dates (tz/day drift)
description: _component_insider_form4 builds cutoff = utcnow().replace(tzinfo=None) - 30d and compares to datetime.strptime(date[:10],'%Y-%m-%d') (also naive). Form-4 dates are filing dates in ET; using a UTC-derived cutoff can drift the window boundary by up to a day near midnight. Same pattern in _component_congress_60d. Minor correctness, not a crash.
fix: Anchor cutoff to ET wall-clock (as opportunity_scanner._now_et does) rather than UTC, so the 30/60-day window matches the date strings' calendar.

title: reflexivity loop variable shadows builtin-ish 'lp' fine, but direction-less loops never classified yet 'detected' non-empty → sample may pick opposite-direction loop
description: When detected loops exist but none match the requested direction, fired=False yet `sample = detected[0]` is still used to render loop_type/strength — so a bearish scan can display a bullish loop's type as the 'value', confusing the UI. Not a crash.
fix: When fired is False, set sample to {} (or omit type/strength) so the displayed value matches the (non-)firing for the requested direction.

title: Congress txn_dt string parsed with wrong date format, silently never filters
description: _c_congress filters trades older than 60d. When txn_dt is a string it parses with strptime(dt, '%Y-%m-%d'). But congress.py emits txn_date as '%m/%d/%Y' (per the sibling modules synth_cluster line 194 which uses '%m/%d/%Y' and idea_generator which reads txn_date). So a '%Y-%m-%d' parse of a '06/26/2026' string raises ValueError, the except passes, and the trade is NOT filtered by date — stale trades beyond 60 days leak into the net calculation.
fix: Try the actual congress date format(s): parse with '%m/%d/%Y' first (and fall back to '%Y-%m-%d'); on the parsed date apply the `< cutoff: continue` filter. Match the format used in synth_cluster._component_congress_60d.

title: Congress date filter only continues on string-parsed dt but not when parse fails; mixes filtered/unfiltered
description: In _c_congress, when dt is a datetime older than cutoff it continues; when dt is a string it parses '%Y-%m-%d' and continues if old. But congress emits '%m/%d/%Y' strings, so the parse raises, except passes, and the trade is counted regardless of age — stale trades pollute the 60d net. Same root cause as the txn_dt format bug.
fix: Parse the string date with '%m/%d/%Y' (the format congress.py actually emits) and apply the cutoff; fall back to '%Y-%m-%d'.

title: realized_return multiplied by 100 assuming decimal, but tracker rows may already store percent
description: _find_analogs does realized_pct = float(realized)*100.0. The seed_synthetic_history in synth_bayessmart writes realized_return as a decimal (0.02), so *100 is correct there; but if research_tracker scores rows in percent units elsewhere, this double-scales. Cross-module unit assumption with no validation. Lower confidence without the tracker source.
fix: Confirm research_tracker's realized_return unit; if it can be either, normalize (e.g. if abs(value)>1.5 treat as already-percent). At minimum document the decimal assumption.

title: sqlite connections opened with check_same_thread=False and used via context manager that commits but does not close
description: _conn() returns a connection; callers use `with _conn() as c:`. For sqlite3, `with conn` is a transaction context manager — it commits/rolls back but does NOT close the connection. _ensure_pattern_column, _load_candidate_rows, attach_pattern_to_forecast each open a fresh connection and never call .close(), leaking a connection/file handle per call. Over many grounded_hypothesis calls this accumulates open handles.
fix: Wrap in `with contextlib.closing(_conn()) as c:` (or add explicit c.close() in a finally), so each short-lived connection is closed after use.

title: _pattern_col_checked latched True only inside the 'column missing' branch path, not when column already exists in some flows
description: In _ensure_pattern_column, `_pattern_col_checked = True` is set inside the `if row is not None:` block after the cols check — so it IS set when the table exists. But if the ALTER raises a non-OperationalError it won't latch and will re-run each call (acceptable). The subtler bug: when the column already exists, the flag is set (good), but the assignment sits at the same indent as the `if 'pattern_vector_json' not in cols` block, so it executes regardless — correct. Net: minor; the function re-opens a connection on every call until latched. Combined with the no-close leak above this is the hot path.
fix: No logic change required, but ensure the connection is closed (see leak finding) since this runs on import and on every _load_candidate_rows.

title: delta_pct computes (lv-pv)/pv when lv may be None after failed coercion
description: After `try: lv=float(latest_value); pv=float(...) except: lv=pv=None`, the code does `if pv: delta_pct = round((lv-pv)/pv*100,4)`. If only latest_value failed to coerce, both are set to None together (ok). But if the try succeeds for lv and pv but pv is a valid non-zero while lv is None is impossible here. Actually lv/pv are both None or both set — safe. Lower: but `if pv:` excludes pv==0 (correct, avoids div0). Minor; flag the missing `lv is not None` guard for defensiveness.
fix: Add `if pv and lv is not None:` to be explicit; behavior currently safe but brittle.

title: Portfolio projection multiplies factor beta (dimensionless) by avg factor return in percent but treats result directly as percent without consistent units
description: _portfolio_projection computes c = beta * af where af is avg per-factor 5d return in PERCENT (from forward_5d *100). Summing beta*percent across factors yields expected_5d_pct. This double-counts the market factor: Mkt-RF beta * Mkt-RF return already captures market move, and the per-holding loop sums the same. More concretely, factor returns from Ken French are EXCESS returns (Mkt-RF is market minus rf); projecting a portfolio's *total* expected return as Σ beta*factor_return omits the risk-free component and any non-Mkt baseline, systematically understating. This is a modeling correctness issue affecting the headline 'expected_5d_pct'.
fix: Document/confirm the excess-return convention and add the rf term, or clearly label the output as a factor-attributed excess return rather than total expected return so the UI isn't misleading.

title: Congress raw 'SP' (spouse-owner) misclassified as Sell via raw.startswith('S')
description: _m_congress_net_60d counts buys when raw in ('P','PE') and sells when raw.startswith('S'). But per opportunity_scanner's comment, 'SP' is the SPOUSE-OWNER code, not a sell, and codes like 'SE' (sale exercise) are sells. raw.startswith('S') catches 'SP' and miscounts spouse-owned purchases as sells, biasing the congress_net signal negative. opportunity_scanner explicitly excludes 'SP' from its sell set; peerdiv does not.
fix: Match opportunity_scanner: sells = raw in ('S','SE','S (partial)','S (Exchange)','E (Exchange)') and explicitly exclude 'SP'; buys = raw in ('P','PE'). Avoid the broad startswith('S').

title: _peers_from_contagion drops tickers containing '.' but BRK.B / BF.B legitimate share-class tickers are silently excluded
description: The dot-filter intended to drop foreign-listed tickers (005930.KS) also drops US share-class tickers like BRK.B, BF.B, which downstream modules CAN price. So peers for financials/industrials lose valid comparables.
fix: Only drop tickers whose suffix after '.' is a known foreign exchange code (KS, TO, L, HK, etc.), not all dots; or keep dotted US class tickers (single-letter suffix A/B).

title: _factor_panel indexes fac[last_idx] and last_row[i] assuming numpy/list 2D shape without validating row length vs cols mismatch handled but float() can raise
description: `out['factors'] = {cols[i]: round(float(last_row[i]),3) for i in range(min(len(cols),len(last_row)))}`. If last_row[i] is NaN, float(NaN) is fine but round(NaN) returns NaN and is serialized as NaN (invalid JSON). The min() guards length, but a NaN factor value propagates into composite scoring (_factor_contribution → num+=w*v with v=NaN → NaN composite for that sector).
fix: Skip non-finite values: `v=float(last_row[i]); if v==v and not math.isinf(v): factors[cols[i]]=round(v,3)`.

title: _ticker_sector caches a None sector result, then returns it as a cache hit forever (TTL) suppressing retries
description: On a Finviz failure sec=None, then `_SECTOR_LOOKUP[sym]=(None, time.time()+TTL)`. Next call `hit=_SECTOR_LOOKUP.get(sym)` is `(None, exp)`, exp>now → returns None (cached failure) for 24h. A transient Finviz hiccup permanently de-sectors a symbol for the day, dropping its insider/congress flow from every sector aggregate.
fix: Only cache successful (non-None) sector lookups; on None, don't store (or store with a short negative-TTL) so the next scan retries.

title: _congress_index calls get_recent_trades(days=30, max_pdfs=40) but does not pass tickers, downloading full PTR set every 10min
description: Unlike synth_peerdiv which pre-warms and partitions, _congress_index pulls the entire recent-trades set on every cache miss (10min TTL). With CACHE_TTL=600 and the sectorflow panel opened repeatedly, this can hammer the congress PDF parser. More of a cost/rate-limit issue than a crash.
fix: This is partly mitigated by congress.py's own cache; if not, gate the pull behind a longer-lived module cache or share the peerdiv congress cache.

title: Sharpe delta subtracts _RF_RATE*100 from expected_return_pct but expected_return is from MC terminal mean over 365d, not annualized excess consistently
description: expected_return_pct is (terminal_mean/initial -1)*100 over a 365-day horizon (≈1y), and expected_vol_pct is terminal std/initial*100 (also ~1y). Subtracting _RF_RATE*100 (4.5%) is a reasonable annual rf, so the Sharpe is roughly annual — acceptable. The latent issue: if horizon_days isn't exactly 252 trading days the 'annual' assumption is off, but it's documented as good-enough. Low severity.
fix: No fix required if horizon≈1y; otherwise scale rf by horizon/365. Document the approximation.

title: Stress-test enrichment fabricates avg_cost=market_value and shares=1.0, distorting any cost-basis/gain logic downstream
description: _stress_test sets row.setdefault('avg_cost', market_value) and shares=1.0 for ad-hoc holdings. get_portfolio_stress_test may use avg_cost for unrealized-gain or beta-weighting; defaulting avg_cost to market_value implies zero gain and shares=1 implies price==market_value, which can mis-scale per-position betas if the stress test multiplies shares*price.
fix: If shares/avg_cost are unknown, pass only market_value and let the stress test treat positions by market value, or set shares=market_value/price using a fetched price rather than the 1.0/MV placeholders.

title: _ml_weighted_return indexes h['market_value'] and h['symbol'] directly, assuming cleaned holdings, but called on 'proposed' which _apply_candidate may build without all keys
description: _apply_candidate appends {'symbol':sym,'market_value':mv} for new positions but copies existing dicts that came from _clean_holdings (which guarantees symbol/market_value). So proposed rows always have both keys — safe. However _whatif_uncached also does sum(h['market_value'] for h in current/proposed) and _weights/_optimizer use h['symbol']; if a caller bypasses whatif() and calls _whatif_uncached directly with raw holdings, KeyError. Internal contract only; low severity.
fix: Defensive .get with validation at the top of _whatif_uncached, or document that inputs must be pre-cleaned.

title: synthetic_insider cache dicts mutated without a lock
description: _cache_get/_cache_set touch module-level `_cache`/`_cache_ts` with no lock while compute_composite/scan_composite_bulk run under safe_executor fan-out, so concurrent reads/writes can corrupt the cache or read partial entries.
fix: Protect _cache/_cache_ts with a threading.Lock.

title: safe_text slices text then ORs with empty string, dropping content when text is falsy after slice
description: safe_text = (text[:10000] or '').replace('`',"'"). If text is None this raises TypeError on text[:10000] before the `or`. summarize_filing is reachable with filing_text possibly None (rule-based path handles None via text.lower() which would also crash). The `or ''` guards an empty string but not None — text[:10000] on None raises.
fix: Coerce first: safe_text = ((text or '')[:10000]).replace('`',"'"). Same for _rule_based_summarize which does text.lower() on a possibly-None text (line 687).

title: social_line bull_ratio formatting crashes if bull_ratio is a non-numeric truthy value
description: (soc.get('bull_ratio')*100):.0f only runs when soc.get('bull_ratio') is not None. If bull_ratio is a string like 'NA' (truthy, not None), the multiply 'NA'*100 produces a 200-char string and :.0f format raises ValueError, aborting _generate_idea_thesis_uncached into the fallback. The guard is `is not None`, not `isinstance(...,(int,float))`.
fix: Guard on isinstance(soc.get('bull_ratio'),(int,float)) before formatting; otherwise emit 'no data'.

title: tts_speech resp.read() may not close underlying streaming HTTP response
description: audio = resp.read() if hasattr(resp,'read') else getattr(resp,'content',None). The OpenAI streaming speech response wraps an httpx response; .read() consumes it but the response/connection isn't explicitly closed, and there's no context manager. Repeated TTS misses can leak connections from the pool.
fix: Use the SDK's streaming context manager (with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(...) as resp: audio = resp.read()) or call resp.close()/resp.stream_to... per the SDK, ensuring the response is released.

title: Rule-based earnings signal: beat_rate truthiness drops a legitimate 0% beat rate
description: if beat_rate and beat_rate>=75 ... elif beat_rate and beat_rate<=40. A genuine beat_rate of 0 (always missed) is falsy, so the `beat_rate and beat_rate<=40` branch is skipped and it never classifies BEARISH on a 0% beat rate — it falls through to NEUTRAL/insider, understating a clearly bearish track record.
fix: Compare against None explicitly: if beat_rate is not None and beat_rate>=75 ... elif beat_rate is not None and beat_rate<=40.

title: overall_score int(total_pnl_pct/5) truncates toward zero asymmetrically and can exceed bounds before clamp
description: min(10,max(1,5+int(total_pnl_pct/5))). int() truncates toward zero, so -4% -> int(-0.8)=0 -> score 5 (neutral) while +4% -> 0 -> 5 too; but -9% -> int(-1.8)=-1 -> 4 and +9% -> +1 -> 6: asymmetric rounding makes mild losses look better than symmetric mild gains. Minor scoring skew, not a crash.
fix: Use math.floor or round consistently: 5+round(total_pnl_pct/5), then clamp, so positive and negative returns are scored symmetrically.

title: json.loads(resp.choices[0].message.content) unguarded against None content within broad except only
description: If the model returns content=None (rare in json_mode but possible on a refusal/length cutoff), json.loads(None) raises TypeError; it's caught by the broad except that falls back to rule-based — acceptable, but the same pattern in analyze_portfolio/earnings/idea returns the rule-based fallback WITH error_detail, while here it silently returns rule-based, making cap/refusal vs genuine error indistinguishable in logs.
fix: Catch and log the parse failure distinctly (log.debug with the exception) before falling back, consistent with the other builders, so a systematic JSON/refusal problem is observable.

title: Earnings prompt IV-vs-historical label asserts overpricing/underpricing on missing data via (x or 0)>0
description: {'options overpricing' if (dossier.get('iv_vs_historical') or 0)>0 else 'options underpricing'}. When iv_vs_historical is None or 0 it prints 'options underpricing' as fact in the prompt, feeding the model a false premise when there's simply no IV data. The N/A in the number doesn't stop the misleading label.
fix: Compute a three-way label: if iv is None -> 'IV vs historical unavailable'; >0 overpricing; <0 underpricing; ==0 in-line. Use that string instead of the binary expression.

title: filled_qty>0 fast-fill enrichment uses '> 0' on a float that may be a string-coerced value
description: _to_result sets filled_qty via float(...), so the `> 0` check is fine, but the `res.get('filled_qty', 0) > 0` combined with `res.get('broker_order_id')` will silently skip fill enrichment if Alpaca returns filled_qty as 0 at submit even though the order later partially fills in the same response window — acceptable, but the real subtle bug is no enrichment when broker_order_id is falsy yet fills exist. Minor.
fix: Consider enriching whenever broker_order_id is present and state in ('filled','partially_filled'), not only when filled_qty>0 at submit time.

title: cash() reads only the 'cash' field; for accounts with crypto/margin this understates available buying power and ignores currency
description: cash() returns money(data.get('cash')). Alpaca's account object also has buying_power, cash_withdrawable, and (for crypto) non-USD balances. Using raw 'cash' for sizing/recon may diverge from actual deployable funds, and there's no check that the account currency is USD.
fix: Document that cash() returns the USD cash field only, and verify data.get('currency')=='USD'; if buying_power is the intended sizing basis, expose it explicitly rather than conflating with cash.

title: Repeated per-symbol _sector_of network calls inside sector-cap loop
description: Gate 11 calls _sector_of(s) once per held position inside the loop, each of which imports synth_sectorflow and may hit a sector lookup. For a large book this is O(positions) lookups every buy evaluation with no caching, and any single failure returns None (treated as a different sector), understating sec_val and letting the cap be bypassed.
fix: Compute the sector map once (e.g. {s: _sector_of(s) for s in positions}) before the loop and reuse; this also makes None-handling consistent.

title: _vol_target_factor assumes annualized_vol is a fraction; double-scaling risk if it returns percent
description: daily_vol_pct = av/sqrt(252)*100. This assumes portfolio_insights.annualized_vol returns a fraction (e.g. 0.25). If that helper returns a percentage (25.0), daily_vol_pct becomes 100x too large and the factor collapses to the 0.25 floor for every symbol, silently shrinking all vol-targeted positions to quarter size.
fix: Confirm/normalize the unit of annualized_vol (assert <~5 to detect percent vs fraction) before scaling, or convert explicitly based on the documented return contract.

title: Pyramiding gain uses (price-avg)/avg with avg>0 guard but min_gain default 0 lets any add through
description: When pyramiding is on but pyramid_min_gain_pct is unset (0), the gate `gain < min_gain` is gain<0, so it only blocks adds that are underwater — but the comment says 'only add to a winner'. With min_gain=0 a flat (0%) position is allowed to be pyramided, contradicting 'winner only'. Also pyramid_max_adds default 0 means `adds >= 0` is always true, blocking ALL adds the moment pyramiding is enabled without configuring max_adds.
fix: Treat an unconfigured pyramid_min_gain_pct as a sensible positive default (or require >0 to add), and treat pyramid_max_adds<=0 as 'unlimited' rather than 'zero allowed', so enabling pyramiding without tuning doesn't either over-add or block everything.
