title: position_aging sort key crashes-safe but treats None age as 0, mixing unaged with brand-new
description: sorted(..., key=lambda x:-(x['age_days'] or 0)). Positions with unknown age (no opened_at) get 0, sorting them alongside genuinely 0-day-old positions, so 'oldest first' ordering is corrupted by missing-data rows appearing as newest.
fix: Sort missing ages last explicitly, e.g. key=lambda x:(x['age_days'] is None, -(x['age_days'] or 0)).

title: positions_detail weight_pct divides by total_mv that can be negative for net-short books
description: weight_pct = market_value/total_mv*100 if total_mv>0. If the book is net short (negative marks aggregate) total_mv could be <=0 and all weights silently become 0.0, hiding concentration. Also individual mv for a short (negative qty) yields negative market_value, distorting the descending sort.
fix: Use abs/gross market value for weighting (sum of |mv|), and handle short positions explicitly so weights and sort reflect exposure.

title: build_briefing calls detect_regime() twice (and per-idea regime is dead)
description: detect_regime() is invoked once per idea inside the loop (line 287, result unused — never stored in the idea dict) and again at line 294 for the briefing. The per-idea call is pure overhead (each call re-fetches SPY 1y closes and computes SMAs) and its result is discarded. For k ideas that is k+1 redundant market fetches.
fix: Remove the per-idea regime = aj_alpha.detect_regime() line inside the loop; compute regime once before the loop and reuse.

title: _current_level parses raw setting with int() but a non-integer string only partly guarded
description: int(raw) is wrapped to catch TypeError/ValueError, returning default 1. But if raw is a float-like string '1.0' (e.g. written by a different code path), int('1.0') raises ValueError and silently resets the escalation level to 1 (moderate), losing a previously-escalated 'aggressive'(2) state on any format drift.
fix: Parse robustly: int(float(raw)) inside the guard, or store/read the level consistently as a plain integer string.

title: build_reflection LLM prompt formats wr with {:.0%} but passes pre-formatted string into {} placeholder
description: The prompt template has 'win-rate {}, drawdown {:.0f}%' and args pass '{:.0%}'.format(wr) as the {} value — correct. But float(day.get('day_pnl') or 0) for '$ {:.0f}' is fine. The subtle issue: dd is passed twice-formatted contexts consistently, but if wr is exactly None the ternary yields 'n/a' (ok). No crash; however r['text'][:300] assumes r['text'] is a str — if aj_routing.complete returns ok with text=None but truthy dict, .strip() would AttributeError (caught by outer except, silently dropping the polish).
fix: Guard: if r.get('ok') and isinstance(r.get('text'), str): before .strip(); minor robustness.

title: crypto vs equity fee selection uses ternary on asset_type but asset_type defaults to 'stock' uppercased mismatch
description: submit() lowercases asset_type to 'stock'/'crypto'; _fees compares asset_type=='crypto'. Consistent. However _fees is also reachable with asset_type values other than these two (e.g. 'etf'); any non-'crypto' value silently uses the equity fee_bps which may be 0, so an exotic asset type pays no fee. Minor, but the branch is binary where the system has >2 asset types elsewhere.
fix: Treat the fee tier by an explicit mapping or document that only stock/crypto are modeled; default unknown types to the equity tier intentionally.

title: cmd_run passes mode straight to run_once without validating it's one of paper|live
description: `mode` is taken from argv after --mode with no validation. A typo ('--mode papr') passes 'papr' to aj_operator.run_once, whose behavior on an unknown mode is undefined; if run_once defaults unknown modes to live-ish or errors deep, the operator gets a confusing failure instead of a clear 'unknown mode'.
fix: Validate `mode in ('paper','live')` and error out with a usage message otherwise.

title: int() of a coerced float truncates toward zero, surprising for fractional minute/day configs
description: For _INT_KEYS, `int(_coerce_float(val, DEFAULTS[key]))` truncates (floor toward zero). A user setting auto_run_interval_min='29.9' silently becomes 29, and exit_cooldown_min='0.6' becomes 0 (feature effectively off). Truncation rather than rounding can silently disable a guard that the operator believed they enabled.
fix: Use round() for these tunables, or reject non-integer input, so 0.6 doesn't collapse to 0 / disabled.

title: apply_preset overwrites strategy keys but presets omit several active guards, leaving stale prior values
description: Each preset sets a fixed subset (e.g. max_book_correlation, atr_stop_mult, kelly_sizing are NOT in any preset). Switching from a previously-customized 'aggressive' setup to 'conservative' leaves those advanced guards at their old aggressive values, so 'conservative' is not actually conservative across the full surface — a partial preset application that can surprise the operator.
fix: Document that presets are additive overlays, or have apply_preset reset all strategy-tunable keys to DEFAULTS first, then apply the preset, so a preset yields a consistent known posture.

title: _coerce_float strips '$' and ',' but also strips them mid-token, mis-parsing values like '1,2' as 12
description: `float(str(v).replace(',','').replace('$',''))` turns '1,2' into '12' and '$1,234.5' into '1234.5' (intended) but also '1,2,3' into '123'. Locale-formatted or fat-fingered inputs are silently reinterpreted as a different, larger number — dangerous for a cap value (e.g. max_order_notional '1,2' -> 12, or '12,5' -> 125).
fix: Only strip a single leading '$' and reject inputs containing commas in non-thousands positions, or parse with a stricter numeric regex; fail to the safe default on ambiguous input.

title: _applied_version int() can throw on non-numeric stored value but is caught — silently resets to 0
description: If aj_schema_version stores a corrupt non-int string, int(v) raises and the except returns 0, causing aj_migrate to re-run ALL migration steps. Re-running _DDL is IF NOT EXISTS-safe, but it then overwrites the schema version, masking corruption rather than surfacing it.
fix: Log a warning when int() fails before returning 0, so corruption is observable rather than silently re-migrated.

title: _canonical falls back to str(payload) which produces unstable, unverifiable audit material
description: If json.dumps fails (e.g. payload contains a non-serializable object default=str can't handle), it stores str(payload). The audit row_hash is then computed over a non-canonical, dict-ordering-dependent string, so verify_audit_chain remains internally consistent but the payload is effectively unparseable and not reproducible. Worse, default=str rarely fails, so this path mainly hides real serialization bugs.
fix: On json.dumps failure, wrap the payload as json.dumps({'_unserializable': str(payload)}, sort_keys=True) so the stored body is still valid canonical JSON.

title: find_stale_running_cycles reads without _write_lock while another process may be mid-writing cycle status
description: This query runs on a shared WAL DB without the write lock; a concurrent open_cycle/mark_cycle could make a just-started cycle appear 'running' with null ended_at and be misidentified as stale by a second process. With single-instance locking this is mostly prevented, but recover_crashed_cycles excludes only current_cycle, so a legitimately-running sibling (if the lock ever fails open) would be marked crashed.
fix: Filter stale cycles by an age threshold (started_at older than N minutes) in addition to status='running', so a freshly-started concurrent cycle is not reaped.

title: prune_routing holds the global write lock across DELETE+commit with no error rollback
description: Inside `with db._write_lock:` it executes DELETE then commit. If commit raises, the exception propagates out of the with-block leaving the transaction uncommitted (sqlite auto-rolls back on next use, but the write lock is released without an explicit rollback and rowcount is read after a failed commit path). No explicit error handling means a partial failure surfaces as an unhandled exception to the caller.
fix: Wrap the DELETE/commit in try/except with conn.rollback() on failure, and read cur.rowcount only after a successful commit.

title: model_leaderboard ok_rate uses SUM(ok)/calls assuming ok is 0/1, NULL ok rows skew it
description: ok_rate = (r['oks'] or 0)/calls. SUM(ok) in SQLite ignores NULLs but COUNT(*) (calls) includes rows where ok IS NULL, so any routing row with a NULL ok is counted in the denominator but not the numerator, deflating the model's ok_rate. recommend_demotions then uses this to demote models below ok_floor — NULL-ok telemetry can wrongly mark a model for demotion.
fix: Either COUNT only non-null ok rows for the denominator (SUM(CASE WHEN ok IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END)) or filter WHERE ok IS NOT NULL when computing rates.

title: Proposal status update to 'executed' swallows all exceptions, can leave proposal stuck while order is filled
description: After a partial/full fill the code updates aj_proposals.status='executed' inside a bare try/except that silently passes. If that UPDATE fails, the order/fills are recorded but the proposal stays 'approved'/'proposed', so UIs and re-scans may treat it as not-yet-executed and could re-propose. Silent pass hides a data-integrity drift.
fix: Log the exception (log.exception) instead of a bare pass, and consider auditing the inconsistency so it can be reconciled.

title: _local_positions maps any non-'paper' mode to 'live' positions, but get_broker may have returned PaperBroker with mode 'paper' — fine; risk is reconcile against a live venue object whose mode is paper
description: _local_positions returns positions_list('paper' if broker.mode=='paper' else 'live'). positions_list only ever queries aj_orders.mode in the DB; there is no 'live' paper book populated unless live fills exist. For a forced-PaperBroker (live off) this is correct. But if a live broker is active, _local_positions queries mode='live' from aj_orders which may be empty while the broker reports real positions — producing a divergence that (correctly) halts, but the 'local' side is structurally empty, so EVERY live position shows as a divergence on first run.
fix: Ensure live fills are recorded with mode='live' so the local book matches; or seed local from the broker on first reconcile to avoid a guaranteed spurious divergence/halt on initial live connect.

title: Proposal redaction whitelists 'result' which may itself contain sensitive fill/PnL data
description: The redaction comment says emit only non-sensitive fields, and picks ('symbol','side','result'). But 'result' is an open-ended value that may include qty, avg_fill_price, fees, or pnl depending on the proposal shape — exactly the portfolio data the comment says must NOT leave the box to a possibly-remote LANGFUSE_HOST.
fix: Replace 'result' with a coarse status string (e.g. result.get('state') or a boolean ok) rather than the whole result object, so no quantities/PnL egress.

title: Closure factory _make is defined but the late-binding fix is fragile to refactor
description: The `_make(n)` factory correctly captures `name` per iteration (good), but it is redefined inside the loop body on every iteration — harmless but wasteful, and a maintainer 'simplifying' by inlining `def _call` directly in the loop would reintroduce the classic late-binding bug where every tool dispatches to the last name.
fix: Hoist _make above the loop (module level or before the for) to make the intent explicit and prevent accidental reintroduction of the late-binding bug.

title: _t_forecast int() on horizon_days crashes on non-numeric input instead of failing soft
description: `horizon = int(args.get('horizon_days') or 20)`. If a caller passes horizon_days='abc' (or a list), int() raises ValueError/TypeError. invoke() wraps tool calls in try/except so it degrades to {'error':...} — acceptable — but the symbol-required check at line 63 runs AFTER the int() at line 62, so a bad horizon with a missing symbol surfaces an opaque int-parse error instead of the clearer 'symbol required'.
fix: Validate symbol first, then coerce horizon defensively: `try: horizon=int(args.get('horizon_days') or 20)` / `except Exception: horizon=20`.

title: contract_ok denylist check is unreachable for the real risk because TOOLS only contains read names; but it also can't catch a renamed mutating tool
description: The belt-and-suspenders denylist checks name.lower() against a fixed set of mutating verb names. A mutating tool added under a NEW name (e.g. 'liquidate', 'flatten', 'panic_sell') passes both the exact-set-equality check (which would already fail since names differ) and the denylist (not in the list). The real guard is FROZEN_TOOLS equality, so the denylist gives false confidence that mutating verbs are caught by name.
fix: Either remove the misleading denylist or, better, assert each tool's fn is in an allow-list of known read functions, so any non-read callable (whatever its name) fails contract_ok().

title: path_allowed does not resolve '..' or absolute paths, allowing traversal past the forbidden set
description: The function splits on '/' and fnmatches segments but never normalizes '..' or rejects absolute paths. A path like '../secrets/key' has segment 'secrets' so it's caught, but '/etc/passwd' or 'foo/../../wealth.db' — the latter has segment 'wealth.db' so caught; however a path using OS-absolute form to a copied secret outside the repo (e.g. '/tmp/exfil/.aj_secret_key') is caught by '.aj_*' on basename, but '/tmp/exfil/copied_key' is NOT. The allowlist is a denylist of names, so any unlisted sensitive location is permitted.
fix: Resolve to a normalized/real path and enforce an ALLOW-list of permitted sandbox directories (positive containment) rather than only a denylist of forbidden names.

title: fill notification falls back to sizing['price'] which may be absent for exit sells, risking KeyError swallowed
description: aj_analytics.notify_fill(..., ex.get('avg_fill_price') or sizing['price']) subscripts sizing['price']. For the exit path sizing includes 'price', so OK; but for the main scan path _size returns aj_strategy.size_order output which may not guarantee a 'price' key — a KeyError here is caught by the surrounding bare except and the fill notification is silently dropped.
fix: Use sizing.get('price') instead of sizing['price'] so a missing key degrades to None rather than relying on the broad except to swallow a KeyError.

title: premarket briefing gated on summary['session']=='premarket' but session captured once at cycle start can be stale by end of cycle
description: summary['session'] is set at the top of run_once; a long cycle could cross the premarket->regular boundary, so the end-of-cycle briefing decision uses a stale session label. Minor, but means a briefing could fire (or not) based on a session that no longer holds.
fix: Re-evaluate aj_db.market_session() at the point the briefing decision is made, or accept the documented snapshot semantics.

title: _exited set built from summary['exits'] using e.get('symbol') but _process_exits sets r['symbol'] AFTER _propose_and_execute — entries with result 'executed' but missing symbol on error path slip through
description: _exited filters exits where result=='executed'. If _propose_and_execute returned executed but the later r['symbol']=sig['symbol'] assignment was reached (it always is), fine; however an exit that raised after execution wouldn't appear, so the same symbol could be re-opened in the scan pass, causing the churn the guard intends to prevent.
fix: Build the exited-symbols set inside _process_exits at the moment of a successful execution (keyed by sig['symbol']) rather than post-hoc from the returned list, so a later exception cannot drop a just-exited symbol from the dedup set.

title: lots deque stores mutable lists [qty, price] and mutates lot[0] in place — correct, but tot_qty sum over float lots accumulates rounding without money()
description: cost = sum(l[0]*l[1] for l in dq) and tot_qty = sum(l[0]) are raw float sums never passed through money() (only the realized_* outputs are). cost_basis and avg_cost thus carry float drift into downstream weight/IPS projection (_project_pulse uses avg_cost), reintroducing the drift money() is supposed to centralize.
fix: Round cost_basis (and derived avg_cost where used for money comparisons) through aj_db.money where these feed cap/weight decisions, or document that lot math intentionally stays full-precision until a money boundary.

title: paper_book orders fills by filled_at string then id, but filled_at is ISO without guaranteed uniform precision across paper/live, risking out-of-order FIFO
description: ORDER BY f.filled_at ASC, f.id ASC relies on filled_at being lexicographically sortable. Paper fills use utc_now_iso() (seconds precision); multiple fills in the same second sort by id (OK). But a live fill timestamp in a different format/precision/timezone (e.g. with milliseconds or a 'Z' suffix vs +00:00) sorts incorrectly relative to paper timestamps, scrambling FIFO lot order and thus realized P&L.
fix: Normalize filled_at to a canonical UTC ISO format on insert (parse_iso then utc_now_iso-style), so lexical ordering equals chronological ordering across venues.

title: closing_sell carve-out compares held_now>0 but uses _held_qty which silently returns 0.0 on any exception, blocking legitimate exits
description: _held_qty wraps everything in try/except returning 0.0. If paper_book() momentarily fails, a legitimate exit/stop-loss SELL of a real held position is treated as held_now=0, closing_sell=False, and is then blocked by the allowlist — exactly the scenario the carve-out exists to prevent (exits must never be blocked).
fix: Distinguish 'flat' from 'unknown': if _held_qty cannot determine the position, fail toward permitting a SELL past the allowlist (it can only reduce risk) rather than blocking, or propagate the uncertainty so the gate doesn't silently block an exit.

title: _held_qty calls symbol.upper() on a possibly-None symbol passed from evaluate's closing_sell path
description: evaluate computes symbol=str(...).upper() before calling _held_qty(symbol), so symbol is a str there. But _held_qty is a module helper; if called elsewhere with None it raises AttributeError inside the try and returns 0.0, silently treating an unknown symbol as flat. Low risk given current callers but the helper is not defensive about its own input.
fix: Guard `(symbol or '').upper()` inside _held_qty so a None symbol yields 0.0 deterministically rather than via the broad except.

title: aj_routing telemetry records cost_usd=0.0 unconditionally even for cloud (paid) public completions
description: Every routing row hardcodes cost_usd=0.0. For public sensitivity routed to OpenAI via chat_any, the call has a real dollar cost, but the eval/telemetry loop (whose stated purpose includes bounding paid spend) always sees 0 cost, so any cost-based analysis or budgeting on aj_routing is wrong.
fix: Estimate/record the actual cost when a paid backend is used (chat_any could return token usage), or at least flag paid vs free so downstream cost accounting isn't silently zeroed.

title: in_cooldown uses strict < comparison so the exact cooldown boundary is still 'in cooldown'
description: return (now-last).total_seconds() < mins*60. At exactly mins*60 seconds it returns False (out of cooldown) — fine — but timestamps are second-truncated, so a re-entry at the same wall-second the cooldown expires may be off-by-one against the order-cap logic elsewhere. Minor consistency nit on boundary semantics.
fix: Document the boundary as exclusive, or use <= if the intent is to include the full final second; align with how other time gates compare.

title: Lease.value returns None after expiry but callers that cached .value earlier still hold the plaintext
description: The Lease redaction protects __str__/__repr__, and value returns None after expiry, but aj_alpaca already extracts .value at construction (kid.value, sec.value) and keeps the string. So the TTL provides essentially no protection for the one real consumer. This is a design gap between the lease contract and its sole caller.
fix: Document that callers must hold the Lease and read .value per use (and fix aj_alpaca accordingly), or drop the TTL pretense; otherwise the expiry is dead protection.

title: has() executes a query on get_conn() but relies on thread-local pooling; cursor not explicitly closed
description: has() and lease() call db.get_conn().execute(...).fetchone() without closing the cursor. With sqlite3 the implicit cursor is GC'd, but on a long-lived thread-local connection these accumulate until GC; more importantly fetchone leaves the statement around. Minor, but in the hot lease path it's avoidable.
fix: Use a context-managed cursor or call .close(); negligible but consistent with the rest of the code's explicit handling.

title: aj_positions count uses len() on data.get('positions') which may be a list not a dict
description: `n = len(data.get('positions') or {})`. The default {} suggests positions is expected to be a dict, but aj_positions.paper_book may return positions as a list. len() works on both, so no crash, but if positions is ever a dict of symbol->lot-list, len() counts symbols which is intended; if it's a flat list of lots, the count is lot count, not position count — the spoken 'open position(s)' would be wrong.
fix: Confirm the shape of paper_book()['positions'] and count distinct symbols explicitly, e.g. len(set of symbols), so the spoken count matches 'positions'.

title: Analyst velocity detail formats target as float even when None
description: When `target` is None the else-branch sets `target = 0`; but if the try-branch raises before reassigning (e.g. float(target) fails), `target` remains the original non-float and `'${:.0f}'.format(target)` would raise. The except catches ValueError/TypeError/ZeroDivisionError around the upside math but leaves `target` as a non-numeric, then the format string at line 315 can raise ValueError outside that try.
fix: After the try/except, coerce `target = float(target) if isinstance(target,(int,float)) else 0` (or wrap the detail format), so the {:.0f} never sees a non-numeric.

title: _cget returns None for a genuine cached negative when value is falsy-but-not-_NEG
description: _cget returns `v[0]` only when `v is not None`. Cached values like an empty list `[]` (negative cache for reddit/stocktwits_trending) are returned as `[]` correctly. But stocktwits_symbol_sentiment relies on `hit is _NEG` to distinguish a cached negative from a real result; _cget returns _NEG (the stored value) which works. However reddit_subreddit_posts caches `[]` and returns it, while a genuine miss also returns None — callers that treat both `[]` and None as 'no data' are fine, but any caller distinguishing 'tried and empty' from 'never tried' cannot, partially defeating the negative cache.
fix: Return a distinct sentinel for cached-empty vs miss across all helpers (as already done for stocktwits via _NEG), or document that empty-list cache and miss are intentionally indistinguishable for posts.

title: _test_openai leaks exception text (may contain key fragments) into the API 'detail' response
description: On a non-401 failure: `return {'ok':False,'detail':'Could not verify: {}'.format(msg[:160])}`. The OpenAI SDK exception string can embed the request including an Authorization header fragment or the key in some error formats; this detail is surfaced to the /api/keys response and potentially logged, partially exposing secret material.
fix: Scrub the message of anything resembling a key before returning (strip 'sk-...' tokens), or return a generic 'Could not verify (network/SDK error).' without the raw exception text.

title: mask() reveals last 4 chars for keys >=12 — combined with known 'sk-' prefix narrows entropy
description: mask returns '••••'+key[-4:] for length>=12. For OpenAI keys the public prefix is known ('sk-'); exposing the last 4 chars in API responses (and these are returned by list_providers/mask_settings) leaks 4 chars of the secret to any client that can read /api/keys. Defensible UX, but it is secret material in an HTTP response.
fix: Consider masking entirely or revealing only last 2 chars; ensure /api/keys is auth-gated so the tail isn't readable by unauthenticated clients.

title: earnings_dossier accepts arbitrary unvalidated AI model string
description: ai_model = request.args.get('model', 'gpt-4o') is passed straight to ai_summarizer.generate_earnings_brief(model=ai_model) with no allowlist. A client can pass an unknown/expensive model id; portfolio_ai_analysis and jarvis_tts validate or default their model/voice, but this route does not.
fix: Validate ai_model against a known set (e.g. {'gpt-4o','gpt-4o-mini',...}) and fall back to the default when not recognized, mirroring the voice allowlist in jarvis_tts_route.

title: intel_feed zip over uncached_filings re-walks list while pair may be None
description: `for f, pair in zip(uncached_filings, summarized)` then `ai_result = pair[1] if pair else {}`. parallel_map returns None for a slot whose work fn raised, but _summarize_and_cache catches its own exceptions and returns a tuple, so pair should be a 2-tuple. However if parallel_map itself fails to schedule (returns fewer items or None entries despite the wrapper), `pair[1]` is guarded by `if pair`, but a non-None non-subscriptable value would still IndexError. Low risk but the indexing is fragile.
fix: Use `ai_result = (pair[1] if isinstance(pair, (list, tuple)) and len(pair) > 1 else {})` to harden against a malformed slot.

title: get_transactions route does not clamp negative limit
description: limit = _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 100) is passed directly to db.get_transactions(..., limit=limit). A negative limit becomes SQL `LIMIT -1` which SQLite interprets as 'no limit' (all rows) — the opposite of the caller's intent and a potential large-payload DoS. Other routes (scanner_watchlist line 2079, congress_all line 2110) explicitly clamp with max(1, ...); this one does not.
fix: Clamp: `limit = max(1, _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 100))` (and optionally cap with min()).

title: scanner_history limit unclamped (negative -> all rows)
description: limit = _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 100) passed to db.get_scan_history without a positive clamp; a negative value yields SQL LIMIT -1 (all rows). Same class of bug the codebase already guards against in scanner_watchlist.
fix: Clamp to a positive minimum: `limit = max(1, _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 100))`.

title: congress_senate limit unclamped
description: limit = _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 200) passed straight to ds.get_senate_trades(limit=limit). A negative limit can slice off rows or, if used as a SQL/list limit downstream, return unintended results. The adjacent congress_all route clamps with max(1,...) for exactly this reason.
fix: Clamp: `limit = max(1, _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 200))`.

title: _evaluate_jarvis_watches updates last-eval timestamp before doing the work, skipping on transient failure
description: Inside the lock, _JARVIS_WATCH_EVAL_LAST is set to now (line 208) BEFORE evaluate_all runs. If evaluate_all raises (caught at line 229) the timestamp has already advanced, so the next tick (within 5 min) is skipped even though no evaluation actually completed. Watches can silently go un-evaluated for an extra cadence on every transient error.
fix: Only advance _JARVIS_WATCH_EVAL_LAST after a successful evaluate_all (move the timestamp assignment to after the try-block succeeds), while still holding the gate to prevent double-run.

title: portfolio_dividends slot-0 sentinel collides if a holding's symbol is literally None
description: _div_task uses `item is None` as the sentinel for the live-quotes batch. The task list is `[None] + equity_syms`. If db ever returns a holding with symbol None (corrupt row), equity_syms would contain None too, and that worker would mistakenly run the quotes batch instead of a dividend fetch, corrupting div_map alignment via zip. Low likelihood but the sentinel is unsafe.
fix: Use a unique private sentinel object instead of None, e.g. `_QUOTES = object()` and test `if item is _QUOTES`.

title: _mc_holdings_from_portfolio drops positions whose live price is exactly 0 instead of falling back to cost basis
description: `px = q.get('price'); if not px: continue` (lines 41-43) skips any holding without a truthy live price. For a genuinely 0-priced or quote-missing position the function silently excludes it from the Monte Carlo portfolio, understating exposure — inconsistent with the rest of the app which falls back to avg_cost for missing quotes.
fix: Use `px = q.get('price'); cur = px if px is not None else h.get('avg_cost'); if not cur or cur <= 0: continue; mv = cur * h['shares']` so missing quotes fall back to cost basis.

title: portfolio_benchmark normalizes to the earliest snapshot even when it is from an empty/zero portfolio
description: base_value = snapshots[0]['total_value'] uses the first ever snapshot. If the earliest snapshot was taken when the portfolio was tiny/zero (total_value 0 or near-0), get_benchmark_history normalizes the benchmark to that base, producing wildly distorted comparison series. There is no guard for base_value <= 0.
fix: Pass the first snapshot with a positive total_value: `base_value = next((s['total_value'] for s in snapshots if s.get('total_value')), None)`.

title: _social_composite buzz averages heterogeneous components, letting one live source dominate
description: buzz = round(sum(parts)/len(parts)). If only the Wikipedia spike component is live, buzz is driven entirely by `50 + spike` with no StockTwits/HN data, presenting a single-source attention proxy as a blended 'buzz score'. Worse, spike_pct is read from wk even when wk is not live (line 2463 reads spike before the _live(wk) check), so a stale/non-live wikipedia 'stats' still surfaces spike_pct in the output (line 2492).
fix: Compute spike only inside the `_live(wk)` branch and set spike_pct in the return to None unless wikipedia is live; optionally weight/label buzz with sources_live so a 1-source score isn't presented as a composite.

title: intel_filings_v2 calls symbol.upper() before validating symbol
description: When _sec_v2_unavailable() is true the route returns `dict(_SEC_V2_DORMANT_ENVELOPE, symbol=symbol.upper())` (line 2361) BEFORE the _valid_ticker check at line 2362. symbol is a path segment and always a str so .upper() won't crash, but the ordering means an invalid symbol gets a 503 'unavailable' envelope rather than the 400 'Invalid symbol' it should — and the same pattern is repeated in intel_form4_v2 (line 2375). Validation should precede capability checks for consistent error semantics.
fix: Move the `if not _valid_ticker(symbol): return 400` check above the _sec_v2_unavailable() check in both intel_filings_v2 and intel_form4_v2.

title: aj_run_route charges the rate limiter before the single-instance lock check, leaking budget on contention
description: _jarvis_act_charge(1) is consumed (line 3405) before aj_operator.run_once. If run_once returns the 'already running' refusal (409 at line 3412), the rate-limit slot was still consumed even though no cycle ran. A client polling Run repeatedly while a cycle is in progress burns the 10/min budget on no-op refusals.
fix: Run the cycle first (or peek the lock) and only charge the limiter when a cycle actually starts; or refund the slot on the 409 refusal path.

title: scanner_profile_save stores arbitrary unvalidated JSON as the scanner profile
description: data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True); if not data -> 400; else scanner.save_scanner_profile(data) with no shape validation. A client can persist arbitrary keys/types (e.g. a list, or fields scan_opportunities later indexes by key) which can crash subsequent scanner_scan runs (KeyError/TypeError) since the saved profile is read back as the scan config.
fix: Validate that data is a dict with the expected profile keys/types (or merge into a known-schema default) before save_scanner_profile, rejecting unexpected shapes with 400.

title: jarvis_tts_route reads voice from settings without guarding non-string DB value
description: voice = data.get('voice') or db.get_settings().get('jarvis_tts_voice') or 'onyx'; then str(voice).lower()[:20]. If the stored jarvis_tts_voice is a non-string (e.g. a number written via /api/settings before the coercion was added), str() handles it, but the subsequent allowlist check will 400 a previously-working configured voice. Minor robustness gap; the bigger issue is settings can store non-allowlisted voices that then 400 every TTS call.
fix: On read, coerce and fall back to default if not in _OK_VOICES rather than 400 when the value came from settings (only 400 when the client explicitly passed an unknown voice).

title: portfolio_dividends includes positions with missing quotes at cost basis in portfolio_yield denominator but annual_income from possibly-stale div_rate
description: total_portfolio_value accumulates market_value using cost-basis fallback (good), but annual_income uses div_data.get('div_rate') which may be 0 for a failed dividend fetch (div_map[sym]=={}). A position whose dividend fetch failed contributes its value to the denominator but 0 income, silently understating portfolio_yield rather than flagging the position as having unknown dividend data.
fix: Track positions with failed dividend fetches separately and either exclude them from the yield denominator or surface a 'dividend_data_unavailable' flag so the summary isn't silently biased low.

title: get_portfolio day_change_pct passed through even when day_change is None/0 inconsistently
description: h.update sets day_change=day_chg (may be None) and day_pnl=round(day_chg*shares,2) if day_chg is not None else None, but day_change_pct=q.get('change_pct') is set unconditionally. A quote can return change_pct while change is None (or vice versa) from the fallback paths, so the UI can show a percent move with no absolute change or a None day_pnl beside a non-None percent — inconsistent day-change reporting.
fix: Gate day_change_pct on the same condition: `'day_change_pct': q.get('change_pct') if day_chg is not None else None`, or compute both consistently from the same source.

title: Snapshot worker mutates holding dicts shared with no other reader but reuses prices dict across alert phase introducing crypto -USD keys
description: _portfolio_live_prices returns a dict whose crypto entries are keyed by the bare symbol AND (from the raw batch) the -USD uppercase key. In the alert phase, prices.update(get_quotes_batch(missing)) merges more uppercase keys. This is benign for current callers, but the alert phase then reads prices.get(alert['symbol']) where crypto alerts stored as bare symbols won't match the -USD-only entry — the same root cause as the crypto-alert defect but also means the prices dict semantics differ between the two phases, which is fragile.
fix: Normalize the prices dict to a single, documented key convention (always bare uppercase symbol) before the alert phase, remapping -USD crypto keys back to their bare symbol.

title: _hits/_misses incremented without lock and read in stats without barrier
description: Documented as intentional, but the lost-update on counters also means hit_rate can momentarily exceed 1.0 or be slightly negative-looking if a read lands mid-update. Low severity (observability only) but flagged since stats() is exposed on a debug endpoint and could mislead.
fix: Acceptable as-is, or use itertools.count / a single lock-free atomic; at minimum clamp hit_rate to [0,1] in stats().

title: cache_get drops error-envelope dicts but len<=3 check misclassifies small valid dicts
description: Read-time defense: `if isinstance(value,dict) and value.get('error') and len(value)<=3: drop`. A valid cached payload that happens to carry a truthy 'error' key among <=3 keys (e.g. a 2-key {'symbol':X,'error':None} is excluded by truthiness, but {'id':X,'error':'partial','data':...} with exactly 3 keys and a non-fatal 'error' note) is silently treated as a miss and evicted, causing perpetual refetch.
fix: Tighten the condition to the exact negative-envelope shape produced internally (e.g. require keys subset of {'symbol','error','note'}) rather than a generic len<=3 + truthy-error test.

title: Exchange transactions counted as sells, skewing buy/sell ratio
description: In get_congress_summary, 'S (Exchange)' and 'E (Exchange)' are bucketed under sells. Exchanges (e.g. fund share-class swaps) are not directional sales; counting them as sells biases buy_pct downward and can flip a ticker's sentiment to BEARISH/MIXED. The inline comment acknowledges the ambiguity but keeps the skew.
fix: Treat exchange variants as a separate 'neutral'/'exchange' bucket excluded from buy_pct, or document that exchanges are intentionally counted as sells.

title: Circuit breaker can stay open until process restart, blanking Congress feature
description: The parse circuit opens on a streak of gate-busy timeouts (busy_streak>=5) and only resets on a successful parse (_note_parse_ok). If genuinely-hung parses leak both gate permits, NO parse can ever succeed, so busy_streak never resets and the breaker stays open for the life of the process — the Congress feature returns empty indefinitely with no time-based recovery.
fix: Add a time-based half-open reset (e.g. reset busy_streak after N seconds since it tripped) so the breaker periodically retries instead of requiring a restart.

title: PTR txn-type fallback can grab a stray P/S from option metadata
description: When no explicit txn type is found after the asset bracket, the code searches `clean[:100]` (pre-date window with owner stripped) for `\b(P|S|PE|SE)\b`. Tickers/words containing isolated P or S (e.g. an option description, a middle initial 'S.', or 'PE' in 'PEPSI' won't trigger due to boundaries, but a lone 'P' in 'P.' will) can mis-tag a transaction's direction, flipping a buy/sell in the parsed output.
fix: Anchor the fallback to the position immediately after the asset-type bracket (after_ticker) only, or require the P/S token to be adjacent to a date/amount, to avoid matching incidental letters.

title: META supply chain references SNAP which is absent from KNOWN_COMPANIES
description: KNOWN_SUPPLY_CHAINS['META'] includes ('SNAP','peer'), but 'SNAP' is not a key/value in KNOWN_COMPANIES, so `_TICKER_TO_NAME.get('SNAP','SNAP')` yields 'SNAP' as the name. Cosmetic: the node shows ticker as name. Not a crash, but the curated graph has an unmapped node.
fix: Add 'Snap': 'SNAP' (and/or 'Snap Inc') to KNOWN_COMPANIES so the node resolves a proper name.

title: Ticker regex matches common English words as tickers
description: The all-caps 1-5 char ticker scan (`\b([A-Z]{1,5})\b`) intersected with _KNOWN_TICKERS still admits tickers that are real words/abbreviations near generic keywords ('ALL','KEY','NOW','ON','GE','HD','DE','MO'...). With the broad context_keywords ('revenue','sales','order','contract'), unrelated prose can register phantom supply-chain edges. _KNOWN_TICKERS limits the blast radius but words like 'ON','GE','NOW','HD','DE' are both tickers and common tokens.
fix: Require the token to be a cashtag ($ON) or appear with a disambiguating context (e.g. '(ON)' or 'ON Semiconductor'), or exclude a small stoplist of word-like tickers from the bare-token pass.

title: xbrl latest() sorts XBRL entries by string 'end' date lexicographically — relies on ISO format
description: `sorted([e for e in entries if e.get('end')], key=lambda e: e['end'], reverse=True)` sorts dates as strings. SEC XBRL 'end' is ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' so lexicographic == chronological, BUT if any entry has a malformed or differently-formatted 'end' the 'latest' picked is wrong, silently returning a stale metric. Also ignores 'fy'/'fp'/'frame' so it may pick a quarterly point over an annual with the same end.
fix: Filter to ISO-shaped ends and/or parse to date; prefer 10-K/annual frames when present so headline metrics aren't a random quarterly snapshot.

title: data_sources _cache_set eviction only prunes when >200 and only removes expired — can exceed cap indefinitely
description: `_cache_set` evicts only entries already past expiry (`v[1] < now`) up to 50, and only when len>200. If 200+ entries are all still fresh (e.g. many distinct GDELT queries within their TTL), nothing is evicted and the dict grows unbounded above 200. The negative-sentinel and long-TTL entries make this realistic.
fix: After the expired sweep, if still over cap, evict the oldest-by-expiry entries (sorted by v[1]) to bring it under 200, mirroring cache_store's LRU.

title: gdelt_tone_timeline assumes timeline[0]['data'] is the tone series
description: `series = _tl[0].get('data') if (_tl and isinstance(_tl[0],dict)) else []`. GDELT TimelineTone can return multiple series objects or reorder them; blindly taking [0] may grab the wrong series (e.g. volume instead of tone) when GDELT changes ordering, silently charting the wrong metric.
fix: Select the series whose 'series' label matches tone (e.g. find the entry where series name contains 'Tone') rather than index 0.

title: get_cached_institutional total_value defaults to 0 masking a genuine None
description: `d['total_value'] = d.get('total_value_usd', 0)`. If total_value_usd is NULL in the row, this returns 0, which downstream may render as '$0 fund' rather than 'unknown'. Minor data-integrity: a real zero and a missing value are conflated.
fix: `d['total_value'] = d.get('total_value_usd')` (preserve None) and let the UI format missing values.

title: jarvis_conversation_exists swallows DB errors as 'does not exist'
description: The except catches (OverflowError, ValueError, TypeError) from int() but the conn.execute itself can raise sqlite3.OperationalError (locked/closed); that is NOT caught here and would propagate, OR if it were, returning False conflates 'DB error' with 'conversation absent', causing ask() to silently fork to a new thread on a transient lock.
fix: Either let operational errors propagate explicitly, or catch them and re-raise/log rather than implicitly returning False; keep the int-coercion guard separate from the query.

title: _migrate_settings int(row['value']) raises if __schema_version__ value is non-numeric
description: `current = int(row['value']) if row else 0`. If an older/corrupt DB stored __schema_version__ as a non-numeric string, int() raises ValueError. init_db wraps _migrate_settings in try/except so it degrades, but the migration then never runs and retired keys are never swept for that install.
fix: `try: current = int(row['value']) except (TypeError,ValueError): current = 0` so a corrupt sentinel is treated as 'needs migration' rather than aborting.

title: Post-earnings move direction compares None>=0 (TypeError, swallowed)
description: move_pct is set to None when `before` is falsy, then `'UP' if move_pct >= 0 else 'DOWN'` evaluates `None >= 0`, raising TypeError. It's inside try/except: continue, so the row is silently dropped rather than recorded — post_earnings_moves loses legitimate quarters whenever a close is 0/None.
fix: Skip when move_pct is None (`if move_pct is None: continue`) before building the direction, instead of letting the comparison raise.

title: avg_surprise scaled by 100 in calendar path but not in dossier path
description: _calendar_for_one computes avg_surprise = mean(surprisePercent)*100 (treating it as a fraction), while get_earnings_dossier computes avg_surprise = mean(Surprise(%)) with no *100. These come from two different yfinance frames with different units, but if either frame's convention differs from the assumption, the same metric is reported on two different scales across the calendar vs dossier views, confusing users comparing them.
fix: Confirm yfinance units for each frame and normalize both to the same scale (percent), documenting the convention; ensure the calendar and dossier report avg_surprise consistently.

title: Insider signal thresholds are asymmetric and can misfire on tiny values
description: signal = BULLISH if buy_val > sell_val*1.5 and len(buys)>=1 else BEARISH if sell_val > buy_val*2 else NEUTRAL. When both buy_val and sell_val are 0 (e.g. all txns had value 0 due to missing price), `0 > 0*1.5` is False and `0 > 0*2` is False → NEUTRAL, fine; but a single tiny buy of $1 with zero sells yields buy_val>0 and BULLISH, overstating conviction on negligible dollar flow.
fix: Add a minimum-dollar floor (e.g. require buy_val above a threshold) before declaring BULLISH/BEARISH.

title: RSI returns inf-derived 100 mapped value never reached due to float('inf') branch
description: `rs = avg_gain/avg_loss if avg_loss else (1.0 if avg_gain==0 else float('inf'))`. When rs is float('inf'), `100 - 100/(1+inf)` = 100 - 0 = 100.0, which is intended. That's fine. The actual issue: after the first division by zero avg_loss can stay 0 for the smoothed loop; with Wilder smoothing once avg_loss hits exactly 0 it stays 0 forever, pinning RSI at 100 even after losses resume within the same window only at the boundary. Minor but produces a stuck-100 RSI on low-volatility uptrends.
fix: Seed avg_loss with a tiny epsilon or fall back to a non-smoothed recompute when avg_loss==0 across the window; e.g. clamp `avg_loss = max(avg_loss, 1e-12)` in the smoothing loop.

title: Stress test reads info.get('sectorKey') but sector mapping keys are display names
description: `entry['sector'] = info.get('sector') or info.get('sectorKey') or 'Unknown'`. yfinance 'sectorKey' returns slugs like 'technology'/'financial-services', not the display names used as keys in _SCENARIOS['...']['sector_overrides'] (e.g. 'Financial Services'). When 'sector' is absent and the code falls back to sectorKey, the sector_override lookup misses and the holding gets beta-adjusted market drop instead of the (much larger) sector-specific drop, understating crisis losses.
fix: Drop the sectorKey fallback (it doesn't match override keys) or map slug->display before lookup. Simplest: `entry['sector'] = info.get('sector') or 'Unknown'`.

title: CoinGecko prev-close inversion divides by (1+pct/100) which is undefined at pct=-100
description: `_denom = 1 + change_pct/100; prev = price/_denom if (price and _denom)`. If usd_24h_change == -100 (coin lost all value in 24h, or a bad feed), _denom == 0 and the `price and _denom` guard treats 0 as falsy so prev=None — acceptable. But a value slightly above -100 (e.g. -99.99999) yields an enormous prev and a giant 'change', polluting the quote. Also `price and _denom` drops a legitimate price of 0.0.
fix: Guard the denominator explicitly: `prev = price/_denom if (price is not None and _denom not in (None,0)) else None`, and clamp/round-trip implausible change_pct (<= -100).

title: Redundant/confusing conditional in get_quote fallback loop
description: Line 595: `fbq = fb(symbol) if fb is not _try_crypto_fallback else fb(symbol)` — both branches are identical, so the ternary is dead and misleading. _try_crypto_fallback takes (symbol, ttl=30) so calling fb(symbol) is fine, but the intent (special-casing crypto) was clearly lost in an edit. Not a runtime bug but a latent maintenance hazard masking that all three fallbacks are invoked identically.
fix: Replace with plain `fbq = fb(symbol)`.

title: get_news caches at most _NEWS_MAX_KEEP but a caller asking for >30 gets silently truncated
description: `fetch_n = max(limit, _NEWS_MAX_KEEP)` so a caller requesting limit=50 fetches 50, but the cache hit path returns `hit[:limit]` where hit was stored from a possibly-smaller fetch_n window of a prior caller who asked for 15 (storing 30). A later limit=50 caller hits the cache and gets only 30 even though 50 exist upstream. The cache key ignores limit by design, but the stored payload length is whichever first caller populated it.
fix: Always fetch and store _NEWS_MAX_KEEP regardless of the requesting limit (cap limit at _NEWS_MAX_KEEP), and document that >30 is unsupported, OR include max(limit,_NEWS_MAX_KEEP) actually fetched count and refetch when a larger limit misses the stored length.

title: Stress-test total_loss_pct divides by total_current_value computed from market_value-or-cost mix
description: total_current_value sums `h.get('market_value',0) or 0` but per-position mv falls back to shares*avg_cost when market_value is missing. So total_current_value (which excludes the cost fallback) can be smaller than the sum of per-position mv used for total_new_value, making total_loss_pct denominator inconsistent with the numerator and producing a percentage that doesn't match the dollar loss.
fix: Compute total_current_value from the SAME mv fallback used per position: `sum(h.get('market_value') or (h.get('shares',0)*h.get('avg_cost',0)) for h in enriched)`.

title: Calmar ratio uses abs(max_dd) but max_dd can be 0 for a monotonically rising series -> None, hiding a strong result
description: `calmar = ann_return/abs(max_dd) if max_dd != 0 else None`. A series with no drawdown (max_dd==0) yields Calmar=None (undefined), which is mathematically correct (infinite Calmar) but the UI shows 'no data' for the best-performing, lowest-drawdown asset — the opposite of the intended signal.
fix: Map max_dd==0 with positive ann_return to a sentinel/cap (e.g. very high Calmar) or label 'no drawdown' rather than None so the strongest asset isn't blanked.

title: Unusual options 'volume' read once may be NaN passing _safe but failing int() later
description: `vol = _safe(row.get('volume')) or 0`. _safe converts NaN to None (via pd.isna) so `or 0` handles it. But `int(vol)` at line 2503 and the sort `x['volume']` assume int; if a row's volume is a float like 250.0 that's fine, but a very large volume stored as numpy int could overflow int() in edge cases on 32-bit — minor. The more concrete issue: notional uses last_price which may be 0 for illiquid contracts, making notional 0 while vol>=200 still flags it as unusual with $0 notional.
fix: Skip contracts with last_price<=0 (or bid/ask both 0) before flagging, so $0-notional rows don't appear as 'unusual'.

title: get_correlation_matrix missing_symbols computed against returns.columns that may be MultiIndex tuples
description: When returns has a MultiIndex (rare path), `str(c).upper()` stringifies a tuple like "('CLOSE','AAPL')" so the membership test against sym_upper never matches and ALL requested symbols are reported missing even though data exists.
fix: Flatten columns to symbol level before the upper() comparison (the single/multi handling in _get_returns_df should already yield flat columns; assert/convert here defensively).

title: Brier skill reference can be 0 when all outcomes identical, silently yielding None skill but verdict path mislabels
description: ref = base_rate*(1-base_rate); when every scored outcome is up (base_rate=1) or down (0), ref=0, skill=None, verdict='INSUFFICIENT SPREAD'. That is reasonable, but brier itself is still reported (could be small) and consumers may rank components with None skill as worst (-9.0 in component_leaderboard _rank), pushing a possibly-accurate-but-low-variance component to the bottom purely due to no outcome spread. This can mis-order the leaderboard that drives adaptive weights.
fix: When skill is None due to zero spread but n is large and brier is low, treat the component neutrally in ranking (e.g. rank key falls back to -brier rather than -9.0) so a degenerate base rate doesn't unfairly demote it.

title: _weights_cache module dict mutated without lock under concurrent ensemble forecasts
description: adaptive_weights reads/writes the module-global _weights_cache from forecast_ensemble._run_uncached, which runs under safe_executor thread pools and multiple request threads. The check-then-set on _weights_cache[key] is unsynchronized; concurrent writers can interleave, and a reader can get a half-updated tuple. Impact is low (weights are advisory) but it is a genuine shared-mutable-state race.
fix: Guard _weights_cache access with a threading.Lock, or accept stale reads but make the write atomic by assigning the fully-built tuple in one statement (already the case) and documenting the benign race.

title: Return-cone tilt uses abs(half_width) so a degenerate inverted IQR still shifts the cone
description: half_width = (p75 - p25)/2; shift = tilt*0.66*abs(half_width). If the bootstrap distribution returns p25>p75 (shouldn't, but possible with rounding or a degenerate sample), abs() masks the inversion and still applies a shift based on a meaningless width, nudging expected_return_pct by an arbitrary amount.
fix: Use max(0.0, p75-p25)/2 and skip the tilt when the width is non-positive, so a degenerate distribution produces no spurious shift.

title: GEX uses a single risk-free rate and DataFrame gamma without scaling check
description: When the option chain DataFrame provides a `gamma` column it is used directly (line 333-340) without verifying it is per-share gamma; mixing provider-supplied gamma with BS-computed gamma for other strikes yields inconsistent GEX magnitudes across strikes within the same symbol. Not a crash but can distort net_gex and walls.
fix: Either always recompute gamma via BS for consistency, or only trust the DataFrame gamma when present for ALL rows of the chain.

title: _dynamic_crypto_id_map mutated without lock from _filtered_universe under concurrent rolls
description: get_full_crypto_universe is guarded by a lock, but _filtered_universe writes _dynamic_crypto_id_map[sym]=entry['id'] without any lock. Concurrent idea generations (multiple users / warmer + UI) mutate this module-global dict concurrently. Dict item assignment is atomic in CPython so unlikely to corrupt, but it's shared mutable state by convention.
fix: Guard writes/reads of _dynamic_crypto_id_map with a lock, or build it once during the locked full-universe pull rather than during every filtered-universe call.

title: get_full_crypto_universe time.sleep(1.2) inside lock holds _full_crypto_lock for entire paginated fetch, serializing all crypto-universe callers for many seconds
description: The CoinGecko pagination loop (up to ~2 pages with 1.2s sleeps) runs while holding _full_crypto_lock. Any other thread calling get_full_crypto_universe blocks for the full fetch duration. For a UI 'full discovery' roll this can stall concurrent requests several seconds.
fix: Fetch outside the lock, then acquire the lock only to store the result (double-checked), so concurrent readers don't serialize behind the network+sleep.

title: _portfolio_total_value uses quoted price else avg_cost, but float(price or 0) double-applies fallback and counts holdings with no price/avg_cost as 0 silently
description: price = quoted price if not None else avg_cost; then total += shares*float(price or 0). If quoted price is None AND avg_cost is None/0, the position contributes 0 to book value, understating portfolio_value used for sizing tiers. A book with several unpriceable names would size positions too small.
fix: Track and surface positions that couldn't be valued (count/symbols) so sizing can warn, or fall back to last-known price; at minimum don't silently treat unpriced positions as $0.

title: Freshness compared via lexicographic string compare of ISO timestamps with potential tz-offset format mismatch
description: get_warmed_dossier compares row['warmed_at'] < _ttl_cutoff_iso() as strings. _now_iso() and _ttl_cutoff_iso() both use datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), which yields '+00:00' suffix; warmed_at is written by _now_iso so formats match. Safe as long as ALL writers use _now_iso. _persist_dossier uses _now_iso (ok). Latent risk if any path writes a differently-formatted timestamp (e.g. with 'Z' suffix) the lexicographic compare breaks.
fix: Parse both sides to datetime for comparison, or assert a single canonical timestamp format across all writers.

title: weight_pct set to 0 when total_value falsy, but rows already require price
description: `r["weight_pct"] = round(r["market_value"]/total_value*100,2) if total_value else 0`. total_value is the sum of priced market values; if every priced position had market_value 0 (price>0 required earlier so unlikely) total_value could be 0 and all weights become 0. Minor, but a single negative+positive cancellation is impossible here. Lower risk; noting the guard exists.
fix: No change needed unless market_value can be negative; consider guarding total_value<=0 rather than just falsy.

title: away_digest 'days' label uses //1440 but 'hours' branch starts at 120 min not 1440
description: away phrasing: >=2880 → days, >=120 → hours, else minutes. The gap between 2880 (48h) and the day label means anything 2 hours to 48 hours is labeled in hours (e.g. '36 hours' instead of '1 day'). Cosmetic, but '36 hours ago' for 1.5 days is awkward and inconsistent with the 2880 cutoff that should arguably be 1440.
fix: Lower the day-label threshold to 1440 (24h) if day phrasing is desired earlier, or document the 48h choice.

title: share_of_move clamp min(...,999) hides genuinely large attributions silently
description: _answer_why _phrase clamps `min(e["share_of_move_pct"],999)`. When a single name accounts for >999% of a tiny net move (others offsetting), it prints '999% of the move' which is misleading rather than informative; the 1.0 abs(total) guard already prevents most, but values like 250% still slip through and read as errors to users.
fix: When share exceeds ~100%, phrase it differently ('more than the whole move — others offset') instead of printing a raw >100% number.

title: _forecast_line threshold uses hr*100 recomputed inline, duplicating the conditional
description: `"Holding my edge." if (hr*100 if hr<=1 else hr)>=55 else "Calibrating."` recomputes the normalization separately from the display expression. If hr is exactly 1.0 it normalizes to 100 (>=55, edge) which is right, but the duplicated conditional is a maintenance hazard and could diverge from the display value if one is edited.
fix: Compute `hr_pct = hr*100 if hr<=1 else hr` once and reuse it for both the format and the comparison.

title: _answer_transactions formats shares/price with {:g}/${:,.2f} but falls back to 0 hiding missing data
description: `t.get("shares") or 0` and `t.get("price") or 0` substitute 0 for missing or zero values. A transaction with a legitimately recorded 0 price (e.g. a transfer/gift) or missing shares prints as '0 SYM @ $0.00', which is indistinguishable from corrupt data and misleads the user about a real fill.
fix: Only default to 0 when the field is None; otherwise display the actual value, and consider a placeholder like '?' for genuinely missing fields.

title: Mover card prints day_pnl via _fmt_usd(r.get('day_pnl')) which may be None → '—' inside a sentence about a move
description: For a big-move card, the detail string interpolates `_fmt_usd(r.get("day_pnl"))`. day_pnl is None when change was unavailable, but the card only triggers when day_change_pct is not None — yet change_pct can be present while change (absolute) is None, yielding '— day P&L on your $X position' which reads as broken.
fix: Guard the card on day_pnl being present too, or phrase without the dollar P&L when it's None.

title: _answer_portfolio all-time detection substring 'overall' matches 'overall market' style false positives
description: alltime = any(p in q_lower for p in (... 'overall' ...)). A question like 'how is my portfolio doing overall today' contains both 'overall' and 'today'; alltime becomes True and best/worst flip to unrealized P&L even though the user said 'today'. The token 'overall' over-triggers all-time mode.
fix: Require all-time tokens AND absence of day tokens ('today','day'), or use word-boundary matching to avoid 'overall' hijacking day-scope questions.

title: _memory_block semmem dedup compares quoted.lower() but seeds 'seen' from lines (already-quoted) lowercased correctly, yet length check len(quoted)>5 lets near-empty quotes through
description: The recall loop appends a hit when `quoted.lower() not in seen and len(quoted)>5`. len('- ""') is 5, so a hit whose text is a single char produces '- "x"' length 6 >5 and is injected — near-empty memories can pollute the prompt. Minor prompt-quality issue.
fix: Check the inner text length (len(hit text)>=N) rather than the formatted quote length.

title: _VS_RE compare gate uses len(ql.split())<=4 so 'compare NVDA vs AMD please' (5 words) skips the instant path
description: The instant keyless 'X vs Y' path requires <=4 words. 'should i compare nvda vs amd' or 'nvda versus amd today' (5+ tokens) bypass it and require the agent. Keyless users asking a slightly verbose comparison get help text instead of the side-by-side.
fix: Raise the word cap modestly (e.g. <=6) or gate on the regex match plus absence of analytical words rather than a strict token count.

title: Near-alert detection skips alerts with level exactly equal to price (dist_pct==0)
description: The near test requires `0 < dist_pct` (strictly greater than 0). An alert whose level exactly equals the current price (dist_pct==0) — the most imminent possible state — is NOT flagged as 'approaching', so the single most relevant near-alert is silently omitted.
fix: Use `0 <= dist_pct <= _NEAR_ALERT_PCT` (and symmetric for below) so an at-the-level alert counts as approaching.

title: _answer_quote volume threshold drops sub-million volume entirely
description: `if vol and vol>=1e6: parts.append('{:.1f}M shares traded')`. Legitimately low-volume names (thin small-caps) simply omit volume, and the format only ever shows millions, so a stock trading 800k shares shows no volume at all rather than '0.8M' or '800K'. Minor display gap.
fix: Show volume in K when between, e.g., 1e3 and 1e6, instead of dropping it.

title: _answer_risk crypto_pct sums weight_pct of crypto rows but weight_pct may be None for unpriced rows
description: `crypto_pct=sum(r.get('weight_pct') or 0 for r in rows if asset_type=='crypto')`. _portfolio_pulse only includes priced rows, so weight_pct is set, but the `or 0` masks any None; combined with top3 also using `or 0`, an unpriced-but-included row (shouldn't happen) would understate exposure silently. Low risk given pulse construction.
fix: No change strictly required; consider asserting weight_pct present to catch future regressions.

title: activity_snapshot sorts warmer cycles by -ts but ts may be non-numeric, raising in sort
description: `rows = sorted(cycles.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])`. If any cycle timestamp value is None or a string (corrupt warmer status), the unary minus / comparison raises TypeError. It's inside a try/except that logs and drops the whole warmer section, so one bad entry hides ALL background activity lines.
fix: Coerce/skip non-numeric ts: `key=lambda kv: -(kv[1] or 0)` and filter entries where ts isn't a number.

title: health_snapshot warmer age uses max(cycles.values()) which can include None/strings
description: `age=int(_t.time()-max(cycles.values()))`. If any cycle value is None or a string, max() raises TypeError (caught, marking warmer alive:False). One malformed cycle entry then misreports the warmer as dead even if others are fresh.
fix: Filter to numeric values before max(): `vals=[v for v in cycles.values() if isinstance(v,(int,float))]`.

title: _answer_ideas uses pool[:3] without filtering composite_score, formats score or 0 for unscored ideas
description: `top=pool[:3]; '{} (score {:.0f})'.format(r['symbol'], r.get('composite_score') or 0)`. Unlike _idea_insights which filters for composite_score is not None, this lists the first 3 pool entries regardless and prints 'score 0' for any unscored idea — misrepresenting a not-yet-scored idea as a zero-quality one.
fix: Filter pool to scored entries first (composite_score is not None) before taking the top 3, matching _idea_insights.

title: _dossier_forecast stance thresholds (>=0.55 bull, <=0.45 bear) leave a dead band but verdict ignored
description: stance derived solely from prob_up bands; ens.get('verdict')/direction is only used for the note. If the ensemble's own verdict disagrees with the prob band (e.g. prob_up 0.56 but verdict='bearish' due to magnitude), the dossier reports 'bull' contradicting the engine's verdict, double-counting noise into the consensus calc.
fix: Prefer the engine's explicit verdict/direction for stance when present, using prob bands only as a fallback, so the dossier doesn't override the engine's own call.

title: proc.stdout/stderr file handles never explicitly closed
description: The Popen object's stdout/stderr pipes are not closed (no context manager, no proc.stdout.close()). On the deadline/cancel path the process is SIGTERM'd but the pipe FDs leak until GC. Under repeated cancelled streaming requests this leaks file descriptors.
fix: After proc.wait()/_terminate(), close the pipes in a finally: for h in (proc.stdin, proc.stdout, proc.stderr): try: h and h.close() except Exception: pass.

title: Broad except swallows BrokenPipe on stdin write with no fallback
description: proc.stdin.write(prompt) is wrapped in a bare except that silently passes. If the write fails (e.g. claude exited immediately), the prompt is never delivered but the loop still runs to the deadline waiting for output that will never come, wasting up to _RUN_DEADLINE seconds before returning None.
fix: On stdin write failure, terminate and return None immediately rather than entering the read loop: except Exception: _terminate(); return None (after defining _terminate earlier, or set a flag).

title: Digest file written without encoding; non-ASCII insight text can raise/garble on some locales
description: open(path, 'w') uses the platform default encoding. The digest text contains smart punctuation (…, —, curly quotes from other modules) and possibly non-ASCII tickers/names; on a system whose default is not UTF-8 (e.g. cp1252) writing these raises UnicodeEncodeError (caught, so the file silently isn't written) or mojibake.
fix: open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') to make the markdown drop deterministic across locales.

title: sendmail splits cfg['to'] on comma but MIME 'To' header set to raw cfg['to'] only once
description: msg['To']=cfg['to'] (the raw comma string) is fine for display, and sendmail recipients are split on ',' — but addresses with display names containing commas ('Doe, John <j@x>') will be mis-split into invalid recipients. Edge case for multi-recipient configs.
fix: Parse recipients with email.utils.getaddresses([cfg['to']]) and pass the extracted addresses to sendmail, rather than a naive split(',').

title: Serial fallback uses generator unpacking that re-raises if any thunk raises
description: else branch: regime, sectors_res, liquidity, crypto = (t() for t in thunks). Each thunk already guards internally and returns None on error, so this is safe — BUT if safe_executor is None AND a thunk's internal try/except somehow lets an exception through (e.g. a non-Exception BaseException), the generator unpacking aborts macro_brief entirely. Low risk since thunks catch Exception broadly.
fix: Acceptable as-is; if hardening desired, wrap: results = [t() for t in thunks] inside its own try, defaulting any to None. No behavior change otherwise.

title: crypto mcap_change format guarded by chg is not None but expansion check uses (chg or 0)
description: 'expanding' if (chg or 0) > 0 else 'contracting' — when chg is exactly 0 it reads 'contracting' (defensible), but when chg is None it also reads 'contracting' even though the parenthetical correctly omits the %. So with dominance present but mcap_change_24h missing, the narrative asserts 'contracting' with no evidence.
fix: Only assert direction when chg is not None: word = 'expanding' if chg and chg>0 else ('contracting' if chg is not None and chg<0 else 'mixed'); or omit the expanding/contracting clause entirely when chg is None.

title: EDGAR non-200 envelope returns 'note' twice-keyed risk and ignores 429 Retry-After
description: On status != 200 it returns an error note but doesn't read Retry-After, so the cache layer may immediately retry and re-throttle. Also r.json() at line 200 is only reached on 200, fine; but a 200 with non-JSON body raises ValueError inside the try and is caught generically as sec_unavailable — acceptable. The main gap: no handling of the SEC 429 backoff the comment explicitly worries about.
fix: On r.status_code==429, optionally surface Retry-After in the note; ensure the 'error' key reliably prevents long TTL caching of the throttle (it does via cache_store negative guard).

title: recall breaks on first below-threshold score but NaN scores never break, can append all rows
description: for i in order: s=float(scores[i]); if s<MIN_SCORE: break. If any score is NaN (truncated/corrupt vector that still matched dim), the comparison NaN<MIN_SCORE is False, so the break never fires for that element and the loop continues appending up to k rows that may be irrelevant, surfacing junk recall.
fix: Skip non-finite scores: if not math.isfinite(s): continue; and keep the break for genuine below-threshold values. Or filter NaN out of scores before sorting.

title: portfolio_correlation least_correlated slice pairs[-5:][::-1] overlaps most_correlated when <10 pairs
description: With fewer than 10 pairs (e.g. 3 symbols → 3 pairs), most_correlated=pairs[:5] and least_correlated=pairs[-5:][::-1] overlap heavily, reporting the same pairs as both most and least correlated, which is confusing/contradictory to the LLM and user.
fix: When len(pairs)<=5, report a single sorted list (or dedupe so a pair never appears in both buckets).

title: portfolio_risk skips sentinel keys starting with '_' but per dict could be empty leaving per={} with no error
description: If every symbol's metrics dict is empty/non-dict, the loop skips all, returning {'period':..., 'per_symbol':{}} with no error and no note. The LLM then sees an empty per_symbol and may assert 'no risk data' or fabricate. A more honest empty-result note is warranted.
fix: After the loop, if not per, return {'note':'risk metrics unavailable for current holdings'} instead of an empty per_symbol.

title: _quote_symbol only suffixes -USD for crypto held in portfolio, missing crypto on watchlist-only queries
description: _quote_symbol maps SYM→SYM-USD only when the symbol is a CRYPTO holding in the portfolio. A user asking get_quote/news for a crypto they only watch (not hold), e.g. 'price of DOGE', gets the bare DOGE quote which 404s or returns an unrelated equity, defeating the mapping's intent.
fix: Also consult the watchlist (or a known-crypto set) so watched-but-unheld crypto symbols are suffixed; or accept an explicit asset_type hint.

title: _t_agent_positions count uses d.get('count') which may diverge from len(rows) after [:30] slice
description: The tool returns count=d.get('count') (full count) but positions list is capped at rows[:30]. The LLM sees count=N but only 30 rows; for >30 positions it may reason about positions it can't see and the total_market_value still reflects all — generally fine, but there's no 'truncated' flag, so the model can't tell the list is partial.
fix: Add a 'positions_truncated': len(rows)>30 flag so the model knows the list is capped.

title: _safe_int_local clamps non-positive to default but allows arbitrarily large limit (no upper cap)
description: _safe_int_local returns n if n>0 else default, with NO maximum. _t_agent_activity passes this straight into 'LIMIT ?' on aj_proposals/aj_orders. A model sending limit=100000 issues two large unbounded queries, and the tool description claims max 25 but the code doesn't enforce it.
fix: Clamp the upper bound: `return min(n,25) if n>0 else default`, matching the documented max.

title: _crypto_symbols subscripts h['symbol'] which can KeyError despite the asset_type guard
description: {h['symbol'].upper() for h in db.get_portfolio() if h.get('asset_type')=='crypto' and h.get('symbol')}. The set comprehension's filter requires h.get('symbol') truthy, so h['symbol'] subscript is safe at runtime — but if get_portfolio yields a row where 'symbol' is present-but-None it's filtered out (None falsy). OK. The actual risk: db.get_portfolio() raising is caught, but a single row that is not a dict (e.g. a tuple) makes h.get raise AttributeError, caught by the broad except and silently returns empty set, disabling all crypto -USD mapping for the cycle.
fix: Guard row type: if isinstance(h,dict) inside the comprehension, so one malformed row doesn't blank the entire crypto set.

title: compute_stress_score cache read can miss because inner writes a different code path
description: compute_stress_score() reads cache key 'stress_score' then calls _compute_stress_score_inner() which recomputes everything and writes 'stress_score'. The outer function never caches its own successful return beyond what inner writes, and on exception returns an uncached error dict. That's acceptable, but the inner function is invoked on every call until it populates the cache, and two concurrent first-callers both run the full 6-indicator fan-out (no coalescing), doubling upstream load.
fix: Add in-flight coalescing (single computation shared by concurrent callers) similar to smart_money.compute_score.

title: Trend-to-probability mapping divides rescaled fp20 by 20 — double-shrinks the trend vote
description: fp20 = fp*20/30 then p = 0.5 + clip(fp20/20, -0.4, 0.4). The /20 maps a 20% move to ±0.4, but fp was already rescaled from 30d to 20d. The comment claims this prevents over-weighting, but combined with the 0.30 composite weight the trend channel is shrunk twice (horizon rescale AND the /20 saturation tuned for 30d magnitudes), systematically under-counting trend.
fix: Pick one normalization: either rescale horizon (fp20) and map with a 20d-appropriate divisor, or keep fp at 30d and map with /20; don't apply the 30→20 rescale and then a divisor calibrated for the original 30d scale.

title: Bollinger/zscore use bb_std.replace(0, np.nan) but a near-constant window yields huge ratios, not just zeros
description: bb_width and bb_position guard only EXACT zero std via replace(0, np.nan). A near-zero (but nonzero) 20-day std on a nearly-flat instrument produces enormous bb_width/zscore_20 outliers that survive into the RF feature matrix and StandardScaler, distorting scaling and predictions. The exact-zero guard misses the dominant near-degenerate case.
fix: Floor the denominator instead of only nan-ing exact zeros, e.g. divide by `bb_std.where(bb_std > eps)` with a small eps relative to price, or winsorize the resulting feature columns before scaling.

title: max(buckets, key=buckets.get) tie-breaking is arbitrary, not the documented bucket order
description: _build_window picks the dominant bucket via `max(buckets, key=buckets.get)`. On ties, Python's max returns the first key in dict-iteration order, which is insertion order of the window's articles — NOT the _BUCKET_ORDER the module documents for tie-breaking. So the displayed dominant narrative on ties depends on article arrival order, making phase detection non-deterministic across runs.
fix: Break ties deterministically: `dominant = max(buckets, key=lambda b:(buckets[b], -_BUCKET_ORDER.index(b) if b in _BUCKET_ORDER else -99))` or iterate _BUCKET_ORDER explicitly.

title: get_top_movers().get('gainers') assumes movers is a dict; bare except swallows AttributeError but loses momentum universe silently
description: `movers = fetcher.get_top_movers(); for g in (movers.get('gainers',[]) or [])`. If get_top_movers returns None, movers.get raises AttributeError, caught by the broad except → momentum universe silently empty. For the momentum strategy this can leave base=[] (momentum builds dynamically) plus no gainers = empty equity pool → scan returns nothing for momentum.
fix: Guard: `movers = fetcher.get_top_movers() or {}` before .get, so a None response degrades to no-gainers rather than silently aborting the whole momentum injection.

title: Sharpe annualization treats per-bar pnl (incl. zeros during flat) as daily returns
description: Sharpe is mean/std * sqrt(252) over pnl_by_bar, which includes 0.0 on every flat day. Padding with zeros deflates both mean and std but not symmetrically (zeros pull std down more relative to a sparse signal), so the annualized Sharpe of a signal that is only occasionally in the market is inflated/distorted versus a true position-time-weighted Sharpe. The docstring acknowledges zeros 'lower vol' but the resulting number isn't a defensible strategy Sharpe.
fix: Compute Sharpe over in-market bars only (pnl where position!=0) or annualize using the fraction of time in market, and document the convention; at minimum expose n in-market bars so the number is interpretable.

title: horizon_override truthiness drops a legitimate horizon of 0 is impossible but negative override ignored
description: horizon = int(horizon_override if horizon_override else out.get('horizon_days',20)). If horizon_override is 0 it is falsy and the signal's horizon is used (0 is invalid anyway, clamped later). But a negative horizon_override (e.g. -1 from a bad API param) is truthy, becomes horizon, then clamped to 1 at line 550 — so a nonsense override silently forces 1-day horizon across the whole backtest rather than being rejected.
fix: Validate horizon_override up front in run_backtest: ignore non-positive overrides (`horizon_override = horizon_override if (horizon_override and horizon_override>0) else None`).

title: Abnormal-return curve mixes per-event NaN benchmark rows into a uniform-weight mean
description: bench_curves stores np.full(NaN) for events lacking a benchmark window, then bench_avg = np.nanmean(bench_arr, axis=0). If only some events have benchmark coverage, the symbol average curve (avg, computed over all events) is differenced against a benchmark average computed over a different subset of events, so abnormal = avg - bench_avg compares non-matching event populations.
fix: Compute abnormal only over events that have BOTH symbol and benchmark windows (mask rows where any benchmark value is NaN), or compute bench_avg over the same event mask used for avg, so the abnormal curve is a like-for-like difference.

title: post_idx clamps to last column so 'post_event_5d' silently measures fewer days for small windows
description: post_idx = min(t0+5, curves.shape[1]-1). For window_days < 5 (allowed: event_study clamps window_days to >=1), t0+5 exceeds the curve, post_idx becomes the last index, and avg_post_event_5d_pct is actually a 'post-window-end' figure mislabeled as 5-day. The summary field name promises 5 days but delivers fewer without flagging.
fix: Return None (or a clearly-named field) for avg_post_event_5d_pct when window_days < 5, since the 5-day post window isn't fully observed.

title: R-squared can be negative but is reported without bound; not clamped
description: r2 = 1 - ss_res/ss_tot. With an intercept-included OLS via lstsq this is normally in [0,1], but because alpha is estimated on EXCESS returns and ss_tot is computed on the demeaned y, a poorly-fitting regression can yield a small negative R² which is then round()'d and surfaced as r_squared. A negative R² in the UI is confusing and, for portfolio_factor_exposure where it feeds downstream displays, may be misinterpreted.
fix: If a [0,1] R² is intended for display, clamp: `r2 = max(0.0, 1.0 - ss_res/ss_tot)`; otherwise document that negative values indicate worse-than-mean fit.
