title: Idiosyncratic-vol residuals recomputed with a second alignment that may differ from the regression's
description: After _regress returns coef, factor_exposure re-iterates stock_dates/stock_ret against fac_index to rebuild residuals for idio vol. If the factor frame contains a date present here but the original _regress alignment dropped it (it shouldn't, same loop), the residual set could differ in size from the regression's n, making idio_vol slightly inconsistent with r2/coef. The duplication is fragile and wasteful.
fix: Have _regress return the residual array (it already computes resid in _ols) and reuse it for idio_vol instead of recomputing, guaranteeing consistency and avoiding the second alignment pass.

title: AI daily-cap check and counter use private ai_summarizer internals via getattr/attribute access
description: _call_openai references ai_summarizer._cap_exceeded and ai_summarizer._record_ai_call (private, underscore-prefixed). If those internals are renamed/removed the cap silently stops being enforced (the getattr default lambda returns False so calls proceed un-capped), and _record_ai_call failure is swallowed — the shared budget could be bypassed, defeating the daily cost cap.
fix: Depend on a public API from ai_summarizer (e.g. a documented check_and_record() helper) or, if none exists, log.warning when the private symbols are missing so an unenforced cap is visible rather than silent.

title: Zero issued price check uses float(issued)==0 but negative prices not handled
description: score_hypothesis invalidates when float(issued)==0 to avoid divide-by-zero, but a negative issued price (corrupt data) passes the check and yields a nonsensical realized_pct with inverted sign at line 634 (dividing by a negative entry flips the meaning of UP/DOWN).
fix: Guard for non-positive: `if not (float(issued) > 0):` invalidate, covering 0 and negative/NaN entry prices uniformly.

title: sec_edgar.get_recent_filings called with positional (symbol, None, 5) assuming a fixed signature
description: _safe_call('filings', sec_edgar.get_recent_filings, symbol, None, 5) passes three positional args. If get_recent_filings's signature differs (e.g. (symbol, form_type=None, limit=5) vs (symbol, limit=5)), the None/5 land on the wrong parameters and either error (swallowed by _safe_call → blank filings) or silently filter by a wrong form. The context block then quietly omits filings.
fix: Call with keyword args matching the real signature, e.g. sec_edgar.get_recent_filings(symbol, limit=5), so an argument-order mismatch can't silently blank the filings context.

title: Finite-difference step h assumes uniform grid; raw (smooth=False) path uses non-uniform strikes
description: In _density_from_calls when smooth=False (or spline failed), grid = raw strikes which are NOT uniformly spaced (e.g. $1 near ATM, $5 in wings). h is taken as grid[1]-grid[0] (the first spacing) and used as the constant denominator for the centered second difference across the whole array. On a non-uniform grid this produces an incorrect d2C/dK2 and therefore a wrong density. The trapz renorm hides scale errors but the shape is distorted.
fix: On the raw/non-uniform path, either re-grid onto a uniform grid via np.interp before differencing, or use np.gradient(np.gradient(C_grid, grid), grid) which respects non-uniform spacing, instead of a constant h.

title: Deep-ITM time-value filter keeps OTM by strike>=spot but uses raw mid without discounting intrinsic for ITM correctly
description: intrinsic = max(spot - strike, 0); time_val = mid - intrinsic. The no-arb intrinsic for a call is S - K·e^(-rT), not S - K. Using undiscounted intrinsic understates intrinsic for ITM strikes, so time_val is overstated and some genuinely deep-ITM (low-information) strikes survive the tv_floor filter, reintroducing the very curvature noise the filter was meant to remove.
fix: Use discounted strike: intrinsic = max(spot - strike*math.exp(-r*T), 0.0) when computing time_val, consistent with the Breeden-Litzenberger discounting used elsewhere in the module.

title: prob_of_target echoes unclamped horizon_days in the response
description: simulate path clamps horizon_days to [1, _MAX_HORIZON] before simulating, but prob_of_target returns the raw caller-supplied horizon_days in the output dict (line 222) rather than the clamped value actually used (sim ran with the clamped value). For an out-of-range horizon the reported horizon_days disagrees with the simulation that produced the probabilities.
fix: Return the clamped horizon used: capture `hd = int(max(1, min(horizon_days, _MAX_HORIZON)))` once, pass it to _simulate_uncached, and put `hd` in the response instead of the raw horizon_days.

title: terminal std uses ddof=1 guarded by len>1 but percentile/mean unguarded for n_paths floor
description: n_paths is floored at 100 so terminal always has >1 element in practice, but _summarize is also reachable via prob_of_target with a possibly tiny path set if _MAX_PATHS logic changed; std(ddof=1) on a single path would divide by zero (numpy returns NaN with a warning). The len(terminal)>1 guard handles std, but np.percentile on a 1-element array is fine. Low risk given current floors but the guard coupling is fragile.
fix: No behavioral change needed today, but assert/clamp n_paths>=2 at the _simulate_uncached boundary so summarize's statistics are always well-defined regardless of caller path.

title: h60 expected_return sign derived from tanh-blended direction but prob_up clipped asymmetrically can disagree
description: direction = 0.6*tanh(cross*15)+0.4*tanh(roc60*3); prob_up = clip(0.5+direction*0.25, .05,.95); expected_pct = direction*vol*... When direction is tiny-positive but clipping/rounding pushes prob_up to exactly 0.5 region, expected_return_pct can be a small positive while prob_up rounds to 0.5 (NEUTRAL), creating an internally inconsistent horizon row (neutral probability, non-zero expected return) that the consensus/divergence logic may read inconsistently.
fix: Derive expected_pct sign from (prob_up-0.5) like _h5 does, or zero out expected_pct when round(prob_up,3)==0.5, ensuring probability and expected return never disagree in sign.

title: target_return default to mean(mean) can be infeasible under box constraints, optimizer falls back to w0
description: For objective target_return with no explicit target, target defaults to np.mean(mean) (the unweighted average asset return). Under tight max_weight bounds the equality constraint w·mean==target may be infeasible, SLSQP fails, and markowitz_optimize silently returns w0 with converged=False. The user asked for a target-return portfolio and gets the naive start point with no explanation of infeasibility.
fix: When res.success is False for target_return/target_vol, surface a clear note in the response (e.g. add 'warning':'target infeasible under constraints; returning feasible start') rather than only converged=False, so the UI can explain the fallback.

title: compare_to_point linearly rescales a 30d trend point to horizon by ×h/30, ignoring compounding
description: point_scaled = forecast_pct * (horizon_days/30). Scaling a percentage return linearly across horizons ignores compounding and the sqrt-time nature of dispersion; for horizon_days far from 30 (e.g. 120) this overstates the point estimate roughly linearly while the bootstrap median grows sub-linearly, inflating spread_vs_median_pct.
fix: Rescale in log/compounded space: `point_scaled = ((1+fp/100)**(h/30) - 1)*100`, or document that the linear scaling is a first-order approximation valid only near h=30.

title: hit values summed assuming 0/1 ints but column can be NULL filtered only partially
description: _stats_for_rows sums r['hit'] over directional rows where hit is not None — fine. But last_100 = directional[-100:] then sums r['hit']; directional already excludes None hits, so OK. The avg/Sharpe uses ALL scored rows' realized_return including NEUTRAL calls (intended). The subtle bug: returns list includes realized_return for rows that may have hit None but realized_return present; Sharpe-of-signal-returns then mixes directional and neutral returns, which can misrepresent the signal's tradeable performance (a NEUTRAL call's return shouldn't count toward the signal's realized Sharpe).
fix: If Sharpe is meant to reflect tradeable signal performance, compute avg/Sharpe over directional rows only (or sign-adjust by predicted direction). At minimum document that avg_return/Sharpe include non-directional rows so the badge isn't misread.

title: log_ml_forecast stores magnitude as forecast_pct/100 but comment says forecast_pct already in percent
description: magnitude = trend.get('forecast_pct'); then magnitude = magnitude/100.0 with comment 'forecast_pct is already in percent'. Dividing a percent (e.g. 5.0 meaning 5%) by 100 yields 0.05 (a decimal fraction), which is the intended decimal magnitude — but other hooks (log_smart_money etc.) pass magnitude=None and the ensemble passes magnitude already as a decimal. The unit of predicted_magnitude is therefore inconsistent across signals (some decimal, some None), and any consumer comparing magnitudes across signals will be wrong.
fix: Standardize predicted_magnitude units across all hooks (store decimal fraction everywhere, as done here) and ensure every producer follows the same convention; document the unit in the schema comment.

title: 13F pct_of_portfolio divides by total that can include misclassified values
description: value_usd is derived by a thousands-vs-dollars heuristic per holding; when holdings mix correctly- and incorrectly-scaled values, the per-holding pct_of_portfolio is computed against a `total_value` that can be off by 1000x for some rows, skewing displayed weights. total_value==0 is guarded, so no ZeroDivisionError, but the percentages can be materially wrong.
fix: Apply one consistent scale decision per filing (e.g. majority vote across holdings) rather than independently per holding before summing total_value.

title: CIK fallback hits a non-existent EDGAR full-text endpoint
description: The fallback builds `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?...` but the documented EDGAR full-text search endpoint is `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index` is not a real path (the public endpoint is `/LATEST/search-index` vs the actual `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index` → it should be `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index`). In practice this URL 404s, so the fallback never resolves a CIK and just wastes a request before negative-caching.
fix: Use the real EDGAR FTS endpoint `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=...&forms=10-K` is incorrect; query `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index` is not public — switch to `https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar` company search or the FTS UI endpoint `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index` replacement `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index`. Concretely, call `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22TICKER%22` -> use `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index` documented as `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index`; verify against EDGAR FTS and correct the path.

title: Insider buy/sell counting uses codes that sec_edgar never emits
description: _score_insiders counts buys/sells by matching transaction_type in ('P','A','BUY','PURCHASE') and ('S','D','SELL','SALE'). sec_edgar normalizes open-market actions to 'BUY'/'SELL' and tags everything else 'OTHER:<code>', so the 'P','A','D','PURCHASE','SALE' branches are dead. 'BUY'/'SELL' still match so totals are roughly right, but 'A' (award) inclusion would have been wrong anyway — the dead codes mask intent and could silently break if normalization changes.
fix: Match only the normalized values: buys = transaction_type=='BUY', sells = transaction_type=='SELL'.

title: Synthetic-insider total channels reads non-existent key
description: The KPI shows `convergence + '/' + totalChannels` where totalChannels = data.total_channels || 6. compute_composite never returns `total_channels`, so it always falls back to 6. It's correct (there are 6 channels) but brittle — if channel count changes server-side the UI won't follow.
fix: Derive the denominator from the channels object length (`Object.keys(data.channels||{}).length || 6`).

title: Congress heatmap opacity can exceed 1.0
description: opacity is `Math.max(0.4, Math.min(1.0, t.total_trades/top)) + 0.1`, so the clamped value (up to 1.0) has 0.1 added, yielding up to 1.1. CSS clamps >1 to 1 so it's harmless visually, but the +0.1 defeats the Math.min(1.0,...) clamp's intent and the most-traded ticker and several others all render at full opacity indistinguishably.
fix: Apply the +0.1 before clamping: `Math.min(1.0, Math.max(0.4, ratio) + 0.1)`.

title: options_skew PCR uses float('inf') when call OI/vol is 0, then compares inf<0.70 (False) / inf>1.30 (True) — bearish always fires on zero-call chains
description: pcr_oi=inf when call_oi==0. For a bearish scan `pcr_oi>1.30` is True, firing the options_skew source purely because there were zero call contracts (often a data gap, not genuine put dominance). This manufactures a bearish signal from missing call data.
fix: When call_oi==0 (or call_vol==0) treat PCR as unknown and do not fire (return no-data) rather than +inf, unless put_oi is itself meaningfully large.

title: Congress signal saturates at ±$100k but the loop already applied a 60d cutoff inconsistently (string dates unfiltered), so net may include stale trades
description: Compounding the date-format bug above: because string-form txn_dt rows skip the cutoff (parse fails), the net summed at line 424-430 can include >60d trades, then saturated to ±1 at $100k. The normalized contribution can be driven by trades outside the intended window.
fix: Fix the date parsing (see the txn_dt finding) so only ≤60d trades feed net before saturation.

title: _options_pcr assigns pcr=5.0 sentinel when call_vol==0, producing a fixed -1 norm regardless of actual put volume
description: When call_vol==0, pcr is hard-set to 5.0 → norm=_clamp((1-5)/0.5)=-1.0 (max bearish) even if put volume is tiny. A near-empty chain with a few puts and no calls is read as maximal bearish skew, polluting the narrative_vs_options divergence pair.
fix: Require a minimum call_vol before computing PCR; if call_vol==0 return None (skip the pair) instead of the 5.0 sentinel.

title: OpenAI client created per-call with key; key resolved from env/ai_summarizer and embedded — fine, but full prompt (incl. raw pattern + analogs) logged on json.loads failure path is benign; no key leak. Flagging temperature/max_tokens hardcode only
description: Low-risk: _call_llm builds an OpenAI client each call (no reuse) and on any exception returns the exception string in the error envelope, which could include API error detail (not the key). Minor: repeated client construction per request adds latency; no secret leakage.
fix: Optionally cache the OpenAI client; ensure error strings returned to the UI are sanitized (they currently embed str(e)).

title: portfolio market_beta reported as None when mkt_beta missing but iqr/best/worst still scaled by scale=1.0 silently
description: When exposures lack 'Mkt-RF' beta, scale defaults to 1.0 but market_beta is reported None. The IQR/best/worst are then scaled by 1.0 and presented as if beta-adjusted, while the UI sees market_beta:None — a mild inconsistency where the bracket claims to be beta-scaled but isn't.
fix: Either report market_beta as 1.0 when defaulting (so the scaling is transparent) or skip scaling/labeling when beta is unavailable.

title: _m_insider_form4_net_60d returns 0.0 vs None inconsistency when net is non-zero but seen_any False is impossible
description: `return round(net/1e6,3) if seen_any or net != 0.0 else 0.0` — if seen_any is False then net is 0.0, so the condition reduces to `False or False` → returns 0.0; if seen_any True returns the rounded net. The `net != 0.0` term is dead (net can't be nonzero without seen_any True). Harmless but the intent (distinguish 'no filings' None vs '0 net' 0.0) is not achieved — it always returns 0.0 for the no-data case rather than None, so 'unknown' and 'flat' collapse, contradicting the docstring which says 0 should rank differently from None.
fix: Return None when not seen_any (no Form-4s in window) and 0.0 only when seen_any and net==0; i.e. `return None if not seen_any else round(net/1e6,3)`.

title: sector parallel_map imports safe_executor inside _compute and spawns 11 workers; per-sector fetches open thread-local connections never closed in this module
description: Unlike idea_pool_warmer which wraps workers to close thread-local sqlite/cache connections, sectorflow's per-sector worker (_build_sector_row) calls narrative/finviz/fetcher which may open thread-local DB/cache handles on its daemon threads; these aren't closed, leaking handles across repeated scans (every 10min TTL).
fix: Wrap the per-sector worker to close thread-local connections (db.close_thread_conn / cache_store.close_thread_conn) in a finally, mirroring idea_pool_warmer._warm_one_with_cleanup.

title: Volume-anomaly 5d/20d ratio uses inconsistent denominators on short history
description: avg_5 divides by a hard 5.0 while avg_20 divides by `max(len(volumes[-20:]),1)`. With fewer than 20 (but >=5) volumes, avg_20 averages over <20 bars, so the 5d/20d 'ratio' compares a 5-bar mean to an N-bar mean (N<20), biasing the ratio and the resulting anomaly score for newly listed names.
fix: Require len(volumes)>=20 for the ratio (or divide avg_5 by len(volumes[-5:])) so the windows are comparable.

title: add_alert raises 500 on a non-string symbol via .upper()
description: symbol = (data.get("symbol", "") or "").upper().strip() only coerces falsy values to "". If the client sends a JSON number for symbol (e.g. {"symbol": 123, ...}), data.get returns the int 123, (123 or "") evaluates to 123, and 123.upper() raises AttributeError, which escapes the route as an uncaught 500 instead of a clean 400. Every other validated route either guards isinstance(...) or runs _valid_ticker first; this one calls .upper() before any type/format check.
fix: Guard the type before string ops: replace the line with `sym_raw = data.get("symbol", ""); symbol = sym_raw.strip().upper() if isinstance(sym_raw, str) else ""`. The existing `if not symbol ...` check at line 1228 then returns the correct 400.

title: get_portfolio silently drops a position from totals when its live price is 0 or missing (no cost-basis fallback)
description: Under `if current_price:` a holding whose live quote is exactly 0.0 OR missing (None) receives no enrichment keys AND is excluded from both total_value and total_cost. Unlike stress_test (line 1381), portfolio_dividends (line 1305), and portfolio_ai_analysis (line 1477) — which all fall back to avg_cost when the price is missing and treat a real 0 as valid — get_portfolio neither falls back nor counts the cost basis. A single transiently-missing quote therefore makes that position vanish from the headline summary, understating total_value/total_cost/num-positions-weighted P&L and producing an inconsistent portfolio total versus the other routes.
fix: Mirror the other routes: compute `cur = current_price if current_price is not None else h["avg_cost"]` and use `cur` for market_value, always accumulating into total_value/total_cost and emitting the enrichment keys (gating only live-price-specific fields like day_change on `current_price is not None`).

title: Snapshot alert check does TypeError comparison when a stored alert price is None
description: In the snapshot worker, `cur >= alert["price"]` / `cur <= alert["price"]` are evaluated whenever cur is not None, but alert["price"] itself is never None-guarded. add_alert now rejects null prices, but legacy/imported rows (or a price_alerts row created before the validation existed) can hold NULL, and in Python 3 `float >= None` raises TypeError. The surrounding try/except logs and aborts the entire alert phase for that cycle, so one bad row disables all alert evaluation every 5 minutes.
fix: Add a guard before the comparison: `ap = alert["price"]; if ap is None: continue` (right after the `if cur is None: continue` at line 360), so a null-priced alert is skipped instead of throwing.

title: portfolio_ai_analysis emits day_change_pct without the change-present gating applied in get_portfolio
description: get_portfolio was deliberately fixed (line 591) so day_change_pct is None whenever the absolute day change is None, to avoid showing a percent move beside a null P&L. portfolio_ai_analysis builds the same per-position payload but passes `day_change_pct: q.get("change_pct")` ungated, so a position with a percent but no absolute change (or vice-versa) is sent to the AI model and UI inconsistently, contradicting the documented invariant and potentially feeding the model a percent with no corresponding move.
fix: Read the change once and gate the percent: `chg = q.get("change")` then `"day_change_pct": q.get("change_pct") if chg is not None else None`, matching get_portfolio.

title: update_settings validates API-key format with re.match, accepting keys with trailing garbage
description: Sensitive provider keys are validated with `re.match(fmt, key.strip())`. re.match only anchors at the start, not the end, so a value whose valid prefix matches but which has extra trailing characters (e.g. 'sk-validprefix...<newline-injected junk>' on a multiline string, or 'sk-...; rm') passes the gate and is persisted. This can flip _llm_available() true for a malformed key and store unexpected content, defeating the stated purpose of the format gate (reject typos before call time).
fix: Use a fully anchored match: `re.fullmatch(fmt, key.strip())` (or ensure each provider fmt ends with `$`). This rejects keys with trailing junk while accepting genuine keys.

title: portfolio_export writes account_type column from the wrong key (acct_type) and may export blank
description: The export header declares an 'account_type' column but the value is read as `h.get("acct_type", "")`. The account_name on the same row is read as `h.get("account_name", "")`. If db.get_portfolio joins the account table as 'account_type' (matching the export semantics) rather than 'acct_type', the exported account_type column is always blank, silently losing account-type data on every export/round-trip. At minimum the two keys are inconsistent (account_name vs acct_type) suggesting one is wrong.
fix: Confirm the joined column name in database.get_portfolio and use it consistently, e.g. `h.get("account_type") or h.get("acct_type", "")` so the export populates regardless of which alias the query returns.

title: _portfolio_live_prices raises TypeError when a crypto holding's symbol is None
description: For crypto holdings the function computes `key = (sym + "-USD").upper()` and earlier builds `[s + "-USD" for s in crypto_syms]`. A corrupt holding with asset_type 'crypto' but symbol None (or non-string) makes `None + "-USD"` raise TypeError, which propagates and 500s every route that prices the portfolio (get_portfolio, stress_test, ai-analysis, dividends, analytics). The stock branch tolerates this slightly better but the crypto concatenation is unconditional.
fix: Filter to string symbols when building the crypto query/key: `crypto_syms = [h["symbol"] for h in holdings if h.get("asset_type") == "crypto" and isinstance(h.get("symbol"), str)]`, and likewise skip non-str in the stock list.

title: portfolio_dividends monthly_income assumes uniform 1/12 split, misrepresenting quarterly/annual payers
description: monthly_income = total_annual_income / 12 is presented as a 'Monthly income estimate'. Combined with annual_income derived from div_rate (an annual figure) this is only correct for monthly-paying instruments; for the typical quarterly U.S. equity it implies smooth monthly cash flow that never actually occurs, and for special/annual dividends it is materially wrong. The summary surfaces it as if it were an actual cadence figure.
fix: Either relabel the field as an averaged estimate explicitly, or weight by each holding's known pay frequency when div_data provides one (e.g. use div_data.get("frequency")); at minimum document that it is annual/12 averaging so the UI does not present it as scheduled monthly income.

title: chart route truthiness check skips indicators for valid-but-empty-container chart payloads and may pass non-list
description: `indicators = fetcher.compute_indicators(data) if data else {}` gates on truthiness of data. If get_chart_data returns a dict envelope like {"candles": [...], "meta": {...}} it is always truthy even when candles are empty (compute_indicators then runs on no candles); conversely if it returns an empty list on a delisted symbol, indicators are skipped — but the response still returns data as-is, so the front-end receives a 200 with empty data and silently no indicators, with no signal distinguishing 'no data' from 'error'.
fix: Make the empty/failed case explicit, e.g. `if not data: return jsonify({"symbol": symbol.upper(), "data": [], "indicators": {}, "error": "no data"}), 200` (or 404), and only compute indicators when data has actual candles.

title: get_alerts builds the quote batch from a.['symbol'] without guarding non-string/None alert symbols
description: `symbols = list({a["symbol"] for a in alerts})` and `q = prices.get(a["symbol"], {})` assume every alert row has a hashable string symbol. A legacy row with a NULL symbol becomes None in the set (hashable, but get_quotes_batch may then choke or .upper() inside fetcher fails), and any non-string would break fetcher's symbol normalization. There is no _valid_ticker/None filter here as there is on write paths.
fix: Filter when constructing the batch: `symbols = list({a["symbol"] for a in alerts if isinstance(a.get("symbol"), str) and a["symbol"]})`, leaving distance_pct None for rows whose symbol cannot be priced.

title: portfolio_import accepts a symbol shape that _valid_ticker would reject, bypassing the app-wide ticker gate
description: Import validates symbols against an inline regex `^[A-Z0-9.\-]{1,10}$` instead of the module's _valid_ticker / _TICKER_RE (`^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9.\-]{0,9}$`). The inline regex permits a symbol starting with '.' or '-' (e.g. '.AB', '-X') which _valid_ticker forbids, so imported positions can carry symbols that every other route considers invalid, later failing quote lookups or _valid_ticker-guarded operations and effectively un-editable via the validated PUT path.
fix: Reuse the canonical validator: replace the inline `re.match(r"^[A-Z0-9.\-]{1,10}$", symbol)` check with `_valid_ticker(symbol)` so import enforces the same ticker shape as the rest of the app.

title: alt_reddit_sub injects unvalidated subreddit and sort path segments into an outbound URL (SSRF/path injection)
description: The <subreddit> path param and the `sort` query param are passed straight into reddit_subreddit_posts, which builds `https://www.reddit.com/r/{subreddit}/{sort}.json` via f-string with NO validation. Unlike every sibling route that calls _valid_ticker, this route validates nothing. A crafted subreddit/sort (e.g. containing '..', '@', or extra path segments) can rewrite the request path or host portion of the upstream URL, enabling request smuggling / SSRF-style redirection of the server's outbound fetch. The route is reachable as GET /api/alt-data/reddit/<anything>.
fix: Restrict both inputs before the downstream call: `if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,30}', subreddit): return jsonify({"error": "invalid subreddit"}), 400` and `sort = request.args.get('sort', 'hot'); if sort not in ('hot','new','top','rising'): sort='hot'`.

title: ideas_enrich does not validate the symbol before calling symbol.upper() / enrich_idea
description: Every other per-symbol route in this range guards with `if not _valid_ticker(symbol): return 400`. ideas_enrich skips this and passes symbol.upper() directly to idea_generator.enrich_idea, which fetches quotes/fundamentals for that ticker. An attacker-controlled or malformed symbol (URL-encoded path, very long string, injection characters) flows unchecked into downstream HTTP fetches and cache keys, and the route returns a generic 500 instead of a clean 400 for obviously-bad input.
fix: Add at the top of the route, after computing symbol from the path: `if not _valid_ticker(symbol): return jsonify({"error": "Invalid symbol"}), 400` before symbol.upper() is used.

title: crypto_yields limit is unclamped — negative limit drops rows, zero returns empty
description: limit = _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 20) is passed unclamped to ds.defillama_top_yields(limit), which slices `pools[:limit]`. A negative limit (e.g. ?limit=-1) becomes a Python negative slice that silently drops the last row(s) and reorders the user's intent, and ?limit=0 returns an empty list with no error. Sibling routes in this same file (scanner_watchlist, congress_senate, etc.) were already hardened with max(1, ...); this one was missed.
fix: Clamp like the sibling routes: `limit = max(1, _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 20))`.

title: screener_universe limit is unclamped and passed to financedb_filter
description: limit=_safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 200) is forwarded directly to ds.financedb_filter as the result cap with no lower/upper bound. A negative value produces a negative slice (truncating from the end / empty results) and an arbitrarily large value can force the screener to materialize the entire universe, pegging the request thread. This is the same unclamped-limit class already flagged for other routes but not for screener_universe.
fix: Clamp before use: `limit = min(max(_safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 200), 1), 1000)`.

title: fred_series observations param is unclamped (negative/huge values reach fetch_series)
description: obs = _safe_int(request.args.get('observations'), 60) is passed unbounded to fred_data.fetch_series(series_id, observations=obs). A negative observations value will, depending on fetch_series' slicing, either error or silently invert the requested window, and a very large value forces an oversized FRED download. There is also no validation of series_id format, but the unclamped observations is the concrete defect: it produces wrong-length or empty series with no 400.
fix: Clamp: `obs = min(max(_safe_int(request.args.get('observations'), 60), 1), 5000)`.

title: congress_all double-truncates: senate is fetched capped at `limit` before merge, so combined cannot show the newest `limit` rows
description: get_senate_trades is called with limit, returning AT MOST `limit` senate rows. House rows are then appended and the merged list is sorted newest-first and sliced [:limit]. Because senate was already truncated to its own newest `limit` BEFORE the merge, if the true newest `limit` combined rows are predominantly senate, older senate rows that should appear (after interleaving with house) are unavailable — the merged top-`limit` is computed from an already-incomplete senate slice. senate_count/house_count are also reported pre-truncation, so they can exceed the number actually returned in trades, misleading the UI.
fix: Over-fetch senate before merging so the post-merge slice is correct, e.g. fetch senate with a larger bound: `senate = ds.get_senate_trades(symbol=symbol, limit=limit*2)` (or an explicit cap), keep the final `combined[:limit]`, and report `senate_count`/`house_count` as the counts actually included in `combined[:limit]`.

title: _social_composite Wikipedia buzz component can exceed/under its intended 0-100 band and is unbounded below before clamp only on one side
description: For Wikipedia the code computes `min(100.0, max(0.0, 50.0 + float(spike)))` treating `spike` as a percentage where +50% -> 100. But spike_pct_vs_baseline is a raw percent that in real data routinely exceeds +/-50% (a viral article can spike +300%). The mapping silently saturates at 100 for anything >= +50% and at 0 for <= -50%, so the Wikipedia buzz contribution is effectively binary at the extremes and drowns out StockTwits/HN nuance in the unweighted mean. float(spike) will also raise (caught as 500 upstream) if spike arrives as a numeric string from the cache. The blend is an unweighted mean (sum/len) so one saturated source dominates buzz.
fix: Coerce defensively and compress the spike instead of hard-saturating, e.g. `try: spv=float(spike)\nexcept (TypeError,ValueError): spv=None` and map with a gentler scale such as `50.0 + spv/2.0` clamped to [0,100], or weight components so Wikipedia cannot exceed a fixed share of buzz.

title: _social_composite spike_pct float() can raise on a non-numeric cached value, 500-ing the whole social panel
description: `round(float(spike), 1) if (_live(wk) and spike is not None) else None` calls float(spike) directly. spike comes from `(wk.get('stats') or {}).get('spike_pct_vs_baseline')`, a value that originates from an external Wikipedia module and may be cached as a string or unexpected type. If float() raises, the exception propagates out of alt_social_pulse (which has no try around _social_composite) and the entire /api/alt-data/social/<symbol> response 500s, defeating the route's deliberate per-source graceful degradation.
fix: Guard the conversion: compute spike once via a helper that returns None on failure, e.g. `def _f(x):\n  try: return float(x)\n  except (TypeError,ValueError): return None` and use the parsed value in both the buzz branch and the spike_pct output.

title: finviz_insiders forwards an arbitrary `option` string to finvizfinance with no allowlist
description: option = request.args.get('option', 'latest') is passed verbatim to finviz_data.insider_trades(option=option). finvizfinance maps option onto a fixed set of insider views; an unexpected value typically raises (KeyError/ValueError) inside the library, which is not wrapped in try/except here, so the route 500s with a stack instead of a clean 400 for bad input. Other routes in this file validate their enumerated params.
fix: Allowlist the option: `option = request.args.get('option', 'latest'); if option not in {'latest','latest buys','latest sales','top week','top owner trade'}: return jsonify({"error":"invalid option"}), 400` (use the set finviz_data actually supports).

title: research_factors_portfolio weights crypto/option holdings into a Fama-French equity factor model
description: The DB-fallback path builds holdings from db.get_portfolio() with NO asset_type filter: every row with shares*avg_cost > 0 is added (line 2052 area). Crypto and option positions (which have no Fama-French equity factor exposure and may not resolve in research_factors) are thus included in the portfolio factor regression, skewing the market-value weights and contaminating the exposure estimate with symbols the factor model cannot price. Sibling scan routes (synthetic_insider_scan, alt_data_scan) deliberately exclude asset_type 'crypto'; this route does not.
fix: Filter the fallback to equities/ETFs: in the loop add `if (h.get('asset_type') or 'stock') not in ('stock','etf'): continue` before computing mv, mirroring the crypto exclusion used by the scan routes.

title: intel_feed result-build dereferences f['ticker']/f['form_type']/... with [] instead of .get(), KeyError if a filing dict is partial
description: When AI is requested, the zip(uncached_filings, summarized) loop builds the response using hard subscripts f['ticker'], f['form_type'], f['filing_date'], f['description'], f['accession'], f['document_url']. The defensive comment notes that a work fn can raise and yield an empty AI slot (handled), but the filing dict `f` itself comes from upstream EDGAR parsing; if any one filing is missing a key (e.g. 'document_url' absent for an unusual form), the whole route raises KeyError and 500s, discarding all already-summarized filings. The non-AI branch (1633-1646) has the identical hard-subscript fragility.
fix: Use .get with safe defaults for the filing fields, e.g. `"ticker": f.get("ticker","")`, `"filing_url": f.get("document_url","")`, etc., in both the AI and non-AI append blocks so one malformed filing can't drop the entire feed.

title: congress_all / congress_senate symbol filter is not validated, so junk symbol param silently returns empty without 400
description: Both routes read `symbol = request.args.get('symbol')` and pass it to get_senate_trades(symbol=...) and use symbol.upper() for the house filter, with no _valid_ticker check. A malformed symbol (e.g. lowercase with punctuation) is uppercased and compared, silently yielding zero matches rather than a 400, and an unexpected non-ticker value is still embedded into the downstream comparison. Sibling per-symbol congress route congress_trades_symbol does validate; the combined/senate routes are inconsistent.
fix: When symbol is provided, validate it: `if symbol and not _valid_ticker(symbol): return jsonify({"error":"Invalid symbol"}), 400` near the top of both congress_senate and congress_all.

title: congress_all assumes member.get('trades') items and member fields are dicts/strings; mixed upstream shapes can break the row build
description: The house merge does `t.get(...)` on each trade and `member.get(...)` for name/filing_date/pdf_url. get_congress_summary is an external parser; if any trade entry is not a dict (e.g. a stray string from a malformed PDF parse), t.get raises AttributeError and the whole /api/congress/all response 500s, even though the try/except around this block only resets house_rows to [] for exceptions raised inside the try — which it is, so it degrades — BUT the senate portion already succeeded and would still be returned. The real issue: a single bad trade aborts ALL house rows rather than skipping just that row.
fix: Wrap the inner per-trade append in its own guard so one bad entry is skipped, e.g. `for t in member.get('trades', []) or []:\n  if not isinstance(t, dict): continue` before building the row.

title: _jarvis_act_refund pops the most-recent timestamp, which under concurrency belongs to a different request
description: _jarvis_act_refund() does _JARVIS_ACT_TIMES.pop() to give back a charged slot. The deque holds timestamps for ALL in-flight charged actions, not just this caller's. If request A charges (appends its timestamp) and then, before A reaches its refund branch, request B charges (appends B's timestamp), A's refund pops B's timestamp instead of A's. A's slot is never returned and B is wrongly refunded, corrupting the rolling-window budget accounting. Callers: aj_run_route's 409 refund (3573) and any future refunder. The lock makes pop atomic but does not make it pop the caller's own entry.
fix: Track the exact timestamps charged and remove those specific values. Have _jarvis_act_charge return the list of appended timestamps and _jarvis_act_refund accept that list, e.g.: in charge, build `stamps=[now]*n`, append them, and `return stamps`; in refund(stamps), under the lock do `for t in stamps: try: _JARVIS_ACT_TIMES.remove(t) except ValueError: pass`. Update aj_run_route to capture the return value and pass it back.

title: _mc_holdings_from_portfolio multiplies by h['shares'] which may be None or missing
description: Line 3199 computes `mv = cur * h['shares']`. Unlike `cur` (which falls back via h.get('avg_cost')), `h['shares']` is accessed with a hard subscript and is never None-guarded. A holding row with shares=None (or no 'shares' key) raises TypeError ('NoneType' * float) or KeyError, which is caught only by the outer route handler and turns the whole Monte Carlo portfolio endpoint into a 500 — even though every other position is valid. Portfolio rows can legitimately carry NULL shares (e.g. watch-only/option placeholders elsewhere in the app).
fix: Guard shares before use: replace lines 3199-3201 with `sh = h.get('shares')` then `if not sh or sh <= 0: continue` and `mv = cur * sh`. This skips the bad row instead of failing the whole request, matching the existing 'skip non-positive' philosophy.

title: _mc_holdings_from_portfolio uses h['symbol'] subscript that KeyErrors on a malformed row
description: Lines 3191 and 3202 access h['symbol'] via hard subscript. If db.get_portfolio() ever returns a row without a 'symbol' key (or a None symbol), prices.get(h['symbol']) / the -USD concatenation raises KeyError or TypeError, failing the entire montecarlo/portfolio endpoint with a 500. The known list documents a similar slot-0/None-symbol fragility elsewhere; this specific helper is not covered.
fix: At the top of the loop add `sym0 = h.get('symbol'); if not sym0: continue`, then use sym0 in place of h['symbol'] at lines 3191 and 3202.

title: research_montecarlo_route forwards unvalidated client holdings entries straight into the simulation engine
description: The POST handler checks only that `holdings` is a non-empty list (3214), then passes each element verbatim to _mc_mod.simulate_portfolio. Individual entries are never validated to be dicts with a numeric 'market_value' and a string 'symbol'. A payload like {"holdings":[1,2]} or [{"market_value":"abc"}] reaches the engine and surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of a 400, and a negative/NaN market_value silently skews the simulation. Contrast with the GET variant which builds clean rows from the DB.
fix: After 3214, normalize/validate: `clean=[]; for h in holdings: if isinstance(h,dict) and isinstance(h.get('symbol'),str) and h['symbol'].strip():` then coerce mv via float() in a try/except, require mv>0, append {'symbol':h['symbol'].strip().upper(),'market_value':mv}. If `not clean: return jsonify({'error':'holdings must be objects with symbol and positive market_value'}),400`. Pass `clean` onward.

title: prob_of_target failure handling only catches TypeError/ValueError, discarding the already-computed sim on any other engine error
description: The prob_of_target call (3234-3238) is wrapped in `except (TypeError, ValueError): pass`, intended so a bad target_nav doesn't break the main result. But prob_of_target runs a second full simulation and can raise other exceptions (RuntimeError, numpy LinAlgError, KeyError, etc.). Any such error escapes the narrow except, propagates to the outer `except Exception` at 3242, and returns a 500 — throwing away the successful `sim` the user actually requested, just because the optional target probability failed.
fix: Broaden the inner guard to `except Exception as _pt_err: log.warning('prob_of_target failed: %s', _pt_err)` so any failure of the optional add-on leaves the primary `sim` intact and still gets returned at 3241.

title: aj_approve_route burns a rate-limit slot on every non-executing outcome (404 / not-approvable / 409 / risk-block)
description: The route charges one rate-limit slot at 3598 before doing any work, but only the happy path actually submits an order. On proposal-not-found (3602, 404), not-approvable (3605, 400), already-being-approved (3611, 409), and risk-gate block (3620, 400) it returns WITHOUT refunding. A UI that polls/retries approvals, or a user clicking a stale/blocked proposal, rapidly exhausts the shared _JARVIS_ACT_MAX=10/60s budget that also gates aj_run and jarvis_act, locking the operator out of legitimate actions. aj_run_route already refunds its no-op (3573); this route does not.
fix: Refund the slot on each early non-execution exit, e.g. add `_jarvis_act_refund(1)` immediately before the returns at 3602, 3605, 3611, and 3620 (the risk-block branch). Leave the happy-path charge in place.

title: jarvis_act single-action path assumes execute_mutating returns a dict (no isinstance guard, unlike the batch path)
description: The batch branch validates `if not isinstance(r, dict): return ... 500` (3776-3777), but the single-action branch at 3795-3796 calls `r = jarvis_tools.execute_mutating(tool, args)` and immediately does `r.get('error')` with no type check and no surrounding try/except. If execute_mutating returns None or a non-dict (e.g. a tuple/string from a buggy or in-flight tool), `r.get` raises AttributeError that escapes to Flask as an unhandled 500 with a stack trace — also defeating the _err() leak protection used everywhere else in this file.
fix: Mirror the batch guard: after 3795 add `if not isinstance(r, dict): return jsonify({'error': 'tool returned invalid result'}), 500` before the 3796 return, and/or wrap the execute_mutating call in try/except returning _err(e).

title: synth_macrotranslate_portfolio labels cost basis (shares*avg_cost) as live market_value
description: When no holdings are supplied, the fallback (4530-4533) builds market_value as `shares * avg_cost` — i.e. cost basis, not current market value — and feeds it to macro_translate as portfolio_holdings 'market_value'. The macro impact attribution then weights positions by what was paid, not what they're worth now, materially skewing the per-position impact for any holding with a meaningful gain/loss. The MC helper at 3186 deliberately uses live prices for the same concept; this path does not.
fix: Reuse live pricing for the fallback: fetch `prices=_portfolio_live_prices(rows)` and compute `px=(prices.get(h['symbol']) or {}).get('price') or h.get('avg_cost')`; mv = `px * (h.get('shares') or 0)`. Fall back to avg_cost only when no live quote, matching _mc_holdings_from_portfolio.

title: synth_whatif_get accepts NaN/inf market_value because float() parses them
description: Line 4599 does `mv = float(request.args.get('market_value') or 0.0)`. Python's float() happily parses 'nan' and 'inf', and the only guard is `mv < 0` (4603) — NaN compares False to every relation, so `mv < 0` is False and a NaN passes. A NaN/inf market_value flows into synth_whatif.whatif and corrupts every downstream weight/concentration computation (NaN propagates), producing a nonsense or all-null what-if with a 200 status.
fix: After parsing, reject non-finite input: `import math` (module-level) and add `if not math.isfinite(mv): return jsonify({'error':'market_value must be a finite number'}),400` before the `mv < 0` check. Apply the same guard to the POST candidate path if it parses market_value.

title: aj_run_route does not refund the rate-limit slot when run_once raises
description: aj_run_route charges a slot at 3565 and only refunds on the specific 'already running' 409 (3573). If aj_operator.run_once raises (caught by the outer `except` at 3576 -> _err 500), the slot stays charged even though no cycle executed. Repeated transient failures of run_once (e.g. broker/import error) silently drain the shared 10/60s budget, throttling subsequent legitimate runs/approvals/acts.
fix: Wrap the run_once call so failures refund: e.g. `try: result = aj_operator.run_once(mode)` ... `except Exception as e: _jarvis_act_refund(1); return _err(e)`, keeping the existing 409-refund branch for the no-op case.

title: jarvis activity SSE generator spins a full snapshot every 2s for 10 min even with no client reading
description: generate() (3915-3952) loops every 2s calling jarvis.activity_snapshot() and json.dumps for up to 600s. The only termination is the 600s deadline or a GeneratorExit on client disconnect — but if the client TCP-disconnects without the WSGI server promptly detecting it (common with buffering proxies / X-Accel-Buffering already disabled), the generator keeps invoking activity_snapshot() (which may itself hit the DB/locks) up to 300 times after nobody is listening. There is no max-iteration / disconnect short-circuit beyond the implicit one; combined with the comment 'reloads/shutdowns are never blocked', a wedged snapshot call inside the loop can still pin a worker thread.
fix: Lower the 600s ceiling is risky (changes behavior); instead make snapshot failures and slow paths cheaper: cap consecutive snapshot exceptions and break after N (e.g. 5) failures, and shorten _time.sleep when sent_any is False to fail fast. Minimal surgical fix: add a consecutive-error counter in the except branch and `break` after a small threshold so a persistently failing snapshot stops re-running instead of looping for 10 minutes.

title: research_optimize compare path float()s arbitrary current_weights values without catching non-numeric input cleanly
description: Line 3326 builds `{k.upper(): float(v) for k, v in current_weights.items()}` inside a try that catches `Exception as ce` and logs+degrades (3330-3332) — good — BUT the dict-comprehension also calls k.upper(), so a current_weights key that is not a string (JSON allows only string keys, but a crafted dict via the engine path or a non-str-coercible value) and a float(v) on a list/dict raises TypeError. That is caught, so the user silently gets an empty compare with no indication the weights they sent were malformed, masking a client bug. More importantly result['weights'] (3327) is assumed present; if the optimizer returns a dict without 'weights' (non-error but unusual shape) it KeyErrors into the same swallow, hiding the contract violation.
fix: Validate inputs explicitly before the call: coerce keys via str(k).upper(), and use result.get('weights') with `if not isinstance(result.get('weights'), dict): cmp_out=default` so a missing-weights optimizer result is detected rather than swallowed as a generic compare failure.

title: _track_record_line double-converts an already-percentage hit_rate (no <=1 guard)
description: _track_record_line formats the agent's grounding line as '{:.0f}% directional'.format(hr * 100, n). It unconditionally multiplies hr by 100. _forecast_line (line 1729) for the SAME accountability source defensively does 'hr * 100 if hr <= 1 else hr', proving hit_rate can already arrive as a percentage (e.g. 58.0). When it does, this line fabricates '5800% directional', feeding a nonsense self-assessment straight into the agent's system prompt grounding. This is a different code path from the display lines already reported.
fix: Mirror the _forecast_line guard: compute hr_pct = hr * 100 if hr <= 1 else hr, then format '{:.0f}% directional ... '.format(hr_pct, n).

title: _forecast_line mixes denominators: hit_rate is directional but n falls back to total n
description: n = tr.get('n_directional') or tr.get('n'). hr is the DIRECTIONAL hit rate, but when n_directional is missing OR zero (falsy), n falls back to tr.get('n') — the total scored-call count, which includes non-directional calls. The line then states 'X% directional hit rate over <total> scored calls', overstating the sample backing the directional rate. A genuine n_directional of 0 also silently borrows the larger total.
fix: Pick the directional count explicitly and don't let 0 fall through: nd = tr.get('n_directional'); n = nd if nd is not None else tr.get('n'); and gate the line on nd (directional sample) when reporting a directional rate.

title: _idea_insights formats composite_score with :.0f without verifying it is numeric
description: top is filtered only on 'composite_score is not None', then '{:.0f}'.format(r['composite_score']) is applied. If the warmed-pool row carries a non-numeric composite_score (e.g. a string score or NaN), format raises ValueError/TypeError. _idea_insights itself has no try/except; it relies on the briefing's per-section guard, so the failure silently drops the entire ideas section. (Distinct function from the already-reported _answer_ideas.)
fix: Coerce/validate before formatting: build top from rows where _finite(r.get('composite_score')) is not None, and format _finite(r['composite_score']) so NaN/strings are excluded rather than raising.

title: day_pnl_pct denominator includes positions whose day change is unknown, skewing the percentage
description: total_value (line 1007) accumulates every position that has a price, but day_pnl (line 1011) only accumulates positions where q.get('change') is not None. prev_value = total_value - day_pnl (line 1031) and day_pnl_pct = day_pnl / prev_value (line 1037) therefore divide a partial-coverage dollar move by a denominator that includes capital with no measured change. When some holdings price but lack a 'change' field (common after a feed hiccup), the reported day P&L % is silently diluted/wrong while still being shown as authoritative.
fix: Track a parallel value base for only the positions that contributed to day_pnl (e.g. day_value += mv when chg is not None) and compute day_pnl_pct against that base, or expose day_pnl as known-but-partial when coverage < 100%.

title: _salvage_payload drops all evidence when the first cached tool result exceeds the digest budget
description: The loop breaks the FIRST time budget - len(chunk) < 0, before appending. If the first tool_cache entry's truncated chunk (~up to 600 chars + name) is larger than the remaining budget (4000 to start, so only possible after prior entries, but a single oversized name can still trip it), digest_parts can end up empty even though real tool data exists, forcing the weaker deterministic recap and discarding usable evidence on the failure path this function exists to handle.
fix: Append the (already length-capped) chunk before checking the budget, then break: digest_parts.append(chunk); budget -= len(chunk); if budget < 0: break — guaranteeing at least one evidence chunk survives.

title: Near-alert loop iterates all active alerts but quotes are fetched for only the first 25 symbols
description: syms is capped at 25 (line 1092) and only those symbols' quotes are fetched. The near-trigger loop, however, iterates over the full `active` list (line 1101). Any active alert whose symbol fell outside the 25-symbol cap gets quotes.get(...) == None and is silently skipped, so users with >25 distinct alerted symbols never receive near-alert cards for the overflow — a silent coverage gap rather than the intended 'cheap' truncation.
fix: Iterate only the alerts whose symbol is in the fetched set: for a in active: if a['symbol'] not in quotes_by_sym: continue — or build the loop from `syms` so the cap and the iteration agree.

title: Regime warn card emitted with empty detail when regime_note is missing
description: When regime is ELEVATED/STRESSED the card detail is regime.get('regime_note') or '' (line 1435). regime_note only gets populated when vix_level matched a band (line 1061); the regime label itself can be set while note is None only if the two ever diverge, but more importantly _card is created with detail='' producing a P1/P2 warn card that renders a title with a blank body. A blank-body urgent card reads like a rendering bug to the user.
fix: Fall back to a non-empty default: regime.get('regime_note') or 'Volatility regime is {} — expect wider swings.'.format(regime['regime']).

title: day_pnl_pct suppressed to None whenever prev_value is non-positive, hiding a real down day
description: day_pnl_pct is computed only when (day_pnl_known and prev_value > 0). prev_value = total_value - day_pnl. On an extreme down day where the measured day_pnl is so large that prev_value rounds to <= 0 (e.g. tiny book, or a data glitch), the percentage is silently dropped to None even though day_pnl itself is reported, so the headline/coach paths that key on day_pnl_pct (lines 1407-1408, 1283) lose the percentage and the drawdown-coach card never fires on exactly the worst days.
fix: Guard only against division by ~zero, not sign: compute when day_pnl_known and abs(prev_value) > 1e-6, or fall back to day_pnl/total_value when prev_value is degenerate, so an extreme day still yields a (large) percentage.

title: Warmer liveness uses max() over raw cycle timestamps that may be booleans
description: vals filters cycles.values() with isinstance(v, (int, float)), but bool is a subclass of int, so a cycle entry like {'quotes': True} passes the filter and max(vals) can return 1 (True) or be polluted by a 0/1 sentinel, yielding age = now - 1 (~1.7 billion seconds) and 'alive': False even when the warmer is healthy, or masking a real stall.
fix: Exclude booleans explicitly: vals = [v for v in cycles.values() if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool)].

title: _symbol_line 52-week range percentage can print negative or >100% with no clamp
description: (q['price'] - lo) / (hi - lo) * 100 is guarded for hi > lo but not for price outside [lo, hi]. When the live price has already exceeded the cached 52-week high (or dropped below the low) — routine intraday on a breakout — this prints e.g. '103% of 52-week range' or a negative percentage in the user-facing strip line, which reads as a math error.
fix: Clamp the displayed figure: pct = max(0.0, min(100.0, (q['price'] - lo) / (hi - lo) * 100)) before formatting (matching how a range fraction should read).

title: away_digest returns early on short gap but still leaves stale `since`/zeroed fields without recap suppression flag
description: When gap_min < _AWAY_MIN_GAP_MIN the function returns `out` with away_minutes set but count=0 and line=None — indistinguishable from 'a real absence with no new insights'. Callers (e.g. the briefing headline peek at line 1481, which only checks count) are fine, but any UI that distinguishes 'too soon to be away' from 'away but nothing happened' cannot, because both shapes are identical. More concretely, when mark_seen=True the watermark was already advanced (line 1537) BEFORE this early return, so a sub-30-min refresh permanently moves the watermark forward and can swallow insights logged in that window from the next genuine digest.
fix: Advance the watermark only after deciding the visit counts as an absence (move the set_setting call below the gap check), or skip mark_seen when gap_min < _AWAY_MIN_GAP_MIN so short refreshes don't burn unseen insights.

title: Briefing logs insights then peeks away_digest in the same call, inflating the away count with current-session cards
description: _run_briefing_uncached calls db.jarvis_log_insights(cards) (line 1455) and then away_digest(mark_seen=False) (line 1479). away_digest queries jarvis_insights WHERE created_at > last_seen. Because the cards just logged carry a created_at later than last_seen, the very cards produced by THIS briefing are counted as 'events logged while you were out', so the headline can claim e.g. '5 events logged while you were out' on the user's first refresh after returning, double-counting what they are looking at right now.
fix: Peek the away digest BEFORE jarvis_log_insights writes the new cards, or have away_digest exclude rows whose created_at >= the briefing's generation start so the current run's own cards aren't reported as missed.

title: Earnings 'days_until' wording assumes a non-negative integer; a past/None value mislabels
description: when = 'today' if days == 0 else ('tomorrow' if days == 1 else 'in {} days'.format(days)). days comes from e.get('days_until') and is only filtered for None or >7 (line 1128). A negative days_until (an earnings date that just passed but wasn't pruned upstream) passes the >7 check and renders 'in -1 days', and a non-int (float) renders 'in 3.0 days'. The card then claims a stale earnings event is imminent.
fix: Filter the lower bound and coerce to int: if days is None or days < 0 or days > 7: continue, and format with int(days).

title: Duplicate _GLOSSARY dict keys silently discard the earlier curated entries
description: The _GLOSSARY dict literal defines several keys twice: 'rsi' (lines 2905 and 2938), 'sharpe ratio' (2917 and 2947), and the drawdown pair where 'max drawdown' is a top-level key (2913) AND an alias of 'drawdown' (2951). In a Python dict literal the LAST occurrence wins, so the richer first 'rsi'/'sharpe ratio' definitions are dead code and never reachable. Worse for drawdown: _GLOSSARY has a 'max drawdown' canonical entry (2913) while 'drawdown' (2951) lists 'max drawdown' as an alias, so _GLOSSARY_INDEX maps the alias 'max drawdown' to canonical 'drawdown' (last writer in the alias loop), making the dedicated 'max drawdown' text unreachable too. Users get a different, shorter explanation than the curated one intended for that term.
fix: Deduplicate the dict: keep only one definition per term. For rsi/sharpe ratio, delete one of the two literal entries (keep the one with the desired text/view). For drawdown, remove 'max drawdown' from the aliases of the 'drawdown' entry (2951) so the dedicated 'max drawdown' canonical entry at 2913 remains reachable, or merge them into a single entry with both aliases. No behavior beyond the explanation text changes.

title: _answer_earnings indexes calendar entries by hard keys with no guard
description: When a symbol is supplied and earnings.get_earnings_calendar([symbol]) returns a non-empty list, the code does e["symbol"], e["earnings_date"], e["days_until"] via hard subscription (line 2564-2565). Unlike the soon-filter path it uses e.get('beat_rate') for the optional field but NOT for the required ones. If the upstream calendar dict is missing 'earnings_date' or 'days_until' (e.g. a partial/null record), this raises KeyError that propagates out of _answer_earnings uncaught, turning a benign 'no date' answer into a 500/crash for that query.
fix: Use .get with fallbacks: e.get('symbol', symbol), e.get('earnings_date') and skip/format gracefully when None, e.get('days_until'). Mirror the defensive pattern already used for beat_rate, e.g. guard `if e.get('earnings_date'):` before composing the answer and otherwise fall through to the 'No upcoming earnings date found' branch.

title: _answer_earnings 'soon' listing accesses e['symbol']/e['earnings_date'] by hard key
description: After building `soon` by filtering only on days_until, line 2579 formats each entry with e["symbol"] and e["earnings_date"] via hard subscription. An entry that passed the days_until filter but lacks 'symbol' or 'earnings_date' (heterogeneous upstream data) raises KeyError, crashing the whole portfolio-earnings answer with no try guard around this function.
fix: Replace with e.get('symbol','?') and e.get('earnings_date','—') in the join at line 2579, e.g. "{} on {}".format(e.get('symbol','?'), e.get('earnings_date') or 'TBD').

title: health_snapshot reports COUNT(*) of all insights under the key 'insights_14d'
description: The query `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM jarvis_insights` has NO time filter, yet the result is stored under out['insights_14d'] (line 1914), implying a 14-day window. As the insights table grows over the app's lifetime this number drifts far from the intended last-14-days metric, misleading the health/diagnostics UI (e.g. showing thousands when only a handful are recent).
fix: Add a WHERE clause bounding to 14 days, e.g. "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM jarvis_insights WHERE created_at >= datetime('now','-14 days')" (using the table's actual timestamp column), or rename the output key to 'insights_total' if a lifetime count is the real intent.

title: _answer_alerts iterates db.get_price_alerts() result without None/list guard
description: Lines 2615-2617 call db.get_price_alerts(include_triggered=True) and immediately list-comprehend over it (`[a for a in alerts ...]`). If the DB call returns None on error (or any non-iterable), this raises TypeError that escapes _answer_alerts uncaught — there is no try/except here, unlike many sibling answer functions. A transient DB hiccup turns 'how many alerts' into a hard failure of the ask path.
fix: Guard the result: `alerts = db.get_price_alerts(include_triggered=True) or []` and ideally wrap the call in try/except returning a graceful 'couldn't read alerts' answer. The `or []` alone prevents the None-iteration crash.

title: _answer_compare_quotes always navigates to s1 even when only s2 was the meaningful subject
description: The success path hard-codes action {"view":"research","symbol": s1} (line 2873). The comparison can conclude that s2 'has the better day' (line 2872), yet the navigation action still opens s1's research view. The action ignores which symbol the user's attention was just directed to, producing a mild but consistent UX mismatch (tail talks about s2, click opens s1).
fix: Pick the action symbol to match the highlighted name: `winner = s1 if (c1 is None or c2 is None or c1 >= c2) else s2` and use that in the action, or omit the symbol and just open the research view. Behavior of the comparison text is unchanged.

title: _answer_why share-of-move phrase drops legitimate negative-share contributors silently
description: _phrase only appends the '% of the move' clause when share_of_move_pct > 0 (line 2407). For a DOWN day, `main` is the detractors list and each detractor's day_pnl is negative while `total` is negative, so share_of_move_pct = day_pnl/total*100 is POSITIVE — fine. But on an UP day where `main`=contributors, if a contributor's share rounds to exactly 0.0 (tiny vs a large total) or the sign of total flips relative to an entry, the >0 test hides the share. More importantly the condition `> 0` excludes the exactly-100%-single-driver edge only when rounding yields 0; combined with the min(...,999) cap this can render 'Most of it: X (...)' with no percentage at all, reading as if attribution failed.
fix: Change the guard to `e.get('share_of_move_pct') is not None and abs(e['share_of_move_pct']) >= 1` and format with abs() so near-zero/negative artifacts are suppressed cleanly while genuine large shares always print: `s += " — {:.0f}% of the move".format(min(abs(e['share_of_move_pct']), 999))`.

title: _symbol_line indexes held['shares']/held['avg_cost'] by hard key inside its own scope
description: After locating a held position, lines 1759-1760 compute mv and cost using held["shares"] and held["avg_cost"] as hard subscripts. The surrounding try only wraps the lookup loop (1750-1756), not this arithmetic. A portfolio row missing 'avg_cost' (e.g. a manually inserted/legacy holding) raises KeyError here, which is NOT caught by _view_context_uncached for the symbol branch (it returns _symbol_line directly at line 1771 before the broad except? — actually the except at 1792 covers it, but the function still loses the whole symbol context line). Either way a single malformed holding suppresses the entire view-context tail.
fix: Use .get with safe defaults: `shares = held.get('shares') or 0; avg = held.get('avg_cost') or 0; mv = (q['price'] or 0)*shares; cost = avg*shares`, and only emit the 'You hold ...' tail when shares > 0.

title: _answer_exposure sorts/filters holdings on r['market_value'] and r['weight_pct'] by hard key
description: Line 2231 sorts pulse['holdings'] by -r["market_value"] and line 2233 filters on r["weight_pct"] >= threshold, both hard subscripts. If any holding dict lacks 'market_value' or 'weight_pct' (the known-defects list already notes weight_pct can be None/missing for unpriced rows), the sort key raises KeyError or the comparison `None >= number` raises TypeError, crashing the entire exposure answer. The sibling _answer_risk at 2758 correctly uses r.get('weight_pct', 0), so this path is inconsistent and unsafe.
fix: Use defensive accessors: sort with key=lambda r: -(r.get('market_value') or 0) and filter with `(r.get('weight_pct') or 0) >= _CONCENTRATION_PCT`. The tops formatting at 2232 already uses r['weight_pct'] hard — switch to r.get('weight_pct') or 0 there too.

title: _answer_biggest uses max() on r['market_value'] hard key and assumes non-empty holdings
description: Line 2246 calls max(pulse['holdings'], key=lambda r: r["market_value"]). Two problems: (1) hard subscript r['market_value'] raises KeyError for any holding missing that field; (2) if pulse is truthy but pulse['holdings'] is an empty list (e.g. all positions filtered out upstream while totals remain), max() raises ValueError ('max() arg is an empty sequence'). Both crash the answer with no guard.
fix: Guard emptiness and use .get: `holdings = pulse.get('holdings') or []` then `if not holdings: return {...no positions...}` and `top = max(holdings, key=lambda r: r.get('market_value') or 0)`.

title: _answer_crypto_share sums and sorts on r['market_value'] by hard key
description: Line 2797 computes mv = sum(r["market_value"] for r in crypto) and line 2800 sorts sorted(crypto, key=lambda r: -r["market_value"]) using hard subscripts. A crypto holding whose market_value wasn't populated (unpriced feed) raises KeyError, crashing the crypto-share answer even though pct already defensively uses r.get('weight_pct') or 0.
fix: Use r.get('market_value') or 0 in both the sum (2797) and the sort key (2800) to match the defensive weight_pct handling in the same function.

title: _answer_risk dereferences rows[0] (top) without checking holdings is non-empty
description: After `rows = sorted(pulse['holdings'], ...)`, line 2759 does `top = rows[0]` and later top['symbol'] (2765, 2778). pulse is only checked for truthiness (2754-2755); if pulse exists but holdings is an empty list, rows[0] raises IndexError and the entire risk answer crashes. Books can be in a transient state where pulse summary fields exist but the per-holding list is empty.
fix: After computing rows, add `if not rows: return {"answer": "No priced positions to assess risk on yet.", "action": {"view": "portfolio"}}` before accessing rows[0].

title: _forecast_line hit-rate normalization misfires for hit rates expressed as 0..1 that round-trip oddly
description: Line 1729 normalizes hr with `hr_pct = hr * 100 if hr <= 1 else hr`. A legitimate hit rate of exactly 1.0 (100% over a small sample) satisfies hr <= 1 and becomes 100 — correct — but a hit rate already stored as a whole percentage of 1 (i.e. 1%) would be wrongly multiplied to 100%. More realistically, the boundary at <= 1 means a track record of exactly 1.0 vs 1.x is ambiguous; combined with the duplicate-logic noted elsewhere this can display '100%' for a 1.0 fraction that actually represents 1 percent in some upstream encodings.
fix: Disambiguate using a tighter bound and the sample size: treat values strictly < 1.0 (or <= 1.0 with n implying a fraction) as fractions, e.g. `hr_pct = hr*100 if 0 <= hr <= 1.0 else hr` is current; safer is to standardize upstream so accountability_report always returns a fraction, then drop the branch entirely: `hr_pct = hr*100`.

title: attribution_window baseline filter recomputes _dt twice and can mis-order on ties
description: Line 2462-2463 builds `older = [s for s in snaps[:-1] if _dt(s) is not None and _dt(s) <= target]` then picks older[-1]. This assumes snaps is sorted ascending by date so older[-1] is the most recent baseline at/under target. If snaps is not guaranteed sorted (db.get_snapshots ordering is not enforced here), older[-1] is simply the last in list order, which may be an EARLIER date than another qualifying snapshot — selecting a worse baseline and producing a wrong delta/attribution window. It also calls strptime twice per element (minor perf).
fix: Sort first and select by date, not list position: `older = [s for s in snaps[:-1] if (_d:=_dt(s)) is not None and _d <= target]; older.sort(key=lambda s: _dt(s)); base = older[-1] if older else min(snaps[:-1], key=lambda s: _dt(s) or latest_dt)`. At minimum compute _dt once per element and explicitly pick the max-date qualifying snapshot.

title: Thanks ack rotation keyed on len(q) but q may differ from the matched message in case/whitespace
description: Line 3168 returns _THANKS_ACKS[len(q) % len(_THANKS_ACKS)] using the ORIGINAL q's length, while the match and remainder stripping operate on ql (lowercased) / stripped. For a one-word 'thanks' vs 'Thanks ' with trailing spaces the index differs, so the 'deterministic, stable' rotation promised in the comment is not stable across trivially different gratitude phrasings — the same logical message can yield different acks. (Distinct from the known issue about remainder already being stripped.)
fix: Key the rotation on a normalized stable length, e.g. len(stripped) or len(remainder is '' so use len(ql.strip())), to make the rotation depend only on the canonicalized message the matcher actually saw.

title: deep_dossier reports HIGH conviction on an all-neutral (mixed) dossier
description: consensus is computed as the largest stance bloc's share. When every adapter returns stance 'neutral' (no bulls, no bears), bulls=bears=0 so disagreement is False, and consensus = max(0,0,n)/n = 1.0. With n>=3 that hits the `consensus >= 0.8 and n >= 3` branch and sets conviction='high'. The headline then reads 'a mixed read with high conviction (3 of 3 signals aligned)', asserting strong conviction on a thesis where every engine actually declined to take a side. The intent (per the docstring) is to shrink conviction toward neutral when signals don't share a directional view, but an all-neutral set is the maximally non-directional case and gets the highest conviction label.
fix: Guard the high/moderate branches on a directional majority. Compute `directional = len(bulls) + len(bears)` and require it before granting conviction, e.g.: change line 4057 to `if disagreement or consensus < 0.6 or n < 2 or net == 0:` so a zero net (all-neutral or perfectly split) always yields conviction='low'. This leaves all current directional behavior unchanged.

title: _clarify_pending check reads _PENDING_CLARIFY without holding the lock
description: _PENDING_CLARIFY is mutated under _PENDING_CLARIFY_LOCK at the set site (4154-4161) and the pop site (4397-4398), but the read here at 4354 (`_PENDING_CLARIFY.get(conv_id)`) is performed WITHOUT acquiring the lock. Two requests on the same conversation can interleave: thread A reads 'no pending clarify' here and proceeds into the correction-rerouting path while thread B is concurrently writing/popping the same conv_id, leading to inconsistent decisions about whether the correction path should be skipped. While CPython's GIL keeps the dict itself from corrupting, the check-then-act across line 4354 and the later pop (4396-4398) is not atomic, which is exactly the kind of race the lock was added to prevent.
fix: Take the lock for the read: replace line 4353-4354 with `with _PENDING_CLARIFY_LOCK:\n    _clarify_pending = (conv_id is not None and _PENDING_CLARIFY.get(conv_id) is not None)`. This matches the locking discipline already used at the set and pop sites without changing behavior.

title: Clarify-resume pops the pending clarify before the TTL check, silently dropping a still-valid intent on failure
description: The pending clarify is popped from the dict at line 4398 unconditionally, and only AFTER that is the TTL freshness checked (4401) and the intent dispatched. If pend.get('intent') is something other than 'forecast' or 'agent', or if the dispatch raises (caught at 4425), the pending clarify has already been removed and is never restored. The user's bare-symbol reply then falls through to the generic quote/agent path, and a subsequent retry has no pending intent to resume — the original clarified intent is lost even though it was within TTL. Pop-before-validate also means a stale entry that fails the TTL check at 4401 falls through correctly, but a valid entry that simply doesn't match the two handled intents is consumed for nothing.
fix: Peek instead of popping until the intent is actually going to be resumed: read with `pend = _PENDING_CLARIFY.get(conv_id)` under the lock, check the TTL, and only `_PENDING_CLARIFY.pop(conv_id, None)` once you've confirmed pend.intent is a handled value and are about to dispatch it. On the exception path leave it in place so a retry can resume.

title: Clarify-resume passes lowercased ql to _agent_ask instead of the original query
description: When resuming a pending 'agent' clarify with a bare-symbol reply, the code calls `_agent_ask(ql, turns, ...)` where ql is the lowercased query (set at line 4188). Every other dispatch in this function passes the original-cased q to the agent/research paths. Handing the agent a lowercased reply (e.g. 'nvda' instead of 'NVDA') can defeat the agent's own symbol/ticker extraction and proper-noun handling, degrading the resumed answer for exactly the reply the clarify flow was designed to complete.
fix: Pass the original-cased reply: change `_agent_ask(ql, turns, progress=progress)` to `_agent_ask(q, turns, progress=progress)` at line 4409.

title: Trading-agent activity formatting prints 'None' when an order lacks a symbol or state
description: Recent-order formatting does `"{} {:g} {} ({})".format(str(o.get('side') or '').upper(), float(o.get('qty') or 0), o.get('symbol'), o.get('state'))`. While side and qty are defended with `or`, o.get('symbol') and o.get('state') are passed straight to str-format, so a missing/None symbol or state renders the literal text 'None' inside the user-facing sentence (e.g. 'Recent agent orders — BUY 10 None (None).'). The known-issues list flags side/qty handling but not the symbol/state None-stringification.
fix: Default both fields: `o.get('symbol') or '?'` and `o.get('state') or 'unknown'` inside the format call so a partial order record degrades to a placeholder rather than the word None.

title: Trading-agent profit_factor rendered raw, can print 'inf' or excessive precision
description: `parts.append("profit factor {}".format(pf))` formats profit_factor with default str() conversion. A profit factor computed as gross_profit/gross_loss where gross_loss is ~0 is commonly float('inf'), which renders as 'inf' in the user-facing sentence; a normal float renders with full repr precision (e.g. '2.3333333333333335'). Both are unpolished compared to the other metrics in the same sentence which use formatted specifiers.
fix: Format and guard: `parts.append('profit factor {:.2f}'.format(pf))` and, just before, skip/clamp non-finite values, e.g. `if pf is not None and math.isfinite(pf):` (math is already used elsewhere in the module) so 'inf' is omitted rather than printed.

title: Trading-agent status prints 'X/None trades used today' when max_trades_per_day is missing
description: Status formatting does `"{}/{} trades used today".format(s.get('trades_today'), s.get('max_trades_per_day'))`. The branch is gated only on `s.get('trades_today') is not None`; max_trades_per_day is not checked, so if the cap is absent/None the line renders 'used 3/None trades used today'. Misleading and unpolished in the default status answer.
fix: Guard the cap too, e.g. `cap = s.get('max_trades_per_day'); if cap is not None: parts.append('{}/{} trades used today'.format(s.get('trades_today'), cap)) else: parts.append('{} trades today'.format(s.get('trades_today')))`.

title: Top-contributor formatting uses hard dict keys, collapsing the whole performance read on a malformed entry
description: `tc[0]['symbol']` and `tc[0]['total_usd']` use bracket indexing on the first top_contributors entry. If that entry is missing either key (a shape the upstream tool could emit), a KeyError is raised, caught by the broad except at 3898, and the user gets the generic 'Couldn't read the trading agent just now (\'symbol\')' fallback instead of the performance summary that was otherwise fully computed (win rate, profit factor, net realized are all discarded).
fix: Use .get with defaults and skip the tail when incomplete: `c0 = tc[0]; sym = c0.get('symbol'); tot = c0.get('total_usd'); if sym is not None and tot is not None: tail = ' Top contributor: {} ({}).'.format(sym, _fmt_usd(tot))`.

title: Non-disagreement dossier headline can claim more aligned signals than actually share the lean
description: In the agreement branch the headline prints `max(len(bulls), len(bears), n - len(bulls) - len(bears))` as the count of 'signals aligned'. When the lean is constructive (net>0) but, say, there are 2 bulls and 3 neutrals (no bears), this max picks the neutral count (3) and prints '3 of 5 signals aligned' for a 'constructive' read — attributing the neutrals as agreement with the bullish lean. The aligned count should reflect the bloc that drives the stated lean, not whichever bloc happens to be largest.
